components.name: Accordion
components.description:
A stack of sections that expand and collapse. Each header is a heading that wraps a real
button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), so it appears in the page outline and works with
`Enter` and `Space`. Built on React Aria `DisclosureGroup`.

Use it to shorten a long page of related, optional content (FAQs, settings groups). Do not
hide content people need to finish their task.

props.name: items
props.description: The sections, in order.

props.name: multiple
props.description:
Allow several sections open at once. By default opening one section closes the others
(single expansion).

props.name: value
props.description: Values of the expanded items (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Values of the items expanded at first (uncontrolled).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the values of all expanded items after the user toggles one.

props.name: variant
props.description: `bordered` (default) draws a card around the sections; `plain` only draws dividers.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description:
Level of the heading that wraps each trigger, `3` by default. Use the level that follows
the heading above the accordion in the page outline.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every section.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the root element.

items.name: KeyboardSingle
items.description: Enter and Space toggle the focused header; opening one closes the others.

docs.summary:
A stack of sections that expand and collapse. Each header is a heading that wraps a real button. Built on React Aria `DisclosureGroup`, `Disclosure` and `DisclosurePanel`.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/Accordion.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-04`).
whenToUse: FAQs, grouped settings, long optional detail on a record.
To shorten a page whose sections people read one at a time.
whenNotToUse: For content people must see to finish the task.
For switching between views: use `Tabs`.
For a single show/hide of one block: a plain disclosure is enough.
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` moves between triggers; `Enter` and `Space` toggle. Optional arrow-key movement between headers (APG) is not added: each trigger is a tab stop.
examples:
<Accordion
  headingLevel={2}
  items={[
    { value: 'shipping', title: 'How long does shipping take?', content: 'Two to five days.' },
    { value: 'returns', title: 'Can I return an order?', meta: '30 days', content: '…' },
  ]}
/>

<Accordion multiple variant="plain" value={open} onChange={setOpen} items={items} />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- FAQs, grouped settings, long optional detail on a record.
- To shorten a page whose sections people read one at a time.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For content people must see to finish the task.
- For switching between views: use `Tabs`.
- For a single show/hide of one block: a plain disclosure is enough.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                     | Type                        | Default      | Notes                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`                  | `AccordionItem[]`           | required     | `{ value, title, meta?, content, isDisabled? }`.                        |
| `multiple`               | `boolean`                   | `false`      | Several sections open at once. Otherwise opening one closes the others. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string[]`                  | `[]`         | Expanded values, controlled / uncontrolled.                             |
| `onChange`               | `(value: string[]) => void` | none         | All expanded values after a toggle.                                     |
| `variant`                | `'bordered' \| 'plain'`     | `'bordered'` | `bordered`: card border and surface. `plain`: dividers only.            |
| `headingLevel`           | `2`-`6`                     | `3`          | Level of the heading around each trigger; follow the page outline.      |
| `isDisabled`             | `boolean`                   | `false`      | Disables every section.                                                 |

`ref` points to the root; `className` and other attributes pass through.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Each header is `h3` (configurable) containing a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `group` labelled by the button. Headings appear in the page outline and in screen reader heading lists.
- Keys: `Tab` moves between triggers; `Enter` and `Space` toggle. Optional arrow-key movement between headers (APG) is not added: each trigger is a tab stop.
- Collapsed panels are hidden (`hidden="until-found"`), so find-in-page can open them, and they take no space.
- The chevron rotates 180 degrees to show the state; the state itself is `aria-expanded`, not the icon. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the rotation is instant.
- The focus indicator is an inset accent outline because the group clips overflow. Forced colors use `Highlight`.
- Disabled items are not focusable.
- Meta text is read after the title; keep it short.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Titles are short phrases or questions in sentence case, and say what is inside.
- Do not put the only copy of important information in a collapsed panel.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The trigger is wrapped in a heading and linked to its panel (`aria-controls`, labelled panel); the handoff had a bare `button` and no panel relationship.
- `multiple` and controlled `value` / `onChange` replace the internal-only `defaultValue` array.
- `variant="plain"` replaces `bordered={false}`. The chevron is the shared `ChevronDownIcon` that rotates (down collapsed, up expanded), instead of a custom right-pointing SVG.
- Not included yet: height animation of the panel (the chevron animates; the panel appears instantly) and arrow-key movement between headers.

alternatives.name: Tabs
alternatives.reason: For switching between views: use `Tabs`.

components.name: ActionList
components.description:
A vertical list of records, each with a title, optional description, a mono meta value and a
"more actions" menu. Built on React Aria `GridList`: rows are reached with the arrow keys
(one tab stop for the list), `Enter` runs `onAction`, and `Tab` or the right arrow moves
from a row to its menu button.

props.name: items
props.description:
The rows, in the order given. The list never sorts: lists are alphabetical by default in
this design system, so sort with `sortByText` before passing them (tasks by urgency and
dated records newest first are the exceptions).

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the list root.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the list root element.

props.name: onAction
props.description:
Called when the user activates a row (click, or Enter on the focused row). Makes the whole
row a press target with hover and pointer cursor. The menu button does not trigger it.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Draws the border, surface and radius around the list. Turn off inside a `Card`. Default `true`.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content when `items` is empty. Default: an `EmptyState` with built-in text.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ moreActions: (title: string) => string; emptyTitle: string; emptyDescription: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the list. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the list (a visible heading).

keys.description: Accessible name of the row actions button. `title` is the text of the row ("More actions for Price list").
Title of the default empty state.

keys.default: Try another filter or search term.
keys.description: Description of the default empty state.

items.name: Default
items.description: Rows are listed in the order given; sort with `sortByText` for the alphabetical default.

items.name: Actionable
items.description: With `onAction` the whole row is a press target; the menu button does not trigger it.

items.name: KeyboardNavigation
items.description: The arrow keys, Home and End move between rows; the right arrow reaches the row menu.

items.name: RowMenu
items.description: Enter opens the row menu, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.

items.name: PortugueseBrazil
items.description: Row action button names, the empty state and numbers follow the provider locale.

docs.summary: A vertical list of records. Each row has an optional leading node, a title, an optional description, a mono meta value and an optional "more actions" menu. Built on React Aria `GridList`, so rows are reachable with the arrow keys and can run an action.
whenToUse: Short lists of things with a few actions each: files, saved filters, members, recent items.
One main line of text per record, with secondary detail.
whenNotToUse: Many comparable columns, sorting or selection: use `DataTable`.
Navigation between pages: use `NavItem` or `Tabs`.
Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.
keyboard: Keyboard: `Tab` enters the list on one row (one tab stop); Arrow Up/Down, Home and End move between rows; Arrow Right moves from the row to its menu button (Arrow Left back); `Enter` on a row runs `onAction`; the menu button follows the Menu contract (`Enter`/`Space`/`Arrow Down` opens, `Escape` closes and focus returns to the button).
examples:
<ActionList
  aria-label="Files"
  items={sortByText(files, (f) => f.name, locale).map((file) => ({
    id: file.id,
    title: file.name,
    description: `Updated by ${file.author}`,
    meta: formatBytes(file.size),
    actions: (
      <>
        <MenuItem onAction={() => download(file)}>Download file</MenuItem>
        <MenuSeparator />
        <MenuItem tone="danger" onAction={() => askToDelete(file)}>
          Delete file
        </MenuItem>
      </>
    ),
  }))}
  onAction={(item) => openFile(item.id)}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Short lists of things with a few actions each: files, saved filters, members, recent items.
- One main line of text per record, with secondary detail.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Many comparable columns, sorting or selection: use `DataTable`.
- Navigation between pages: use `NavItem` or `Tabs`.
- Choosing options in a form: use `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup` or `Select`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=grid]            named by aria-label / aria-labelledby
  div[role=row]           one tab stop for the whole list; arrow keys move between rows
    span  leading         optional (Avatar, Icon)
    span  title / description
    span  meta            mono, text-2
    MoreActionsMenu       IconButton "More actions for {title}" + Menu (optional)
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                | Default | Notes                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`      | `ActionListItem[]`  | -       | `id`, `title`, `textValue`, `description`, `meta`, `leading`, `actions`, `isDisabled` |
| `aria-label` | `string`            | -       | Required (or `aria-labelledby`)                                                       |
| `onAction`   | `(item) => void`    |         | Row click or Enter. Makes the row a press target                                      |
| `bordered`   | `boolean`           | `true`  | Border, surface and radius. Turn off inside a `Card`                                  |
| `emptyState` | `ReactNode`         |         | Default: compact `EmptyState` with built-in text                                      |
| `messages`   | `Partial<messages>` |         | `moreActions(title)`, `emptyTitle`, `emptyDescription`                                |

`actions` is a node: `MenuItem`, `MenuSection` and `MenuSeparator` elements from `Menu`. Put the handler on the item (`<MenuItem onAction={...}>`). Destructive items use `tone="danger"` and still ask for confirmation in a dialog.

The list renders `items` in the order given. Lists are alphabetical by default in this design system: pass them through `sortByText` first (exceptions: tasks by urgency, dated records newest first).

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `GridList` gives `role="grid"` with `row` and `gridcell` roles; rows are not a `list`/`listitem` pair because they are focusable and actionable.
- Keyboard: `Tab` enters the list on one row (one tab stop); Arrow Up/Down, Home and End move between rows; Arrow Right moves from the row to its menu button (Arrow Left back); `Enter` on a row runs `onAction`; the menu button follows the Menu contract (`Enter`/`Space`/`Arrow Down` opens, `Escape` closes and focus returns to the button).
- Every menu button has its own name ("More actions for Price list 2026") so a screen reader user can tell them apart.
- Row actions never rely on color; the meta value is text. Disabled rows are dimmed and skipped.
- Known quirk: React Aria moves focus to the row after an overlay inside a row closes. The component hands focus back to the button that was pressed.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Titles are the record name, not a sentence. Descriptions say who or when ("Updated by Ana").
- Menu items are verb + object ("Download file", "Delete file").

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<ActionList
  aria-label="Files"
  items={sortByText(files, (f) => f.name, locale).map((file) => ({
    id: file.id,
    title: file.name,
    description: `Updated by ${file.author}`,
    meta: formatBytes(file.size),
    actions: (
      <>
        <MenuItem onAction={() => download(file)}>Download file</MenuItem>
        <MenuSeparator />
        <MenuItem tone="danger" onAction={() => askToDelete(file)}>
          Delete file
        </MenuItem>
      </>
    ),
  }))}
  onAction={(item) => openFile(item.id)}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Real list semantics and keyboard support (`GridList`) instead of clickable `div`s; rows can be activated with `Enter`.
- The `···` button is the shared `MoreActionsMenu` (label from messages, names the row, `Menu` keyboard model) instead of a hand-made popover.
- `actions` is a `MenuItem` node (composition) instead of an array of `{ label, danger, separator }`; `onItemClick` is `onAction`; `title`/`description`/`meta` accept nodes.
- Text uses `text-2` for descriptions (contrast stays above 4.5:1 on hover and raised surfaces).
- Empty state and disabled rows added. Drag handle is not included.

components.name: AgentCard
components.description:
A card for one agent: icon, name, status, description and a footer with the last activity
and the number of items waiting for approval.

The whole card is clickable through the "stretched link" pattern: the agent name inside the
heading is the only link (or button), and a pseudo-element extends its hit area over the
card. The accessible name is just the agent name; status, description and footer are the
description. There is no nested interactive element and no `role="button"` on a `div`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the agent. It is the accessible name of the card's single link or button.

props.name: area
props.description: Short caption under the name (the area the agent works in).

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon of the agent: any icon of the curated set (for example `SearchIcon`) or another Lucide icon. Decorative.

props.name: description
props.description: One or two sentences about what the agent does. Part of the accessible description.

props.name: status
props.description:
Lifecycle of the agent. `testing`, `active` and `paused` are available. `soon` is not
interactive: dashed border, no link, no pending count. Default `active`.

props.name: pending
props.description: Number of items waiting for approval. Shown (accent number plus text) only when above zero and the agent is available.

props.name: lastActivity
props.description: Text about the last activity ("Last reply sent at 08:40"). Shown in the footer.

props.name: href
props.description: Destination of the card. Renders a real link (router-aware through `DSProvider`).

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Called when the card is activated. Without `href` it renders a real button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the agent name (`h1` to `h6`). Default `3`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ statusTesting: string; statusActive: string; statusPaused: string; statusSoon: string; notConfigured: string; pending: (n: number) => string; }>
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

keys.description: Status badge text.
Footer text of a card that is not available yet and has no last-activity text.
Text after the (separately styled) pending number: "4 to approve".

docs.summary:
A card that represents one AI agent: icon, name, status, description and a footer with the last activity and the number of items waiting for approval. The whole card opens the agent. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/agents/AgentCard` (TODO `CMP-AGT-01`).
whenToUse: A grid of agents (or automations) on an overview page, each leading to its own screen.
To make "what needs me" visible: the accent number is the only call for attention on the card.
whenNotToUse: A generic clickable card of any other content: build it with `Card` and the same stretched-link technique.
Several actions per card: this card has exactly one (open). Put other actions on the agent's own screen.
keyboard: One tab stop per available card; `Enter` activates a link or button, `Space` also a button.
examples:
<AgentCard
  name="Marketplace agent"
  area="Marketplace"
  icon={ShoppingBag}
  status="active"
  pending={4}
  description="Answers buyer questions and reviews. You approve before it sends."
  lastActivity="Last reply sent at 08:40"
  href="/agents/marketplace"
/>
<AgentCard name="Chat agent" status="soon" description="Will draft orders from the conversation." />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A grid of agents (or automations) on an overview page, each leading to its own screen.
- To make "what needs me" visible: the accent number is the only call for attention on the card.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A generic clickable card of any other content: build it with `Card` and the same stretched-link technique.
- Several actions per card: this card has exactly one (open). Put other actions on the agent's own screen.

sections.heading: Pattern decision: stretched link
sections.content:
The card needs to be fully clickable, show a status badge and still have a clean accessible name. Three options were weighed:

1. Wrap the card in a link or button: the accessible name becomes the concatenation of every text inside (name, caption, status, description, footer), and block content inside a `<button>` is invalid HTML.
2. `div role="button"` (the handoff): no native semantics, and a badge nested in a button.
3. **Stretched link (chosen)**: the agent name, inside the heading, is the only real link or button. A `::after` pseudo-element on it covers the card, so a click anywhere activates it. The accessible name is just the agent name; the status, description and footer are the accessible description (`aria-describedby`). No nested interactive elements.

The focus ring is drawn around the whole card (`:has()` on the focused link), hover brightens the card border.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (card, data-status)
  header
    icon box (decorative)
    h{headingLevel} > a | button   <- the only interactive element, stretched over the card
    area caption
    Badge (status)
  p description
  footer
    last activity text
    pending: accent number + "to approve"
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                                          | Default    | Notes                                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`         | `string`                                      | required   | Accessible name of the link or button.                                                     |
| `area`         | `string`                                      |            | Caption under the name.                                                                    |
| `icon`         | `IconComponent`                               |            | Any Lucide icon (curated set or passed in). Decorative.                                    |
| `description`  | `ReactNode`                                   |            | One or two sentences.                                                                      |
| `status`       | `'testing' \| 'active' \| 'paused' \| 'soon'` | `'active'` | Text from messages. `soon` is not interactive (dashed).                                    |
| `pending`      | `number`                                      | `0`        | Shown only above zero and when available.                                                  |
| `lastActivity` | `ReactNode`                                   |            | Footer text. `soon` without it shows "Not set up yet".                                     |
| `href`         | `string`                                      |            | Renders a real `<a>`; router-aware through `DSProvider`.                                   |
| `onOpen`       | `() => void`                                  |            | Press handler. Without `href` the element is a `<button>`.                                 |
| `headingLevel` | `1`-`6`                                       | `3`        | Level of the name heading.                                                                 |
| `messages`     | partial catalog                               |            | `statusTesting`, `statusActive`, `statusPaused`, `statusSoon`, `notConfigured`, `pending`. |

Place the cards in a `ul` when they form a list; the grid is yours (for example `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(320px, 1fr))`, 16 px gap).

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- One tab stop per available card; `Enter` activates a link or button, `Space` also a button.
- The status is text in a `Badge` (color and dot only reinforce it) and is part of the description, so it is read after the name.
- A `soon` card has no link or button and no tab stop; the heading and the "Coming soon" badge say why.
- Count: "4 to approve" is real text in reading order (the number is just styled), pluralized and number-formatted through messages and `Intl`.
- Contrast: the caption and last-activity text use `--ds-text-3` on the surface (passes 4.5:1 there; do not move the card onto a raised surface). Forced colors: the ring becomes a `Highlight` outline.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Name: the agent's job in two or three words. Description: what it does and that you approve, in one or two sentences.
- Last activity in the past tense with a time: "Last reply sent at 08:40". Do not add decorative metrics.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<AgentCard
  name="Marketplace agent"
  area="Marketplace"
  icon={ShoppingBag}
  status="active"
  pending={4}
  description="Answers buyer questions and reviews. You approve before it sends."
  lastActivity="Last reply sent at 08:40"
  href="/agents/marketplace"
/>
<AgentCard name="Chat agent" status="soon" description="Will draft orders from the conversation." />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A real link or button (stretched link) instead of `div role="button"` with a nested badge.
- `soon` is not interactive and not focusable.
- Icon is a Lucide component drawn by `Icon` (the handoff fetched an SVG from a CDN at runtime).
- Status labels, "Not set up yet" and "to approve" come from messages (pluralized, localized); the number uses `Intl`.
- Sizes and spacing are `--ds-agent-card-*` tokens; no `style` prop; no JS hover state.

alternatives.reason: A generic clickable card of any other content: build it with `Card` and the same stretched-link technique.

components.name: Alert
components.description:
An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, an action and a dismiss button.
The icon is decorative and a visually hidden prefix names the tone for screen readers.

props.name: tone
props.description: Kind of message: `info` (neutral, default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading of the alert, in one line: what happened. Plain text, not a document heading.

props.name: children
props.description: The detail: why it happened and what to do.

props.name: action
props.description: A single action next to the text, usually a link or a small `Button` ("Update card").

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The alert is removed by the parent.

props.name: urgent
props.description:
The message interrupts the user's task and must be announced immediately (`role="alert"`,
assertive). Use it only for failures the user must know about right now.

props.name: announce
props.description:
Whether the alert is a live region (`role="status"`, polite). Default `true`, because most
alerts appear after something the user did. Set `false` for a static notice that is part
of the page content from the start: it then has no role and is read in page order.
Ignored when `urgent`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Name of the dismiss button.
Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of alert; color and icon alone cannot.

items.name: Urgent
items.description: Urgent alerts use `role="alert"` and interrupt screen readers. Reserve them for failures that need attention now.

items.name: StaticNotice
items.description: A static notice that is part of the page from the start has no live region role.

items.name: Dismissible
items.description: Tab to the dismiss button, press Enter.

docs.summary: An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, one action and an optional dismiss button.
whenToUse: Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.
whenNotToUse: Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
A field error: use the field's error message.
A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
examples:
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
- Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
- A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=status | alert | none]  (tinted surface, 1px tinted border, radius lg)
  Icon (decorative)  info | success | warning (triangle) | danger
  content
    VisuallyHidden   "Information" | "Success" | "Warning" | "Error"
    title            optional, 14/22, weight 500
    children         13/18, text-2
  actions            action slot · dismiss IconButton
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                                           | Default  | Notes                                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tone`      | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | `info` is neutral; the others tint border and background                       |
| `title`     | `ReactNode`                                    |          | What happened, one line                                                        |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                    |          | Why, and what to do                                                            |
| `action`    | `ReactNode`                                    |          | One link or small `Button`                                                     |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void`                                   |          | Shows the dismiss button; the parent removes the alert                         |
| `urgent`    | `boolean`                                      | `false`  | `role="alert"` (assertive). Only for failures that need attention now          |
| `announce`  | `boolean`                                      | `true`   | `false` removes the live region role for static notices. Ignored when `urgent` |
| `messages`  | `{ dismiss, info, success, warning, danger }`  |          | Per-instance overrides                                                         |

The vocabulary uses `info` instead of `neutral` for the plain tone, as in the handoff. Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility: role decisions
sections.content:
- **Default `role="status"` (polite).** Most alerts appear after something the user did (submit, import). A status region is announced politely, without stealing focus or interrupting speech. The handoff used `role="alert"` for every `danger` alert, which interrupts for things that are not urgent; urgency is now an explicit `urgent` prop, not a function of the tone.
- **`urgent` gives `role="alert"` (assertive).** Use it for a failure the user must know right now (lost connection, session expired). Avoid more than one at a time.
- **`announce={false}` gives no role.** A notice that is part of the page when it loads (a permanent banner, a form-level note) does not need a live region; screen readers read it in page order. A live region that never changes is noise, and many `status` regions on one page are worse.
- Live regions announce **changes**: for the announcement to work, render the Alert when the event happens and keep the region mounted; do not render it hidden and unhide it.
- **The tone is not only color and icon.** The icon is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden prefix ("Error", "Warning", "Success", "Information", from messages) names the kind of alert for screen readers.
- The **dismiss button** is an `IconButton` named "Dismiss alert" (messages), reachable by Tab and operated with Enter or Space. After dismissing, the parent should move focus somewhere sensible if the alert held it.
- Text contrast on the tinted backgrounds is at least 4.5:1 (checked in the browser test with the real computed colors). The 6% and 30% tints are component tokens (`--ds-alert-*`).
- Forced colors: the browser repaints border and icon with system colors; the icon and the hidden tone prefix still name the tone.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: what happened, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Payment declined").
- Text: why and what to do ("The card ending in 4242 was declined. Use another card.").
- The action is a verb plus object ("Update card"), not "Click here".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Icons are bundled Lucide icons, `aria-hidden`, instead of the text glyphs "i", "check" and "!" that screen readers read aloud. Warning and danger have different icons.
- `role` is `status` by default, `alert` only when `urgent`, none with `announce={false}`.
- Dismiss option, visually hidden tone prefix, and `messages` (English and pt-BR).
- The 6% tint and 30% border are tokens instead of inline `color-mix`; the handoff `--radius` (undefined) is `--ds-radius-lg`.
- No `style` prop.

and two actions, send and discard.

docs.summary:
A reply waiting for approval: the original message, an editable draft written by an agent, an optional warning and two actions, send and discard. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/agents/ApprovalCard` (TODO `CMP-AGT-02`).
whenToUse: An approval queue: replies, messages or changes an agent prepared that go to a customer or touch money.
Any "review the draft, edit it, send or discard it" step with many items on one screen.
whenNotToUse: A single decision with a consequence you cannot take back: use a `Dialog` with a confirmation.
Free chat with an agent: use `ChatPanel`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- An approval queue: replies, messages or changes an agent prepared that go to a customer or touch money.
- Any "review the draft, edit it, send or discard it" step with many items on one screen.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A single decision with a consequence you cannot take back: use a `Dialog` with a confirmation.
- Free chat with an agent: use `ChatPanel`.

sections.heading: Principles
sections.content:
**Approve before sending.** Anything an agent writes to a customer goes through this card first. The draft is editable ("You can edit before sending"). Reviews of 1 to 3 stars always carry a `flag`.

**Undo, don't confirm.** Send and discard act immediately. Do not open a confirmation dialog; show a toast with **Undo** (see the recipe below). A confirmation for every card would train people to click through it.

**Secondary buttons, on purpose.** A screen has many cards and only one primary action (AGENTS.md section 5). Send is `secondary`, Discard is `ghost`. The button text is verb plus object ("Send reply", "Discard reply"), not a bare "Send".

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
article (named by the heading)
  header
    h{headingLevel}    Badge (Question | Review) + author in mono   <- the accessible name
    Rating             reviews only
    item               optional Swatch dot + item name
    time               when
  body
    message            original text, visually hidden label "Customer message:"
    Textarea           label "Agent reply", aside "You can edit before sending"
    flag               optional warning (icon + text), the card's description
    actions            Discard (ghost)                 Send (secondary)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                       | Type                                    | Default      | Notes                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`                                     | `'question' \| 'review'`                | `'question'` | Badge text from messages.                                                                   |
| `author`                                   | `string`                                |              | Mono, part of the accessible name.                                                          |
| `rating`                                   | `number`                                |              | Reviews only; halves allowed.                                                               |
| `itemName` / `itemColor`                   | `string`                                |              | Item reference; the color is a decorative `Swatch` (hex).                                   |
| `when` / `whenDateTime`                    | `ReactNode` / `string`                  |              | Display text and ISO date for `<time>`.                                                     |
| `message`                                  | `ReactNode`                             | required     | The original message.                                                                       |
| `draft` / `defaultDraft` / `onDraftChange` | `string` / `string` / `(draft) => void` |              | Controlled or uncontrolled draft.                                                           |
| `flag`                                     | `ReactNode`                             |              | Warning text. Linked with `aria-describedby`.                                               |
| `onSend` / `onDiscard`                     | `() => void`                            |              | Run the action now and offer Undo.                                                          |
| `headingLevel`                             | `1`-`6`                                 | `3`          |                                                                                             |
| `messages`                                 | partial catalog                         |              | `kindQuestion`, `kindReview`, `messageLabel`, `draftLabel`, `draftHint`, `send`, `discard`. |

sections.heading: Undo recipe
Accessibility
sections.content:
- `article` named by its heading through `aria-labelledby` ("Review buyer_sp"); with several cards, screen reader users can jump by heading or article.
- The two buttons are described by the heading (`aria-describedby`), so "Send reply, Review buyer_sp" is spoken without making every button name unique.
- The kind is a text badge, the rating is an image with a text alternative, the flag is text with a decorative icon: nothing relies on color alone. The flag uses `--ds-warning` on the surface (4.5:1 or better).
- Tab order follows reading order: draft, Discard, Send. The draft is a real labelled `Textarea` (its hint is the field description).
- The original message is announced after a hidden "Customer message:" label.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- The draft is a customer-facing reply: short, factual, no promises about delivery time or discounts, no emoji (AGENTS.md section 5). That is the agent's job; the card only makes it visible and editable.
- `flag` explains the risk and what to do: "2-star review: read it carefully before sending."

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The `section` has an accessible name (`article` named by a real heading).
- Strings (kind, labels, buttons) come from messages; the Portuguese originals are the `pt-BR` catalog. Buttons say "Send reply" / "Discard reply".
- The item dot uses `Swatch`; spacing uses `--ds-approval-card-*` tokens; the textarea is the design system `Textarea`.
- The flag is linked as the card's description and has an icon, not only a colored dot.
- Documented: Send and Discard are secondary/ghost, and undo is a toast.

components.name: AppShell
components.description:
The application layout: a sidebar, and a main column with a top bar above a scrollable
content region. The sidebar and the content scroll independently; the page itself does not.

Landmarks: the sidebar (`aside`, from `Sidebar`), the top bar (`header`), one `main`
(`id="main"`), and the optional detail `aside`. A skip link to `main` comes first.

Responsive contract (TOK-010): the shell measures its own width (a container query, so it
also works inside a frame). From `--ds-breakpoint-md` (768px) up the sidebar sits in the flow.
Below it the sidebar leaves the flow and opens as an off-canvas panel over the content,
controlled by `isNavOpen` and `AppShellNavToggle`; while it is open the rest of the page is
inert, `Escape` and the scrim close it, and focus returns to the toggle. The shell works from
320px. It fills its parent: give the parent a height, or it takes the viewport height.

props.name: sidebar
props.description: The app sidebar: a `Sidebar` element. Below the md breakpoint it becomes an off-canvas panel.

props.name: topBar
props.description:
The page header: a `TopBar` element. Put an `AppShellNavToggle` in its `children` so narrow
screens can open the sidebar.

props.name: children
props.description: The page content. It is rendered inside the one `main` landmark.

props.name: detail
props.description:
Optional detail pane at the inline end, `--ds-app-shell-detail-w` (360px) wide, for the
record selected in the main content. It is an `aside` landmark with its own scroll. Below
the md breakpoint it moves under the main content.

props.name: detailLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the detail aside. Default "Details" from the message catalog.

props.name: mainId
props.description: `id` of the `main` element, and the target of the skip link. Default `main`.

props.name: padded
props.description: Pads the main content with `--ds-app-shell-main-padding`. Turn it off when the content brings its own padding (a `Container` has a gutter). Default `true`.

props.name: skipLink
props.description: Renders the skip link as the first focusable element. Default `true`; turn it off only if the app has its own.

props.name: isNavOpen
props.description: Controlled state of the off-canvas sidebar (narrow screens only). Pair with `onNavOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultNavOpen
props.description: Initial state of the off-canvas sidebar when uncontrolled. Default `false`.

props.name: onNavOpenChange
props.description: Called when the off-canvas sidebar opens or closes (toggle, `Escape`, scrim, close button).

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ navToggle: string; navClose: string; detail: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Text of the button that opens the navigation panel on narrow screens.
Text of the button that closes the navigation panel on narrow screens.
Accessible name of the detail aside landmark.

items.description: Sidebar on the left, top bar and scrolling content on the right. The sidebar and the content scroll apart.

items.name: WithDetail
items.description: The detail aside (360px) holds the record selected in the content.

items.name: WithoutSidebar
items.description: Without a sidebar the shell is a header and content.

items.name: Unpadded
items.description: Content without padding, for a table or a page that brings its own container.

whenToUse: The frame of every screen of an app: `Sidebar` + `TopBar` + content (+ optional detail pane).
whenNotToUse: A marketing page or a single-column document: use `Container` and let the page scroll.
Inside another AppShell.

<AppShell
  sidebar={<Sidebar workspace={workspace} sections={sections} value={route} onChange={go} />}
  topBar={
    <TopBar title="Orders" actions={<Button variant="primary">New order</Button>}>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - The frame of every screen of an app: `Sidebar` + `TopBar` + content (+ optional detail pane).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A marketing page or a single-column document: use `Container` and let the page scroll.
- Inside another AppShell.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root  (container, fills the parent, no page scroll)
  SkipLink                       first focusable element
  div.nav                        wraps the Sidebar (aside); off-canvas below md
  div.scrim                      only when the panel is open
  div.column
    TopBar                       header
    div.body
      main#main                  scrolls on its own
      aside "Details"            optional, 360px, scrolls on its own
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                             | Type                              | Default   | Notes                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sidebar`                                        | `ReactNode`                       |           | A `Sidebar`                                                         |
| `topBar`                                         | `ReactNode`                       |           | A `TopBar`; put `<AppShellNavToggle />` in its `children`           |
| `children`                                       | `ReactNode`                       |           | The page, inside the one `main`                                     |
| `detail`, `detailLabel`                          | `ReactNode`, `string`             | "Details" | Optional aside at the inline end (`--ds-app-shell-detail-w`, 360px) |
| `mainId`                                         | `string`                          | `'main'`  | `id` of `main` and the skip link target                             |
| `padded`                                         | `boolean`                         | `true`    | Pads `main` (24px); turn off for content with its own padding       |
| `skipLink`                                       | `boolean`                         | `true`    |                                                                     |
| `isNavOpen`, `defaultNavOpen`, `onNavOpenChange` |                                   | `false`   | Off-canvas sidebar state (below md)                                 |
| `messages`                                       | `{ navToggle, navClose, detail }` |           | Per-instance overrides                                              |

The shell is `100dvh` tall (capped by its parent's height): give the parent a height to embed it.

sections.heading: Responsive decision (TOK-010)
sections.content:
**The DS guarantees every component works from 320px wide, and AppShell collapses its sidebar into an off-canvas panel below `--ds-breakpoint-md` (768px).**

Why built in rather than left to apps: a sidebar hidden by an app without a way back strands keyboard and touch users, and every product would build the same panel. It is kept simple: it reuses the same `Sidebar` element (no second copy, no lost state) and CSS does the layout.

- The shell measures **its own width** with a container query, so it behaves the same in a frame, a preview or a test. The 768px in the CSS is `--ds-breakpoint-md`; CSS cannot read variables inside a query, so `AppShell.test.tsx` asserts the two agree at 767/768px.
- From md up the sidebar sits in the flow. Below, it leaves the flow; `AppShellNavToggle` (visible only below md) opens it as a panel over a scrim.
- While open: focus moves into the panel, the rest of the page is `inert`, `Escape`, the scrim or the "Close menu" button close it, and focus returns to the toggle. It is not a `Dialog`: it keeps the sidebar's own landmarks.
- The detail pane moves **under** the main content (half the height at most, own scroll) below md.
- Breakpoint tokens: `--ds-breakpoint-sm|md|lg|xl` (480 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 px); content: `--ds-content-max`, `--ds-content-gutter`; `--ds-container-sm|md|lg`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Landmarks: `aside` (Sidebar, "Sidebar"), `header` (TopBar), **one** `main`, optional `aside` ("Details"). Each `nav` in the sidebar is named by its caption.
- The skip link is the first stop and moves focus to `main`.
- `main` and the detail aside scroll independently. While they overflow they become keyboard stops (`tabindex="0"`) so the arrow keys scroll them; with nothing to scroll there is no extra tab stop.
- The closed panel is `visibility: hidden` and `inert`, so it is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
- The panel slide respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; the layout mirrors in RTL.
- `AppShellNavToggle` reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. It is an `IconButton` (menu icon) named "Menu" (`pt-BR` "Menu"; pass a string child to rename it); the close button is an `IconButton` (x icon) named "Close menu" / "Fechar menu", which sits on the scrim beside the panel and never wraps.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- One `h1` per page: `TopBar` renders it from `title`.
- One primary action per screen, at the end of the top bar.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The handoff assumed a 1180px minimum width and a fixed 240px sidebar. The shell now works from 320px, and the sidebar width stays a token.
- The skip link, the single `main` and the independent scrolling were left to each screen; the shell provides them.
