components.name: Avatar
components.description:
A circular photo or initials of a person, in grays (never a color per person). The `name`
drives the initials and the accessible name; a photo that fails to load falls back to the
initials.

props.name: name
props.description:
The person's full name. Drives the initials and the accessible name (`alt` of the photo).
Optional: still used to compute the initials.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Hides the avatar from assistive technology (`alt=""`). Use it when the name is shown next to it.

props.name: src
props.description: URL of the photo. If it fails to load, the initials are shown instead.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 24px, `md` 28px (default), `lg` 40px.

props.name: ring
props.description: Draws a 2px ring in the surface color, to separate overlapping avatars. Default `false`.

docs.summary: A circular photo or the initials of a person, in grays. There is no color per person.
whenToUse: Identify who owns, created or is assigned to something.
Next to a name in a list, a comment or a menu.
whenNotToUse: For a company logo or a product thumbnail: use an image.
For a status: use `Badge`.
examples: Ada Lovelace

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Identify who owns, created or is assigned to something.
- Next to a name in a list, a comment or a menu.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a company logo or a product thumbnail: use an image.
- For a status: use `Badge`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span.root (circle, role="img" + aria-label when it initials)
  img | span[aria-hidden] initials
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                   | Default | Notes                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`               | -       | Required unless `decorative`. Drives the initials and the accessible name              |
| `src`        | `string`               |         | Photo URL. A load error falls back to the initials                                     |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`  | 24, 28 and 40 px (`--ds-avatar-size-*`)                                                |
| `ring`       | `boolean`              | `false` | 2px surface-colored ring, to separate overlapping avatars                              |
| `decorative` | `boolean`              | `false` | Hides the avatar from assistive technology (`alt=""`). Use it next to the visible name |

The type makes `name` required when the avatar is not decorative. Other `span` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Initials
sections.content: `getInitials(name, locale)` (also exported) takes the first letter of the first and of the last word: "Ana Maria da Silva" is `AS`; a single word gives one letter. It uses `Intl.Segmenter` (combined characters stay whole) and `toLocaleUpperCase` with the `DSProvider` locale (`i` becomes `İ` in Turkish). The gray shade is derived from the name, so one person always looks the same.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content: - With initials the root is `role="img"` named by `name`; the letters are `aria-hidden` so they are not read twice. - With a photo the `` has `alt={name}`. A decorative avatar has `alt=""` and no role. - The handoff set `alt` to the initials ("AL"), which is meaningless to a screen reader; the full name is used now. - If the image cannot be loaded the initials appear and the accessible name stays the same. - Avatars are not interactive. Put one inside a button or link that has its own name and mark it `decorative`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Pass the full display name, not the initials.
- Never pass an email or an id as `name`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: ```tsx Ada Lovelace ``` Stacked avatars: wrap them in a flex container with `role="group"` and an `aria-label`, give each `ring`, and overlap with a negative inline margin. A dedicated `AvatarGroup` is not part of this version.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `name` replaces `initials`; initials are computed and locale-aware.
- `alt` is the person's name, or empty when `decorative`.
- Image error fallback.
- `size` is `sm | md | lg` (tokens) instead of a number; `tone` and `ring` color props are gone (shade is derived from the name, ring is a boolean).
- No `style` prop.

alternatives.name: Badge
alternatives.reason: For a status: use `Badge`.

components.name: Badge
components.description:
A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the
dot only reinforce it.

props.name: children
props.description: The status text. Required: color and the dot never carry the meaning alone.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Meaning of the badge: `accent` open or in progress, `success` done, `warning` pending,
`danger` failed, `neutral` everything else (default).

props.name: dot
props.description: Shows the small decorative dot before the text. It is hidden from assistive technology. Default `true`.

docs.summary: A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the dot only reinforce it.
whenToUse: Show the state of a record in a list, a table row or a card header: Draft, In progress, Shipped, Failed.
Keep the text short (one to three words, sentence case).
whenNotToUse: For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.
examples:
<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
<Badge dot={false}>Draft</Badge>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Show the state of a record in a list, a table row or a card header: Draft, In progress, Shipped, Failed.
- Keep the text short (one to three words, sentence case).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
- For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
- For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
[ dot ] Text
```

- `dot` (optional, decorative, `aria-hidden`).
- `text`: required, the status.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                                                          | Default     | Notes                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`      | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | `accent` open or in progress, `success` done, `warning` pending, `danger` failed |
| `dot`       | `boolean`                                                     | `true`      | Decorative dot before the text                                                   |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                   | required    | The status text                                                                  |
| `className` | `string`                                                      |             | Merged with the component class                                                  |

Other `span` attributes and `ref` are passed to the root element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A Badge is plain text in a `span`: there is no role and no keyboard behavior.
- The dot is `aria-hidden`; the tone is never the only carrier of meaning, because the text names the status (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Text on every soft tint keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast (checked in the browser test by compositing the real computed colors).
- In forced-colors mode the Badge gets a border and the dot takes the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Sentence case, no punctuation, no emoji: "In progress", not "IN PROGRESS!".
- Name the state, not the action: "Shipped", not "Ship".
- If the status can be unknown, say so with text ("Unknown"), do not omit the Badge.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
<Badge dot={false}>Draft</Badge>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Tones use only the semantic tokens (`--ds-*-soft`). The handoff built the danger tint with a different `color-mix` (14%) than the token (10%); the token is now the single source.
- Height, dot size and padding are component tokens (`--ds-badge-*`).
- The dot is explicitly decorative; `children` is required.
- No `style` prop.

alternatives.name: Tag
alternatives.reason: For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.

alternatives.name: Alert
alternatives.reason: For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.reason: For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

components.name: Banner
components.description:
A persistent, full-width message for a whole page or section: maintenance, a limited account,
an offline mode. It stays until the condition ends or the user dismisses it.
The icon is decorative and a visually hidden prefix names the tone for screen readers.

props.name: tone
props.description: Kind of message: `info` (neutral, default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading in one line: what is going on. Plain text, not a document heading.

props.name: children
props.description: The detail: why, and what to do. Keep it to one or two sentences.

props.name: action
props.description: A single action next to the text, usually a link or a small `Button` ("Update card").

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The banner is removed by the parent.

props.name: urgent
props.description:
The banner appears while the user is working and interrupts the task, so it must be announced
immediately (`role="alert"`, assertive). Only for a failure the user must know about right
now. A banner that is on the page from the start never needs it.

props.name: announce
props.description:
Whether the banner is a live region (`role="status"`, polite). Default `false`, because a
banner is usually part of the page when it loads and a live region that never changes is
noise. Set `true` when the banner is added to the page after load (a lost connection that
is restored, a session that is about to expire). Ignored when `urgent`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Name of the dismiss button.
Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of banner; color and icon alone cannot.

items.name: Urgent
items.description: Urgent banners use `role="alert"` and interrupt screen readers. Use them only when they appear while the user is working.

items.name: Announced
items.description: A banner added after the page loaded is a polite live region.

items.name: Dismissible
items.description: Tab to the dismiss button, press Enter.

docs.summary: A persistent, full-width message for a whole page or section: maintenance, a limited account, an offline mode. It has a tone, an icon, an optional title, one action and an optional dismiss button.
whenToUse: A condition that affects the whole page or area and lasts until it is resolved or dismissed: scheduled maintenance, a trial ending, a read-only mode.
Place it at the top of the page or section it applies to, above the content.
whenNotToUse: Feedback about something that just happened and goes away by itself ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
A message about one piece of content, inside it (a form, a card): use `Alert`.
A field error: use the field's error message.
A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
The status of a record: use `Badge`.
examples:
<Banner title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Banner>

<Banner
  tone="warning"
  title="Trial ends in 3 days"
  action={<Button size="sm">Choose plan</Button>}
  onDismiss={() => setHidden(true)}
>
  Choose a plan to keep your data.
</Banner>

<Banner tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost">
  Changes are not being saved.
</Banner>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A condition that affects the whole page or area and lasts until it is resolved or dismissed: scheduled maintenance, a trial ending, a read-only mode.
- Place it at the top of the page or section it applies to, above the content.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Feedback about something that just happened and goes away by itself ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
- A message about one piece of content, inside it (a form, a card): use `Alert`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- The status of a record: use `Badge`.

### Banner, Alert and Toast

|             | Banner                                             | Alert                                   | Toast                                |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Scope       | Page or section                                    | Inline, next to the content it explains | The app, in a corner                 |
| Lifetime    | Persistent, until resolved or dismissed            | Persistent while relevant               | Transient, auto-dismisses (pausable) |
| Shape       | Full width, flat, top and bottom border only       | Rounded card                            | Elevated overlay                     |
| Live region | None by default (it is on the page from the start) | Polite status by default                | Always announced                     |

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=alert | status | none]  (tinted surface, 1px tinted top and bottom border, full width)
  Icon (decorative)  info | success | warning (triangle) | danger
  content
    VisuallyHidden   "Information" | "Success" | "Warning" | "Error"
    title            optional, 14/22, weight 500
    children         text-2, on the same line as the title when it fits
  actions            action slot · dismiss IconButton
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                                           | Default  | Notes                                                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`      | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | `info` is neutral; the others tint border and background              |
| `title`     | `ReactNode`                                    |          | What is going on, one line                                            |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                    |          | Why, and what to do                                                   |
| `action`    | `ReactNode`                                    |          | One link or small `Button`                                            |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void`                                   |          | Shows the dismiss button; the parent removes the banner               |
| `urgent`    | `boolean`                                      | `false`  | `role="alert"` (assertive). Only when it appears while the user works |
| `announce`  | `boolean`                                      | `false`  | `role="status"` (polite), for a banner added after the page loaded    |
| `messages`  | `{ dismiss, info, success, warning, danger }`  |          | Per-instance overrides                                                |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility: role decisions
sections.content:
- **No role by default.** A banner is normally part of the page when it loads; screen readers read it in page order. A live region that never changes is noise.
- **`announce` gives `role="status"` (polite).** Use it when the banner is inserted after load (connection restored, session about to expire). Render the banner when the event happens and keep it mounted; do not render it hidden and unhide it.
- **`urgent` gives `role="alert"` (assertive).** Use it only for a `danger` or `warning` banner that appears dynamically and needs attention now (connection lost, session expired). A `danger` or `warning` banner that is on the page from the start must not be `urgent`: the tone does not imply urgency.
- **The tone is not only color and icon.** The icon is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden prefix ("Error", "Warning", "Success", "Information", from messages) names the kind of banner.
- The **dismiss button** is an `IconButton` named "Dismiss banner" (messages), reachable by Tab and operated with Enter or Space. After dismissing, move focus somewhere sensible if the banner held it.
- Text contrast on the tinted backgrounds is at least 4.5:1 (checked in the browser test with the real computed colors). The tints are component tokens (`--ds-banner-*`).
- Reflow: the text and the actions wrap; at 320 px the action moves below the text.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: what is going on, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Trial ends in 3 days").
- Text: why and what to do, one or two sentences.
- The action is a verb plus object ("Choose plan"), not "Click here".
- Do not stack more than one banner per page area.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Banner title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Banner>

<Banner
  tone="warning"
  title="Trial ends in 3 days"
  action={<Button size="sm">Choose plan</Button>}
  onDismiss={() => setHidden(true)}
>
  Choose a plan to keep your data.
</Banner>

<Banner tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost">
  Changes are not being saved.
</Banner>
```

alternatives.name: Alert
alternatives.reason: A message about one piece of content, inside it (a form, a card): use `Alert`.

alternatives.name: Dialog
alternatives.reason: A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.

alternatives.name: Badge
alternatives.reason: The status of a record: use `Badge`.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description:
The path to the current page as an ordered list of links inside a `nav` landmark. The
separators are decorative (`aria-hidden`), so a screen reader hears a list of N items. Long
labels are truncated with an ellipsis (the current page keeps the most room); collapsing the
middle of a long trail into a menu is not supported yet.

props.name: items
props.description:
The trail from the root to the current page. The last item is the current page: it gets
`aria-current="page"` and is not a link.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Accessible name of the breadcrumb navigation landmark.

items.name: KeyboardNavigation
items.description: Tab visits each ancestor link in order; the current page is plain text.

docs.summary:
The path from the root to the current page, as an ordered list of links inside a `nav` landmark. Built on React Aria `Breadcrumbs` and `Breadcrumb`.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/Breadcrumb.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-03`).
whenToUse: Deep hierarchies (Orders > Northwind Traders > ORD-1048) where people need to go up a level.
Inside the `TopBar` instead of a title.
whenNotToUse: For the steps of a process: use a stepper (`StatusSteps`).
For the main navigation: use `Sidebar` and `NavItem`.
For a flat app with two levels: a page title and a "Back" link are enough.
examples:
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: 'Orders', href: '/orders' },
    { label: 'Northwind Traders', href: '/customers/northwind' },
    { label: 'ORD-1048' },
  ]}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Deep hierarchies (Orders > Northwind Traders > ORD-1048) where people need to go up a level.
- Inside the `TopBar` instead of a title.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For the steps of a process: use a stepper (`StatusSteps`).
- For the main navigation: use `Sidebar` and `NavItem`.
- For a flat app with two levels: a page title and a "Back" link are enough.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                                 | Notes                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`      | `{ label: string; href?: string }[]` | Root first. The last item is the current page: plain text, `href` ignored. |
| `aria-label` | `string`                             | Overrides the landmark name ("Breadcrumb" from the catalog).               |
| `messages`   | `{ label?: string }`                 | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                  |

`ref` points to the `<nav>`; `className` and other `nav` attributes pass through. Links go through the router set on `DSProvider`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `nav` named "Breadcrumb" containing an `ol`: a screen reader announces a list and its length.
- The current page is `aria-current="page"` and is not a link.
- Separators are decorative icons with `aria-hidden`, so they are never read. They mirror in right-to-left locales.
- Tab visits each ancestor link in order. Link text is `--ds-text-2` and turns ink with an underline on hover.
- Truncation: ancestors shrink first (three times faster than the current page) and show an ellipsis; labels are not wrapped. Give the full text to users some other way when it matters (the page title).
- Collapsing the middle of a long trail into a menu ("...") is not supported yet; it needs the `Menu` component (P3).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are the page titles, short, in sentence case. The last label matches the page `h1`.
- Do not include "Home" unless it is a real destination people use.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: 'Orders', href: '/orders' },
    { label: 'Northwind Traders', href: '/customers/northwind' },
    { label: 'ORD-1048' },
  ]}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ordered list inside a named `nav` (the handoff was a flex of loose links and `/` spans).
- Separators are icons, hidden from assistive technology; the current page uses `aria-current` and is not a link.
- Real routed links (`href` through `DSProvider`) instead of `href="#"` plus `onClick`. Hover color is CSS.
- The landmark name comes from the message catalog (English and pt-BR).

alternatives.name: StatusSteps
alternatives.reason: For the steps of a process: use a stepper (`StatusSteps`).

alternatives.name: Sidebar
alternatives.reason: For the main navigation: use `Sidebar` and `NavItem`.

alternatives.name: NavItem
alternatives.reason: For the main navigation: use `Sidebar` and `NavItem`.

components.name: Button
components.description:
An action button built on React Aria's `Button`.

Use one `primary` button per screen. While `isPending` the button keeps its width, shows a
spinner, stays focusable, sets `aria-disabled` and ignores presses, so it can be explained
by a tooltip and focus is never lost.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual style.
- `primary`: the single main action of the screen (light ink on dark). One per screen.
- `secondary`: default for other actions.
- `ghost`: tertiary, low emphasis actions.
- `danger`: destructive action that is not yet confirmed.
- `danger-solid`: the confirm button of a destructive dialog.

props.name: size
props.description: Height token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the width of the container.

props.name: leading
props.description: Node before the label, usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative; the label names the button.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Node after the label, for example a `Kbd` shortcut hint.

props.name: children
props.description: Label: a short verb plus object in sentence case ("Create order").

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<button>` element.

items.name: Primary
items.description: Use one `primary` button per screen, at the top right of the view.

items.name: DangerSolid
items.description: The confirm button of a destructive dialog.

items.name: Pending
items.description: The button keeps its width and stays focusable while pending; presses are ignored.

items.name: LongText
items.description: Long labels wrap instead of overflowing their container.

items.name: Rtl
items.description: Right-to-left layout: icons and labels swap sides through logical properties.

items.name: KeyboardActivation
items.description: Keyboard: Tab focuses, Enter and Space press.

items.name: Focused
items.description: Focus state shown through a play function.

docs.summary:
The control for an action. Built on React Aria's `Button`, styled with tokens and `data-*` state attributes.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/Button` (CMP-FRM-01).
whenToUse: To run an action in place: "Create order", "Mark as shipped".
`danger` for a destructive action that opens a confirmation, `danger-solid` for the confirm button inside that dialog (initial focus stays on Cancel).
`ghost` for low-emphasis actions such as "View all" in a card header.
whenNotToUse: To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
For a two-state toggle: use a toggle component.
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press (RAC). One tab stop.

sections.heading: One primary per screen
sections.content: Use **one `primary` button per screen**, at the top right of the view, ideally with a keyboard shortcut. Primary is "ink for action": light on dark, never the accent color. Every other action is `secondary` or `ghost`. A second primary button means the screen has two main jobs: split the screen or demote one action.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- To run an action in place: "Create order", "Mark as shipped".
- `danger` for a destructive action that opens a confirmation, `danger-solid` for the confirm button inside that dialog (initial focus stays on Cancel).
- `ghost` for low-emphasis actions such as "View all" in a card header.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
- For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
- For a two-state toggle: use a toggle component.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: `[leading] label [trailing]` inside one native `<button>`. When pending, the content keeps its box (invisible) and a `Spinner` is centered on top, so the width never changes.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                                                                | Default       | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`    | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger' \| 'danger-solid'` | `'secondary'` | See above.                                                                                |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                              | `'md'`        | 32, 40, 48 px (`--ds-control-h-*`). Taller if the label wraps.                            |
| `fullWidth`  | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Fills the container.                                                                      |
| `leading`    | `ReactNode`                                                         | none          | Usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative.                                                 |
| `trailing`   | `ReactNode`                                                         | none          | For example a shortcut hint in mono.                                                      |
| `isPending`  | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Busy: spinner, `aria-disabled`, presses and form submission ignored, stays focusable.     |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Native `disabled`: not focusable, 35% opacity.                                            |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`                                           | none          | React Aria press event (mouse, touch, keyboard, screen reader). Prefer it over `onClick`. |
| `type`       | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'`                                   | `'button'`    | Stays `button` so a button never submits a form by accident.                              |
| `className`  | `string`                                                            | none          | Merged with the component class.                                                          |

Other React Aria `Button` props (`form*`, `autoFocus`, `aria-*`, `onHoverStart`, ...) and `ref` pass through. `style` and render-prop children are not accepted.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A real `<button>`; the name is its visible label.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press (RAC). One tab stop.
- Focus: accent border plus a 3px ring through `data-focus-visible`, a transparent outline that forced-colors mode repaints as `Highlight`. Mouse clicks do not show the ring.
- Pending: the button stays in the tab order (focus is not lost while waiting) with `aria-disabled="true"` (React Aria does not set `aria-busy`). React Aria announces the busy state when the focused button becomes pending and again when it finishes. The spinner is named "Loading" (pt-BR "Carregando", from the `Spinner` messages) and sits inside the button so it is part of the button's content.
- Disabled: removed from the tab order. Explain _why_ in nearby text rather than relying on a disabled button alone.
- Targets: at least 32px high, above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8.
- Contrast: label colors meet 4.5:1 on their backgrounds in every variant; disabled controls are exempt.
- Reduced motion: the only transition is a 150ms background color change, which the global reduced-motion rule neutralizes. The pending spinner turns into a static ring.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Verb plus object, sentence case: "Create order", "Retry charge". Never a bare "OK" or "Send".
- Destructive buttons name the action: "Delete order".
- No exclamation marks, no emoji, no decorative ellipsis. Use "..." only when the action opens something that needs more input ("Move to...").

sections.heading: States
sections.content: Hover (one surface step lighter; primary dims with `--ds-button-hover-brightness`), focus-visible, disabled, pending. Hover, focus and pending are CSS (`data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-pending`), never React state. There is no press animation.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: ```tsx ```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Hover is CSS, not JS state.
- `isPending` replaces the "disabled plus spinner in leading" recipe: width-stable, focusable, announced, and it ignores presses.
- Sizes are 32 / 40 / 48 px. The handoff `Button.prompt.md` said 28 / 32 / 40; the code and the tokens win.
- `onPress` (React Aria) is the primary event; `disabled` is now `isDisabled`.
- `style` was removed; the primary hover brightness (0.88) and the danger-solid one (0.9) are component tokens.
- Wrapping instead of `white-space: nowrap`, so long labels never overflow.

alternatives.name: Link
alternatives.reason: To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.

alternatives.name: IconButton
alternatives.reason: For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.

components.name: Calendar
components.description:
A month calendar (React Aria `Calendar`, an ARIA grid). The value is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string.
Months, weekday names and the first day of the week follow the `DSProvider` locale.

Keys: arrows move by day and week, `PageUp` / `PageDown` by month, `Shift+PageUp` /
`Shift+PageDown` by year, `Home` / `End` to the start / end of the week, `Enter` / `Space`
select. Each day button is named with its full date ("Wednesday, October 28, 2026"); today is
ringed and named "Today".

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Earlier days are disabled.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Later days are disabled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the whole calendar: days cannot be focused or selected.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: The calendar can be navigated and focused but the value cannot change.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Moves focus into the grid on mount.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `previousMonth`, `nextMonth`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Accessible name of the calendar grid. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is given.
Accessible name of the calendar grid.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Id of the element that names the calendar. Required unless `aria-label` is given.
Id of the element that names the calendar.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` for none. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initially selected date when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the picked date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

keys.description: Footer button that picks today's date.
Footer button that empties the field.
Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.

items.name: Open
items.description: The calendar open under the field, for the visual review (TEST-020).

items.name: PickDate
items.description: Pointer path: open the calendar, click a day, the popover closes and the field shows the date. TEST-012.

docs.summary: `DatePicker` is a date field (typed segments) with a calendar popover and "Today" / "Clear" buttons. `Calendar` is the standalone month grid. Built on React Aria `DatePicker`, `DateInput`, `DateSegment`, `Calendar`, `CalendarGrid`, `CalendarCell`, `Popover`. Task: CMP-INP-02.
whenToUse: A single calendar date: delivery, due date, birthday.
`Calendar` alone for inline planners and for composing your own picker.
whenNotToUse: A date range: not supported yet (range picker is P2).
A time of day or a timestamp: the value has no time and no time zone.
Dates years away from now: typing the segments is faster than the grid.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A single calendar date: delivery, due date, birthday.
- `Calendar` alone for inline planners and for composing your own picker.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A date range: not supported yet (range picker is P2).
- A time of day or a timestamp: the value has no time and no time zone.
- Dates years away from now: typing the segments is faster than the grid.

sections.heading: Value contract
sections.content: `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `min` and `max` are **ISO strings `YYYY-MM-DD`** (the `ISODate` type of `src/utils/date`), never `Date`. Conversion to React Aria's `CalendarDate` happens inside the component (`@internationalized/date`, see below), so the day cannot shift with the viewer's time zone. Invalid strings are treated as "no date". `onChange` receives a string only once every segment is filled, or `null` from the Clear button; an incomplete date is not reported. The form receives the ISO string under `name`.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                           | One is required.                                                                                                                |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`                                                                | ISO string or `null`.                                                                                                           |
| `min`, `max`                                                                                         | ISO strings. Outside days are disabled in the grid; typed dates outside are invalid. "Today" is disabled when today is outside. |
| `description`, `errorMessage`, `size`, `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | As in `Select`.                                                                                                                 |
| `messages`                                                                                           | `today`, `clear`, `openCalendar`, `previousMonth`, `nextMonth`, `requiredMark`.                                                 |

`Calendar` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange(iso)`, `min`, `max`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `autoFocus`, `messages`, and requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

sections.heading: Locale
sections.content: Segment order and separators, placeholders (`dd/mm/aaaa`), month names, weekday letters and the first day of the week come from the `DSProvider` locale through React Aria; there are no hard-coded names. Only the button texts are in the message catalog (`Calendar` key for the month buttons, `DatePicker` for the rest).

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key (calendar grid)               | Behavior                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrows                            | Previous / next day, previous / next week                     |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`             | Previous / next month                                         |
| `Shift+PageUp` / `Shift+PageDown` | Previous / next year                                          |
| `Home` / `End`                    | First / last day of the **month** (React Aria; APG says week) |
| `Enter` / `Space`                 | Select the focused day                                        |
| `Escape`                          | Close the popover, focus returns to the button                |

In the field: digits fill the segment and move to the next; arrows change a segment's value; `Backspace` clears a segment; `Tab` moves between segments. Each day is named with its full date ("Wednesday, October 28, 2026", "Today, ..."), so the grid is usable without sight. Today has a ring (`--ds-text-3`), the selected day an accent fill with `--ds-text-inverse`; disabled days are dimmed and `aria-disabled`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label with the date's role ("Delivery date"). Errors say how to fix: "Choose a date after today."

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<DatePicker
  label="Delivery date"
  name="delivery"
  min="2026-10-30"
  value={date}
  onChange={setDate}
/>
```

sections.heading: Dependency note
sections.content: The component imports `@internationalized/date`, which React Aria already depends on. It is not a direct dependency of this package yet, so under pnpm's strict layout it must be added to `package.json` (`pnpm add @internationalized/date@^3.12.4`, already in the lockfile as a transitive dependency).

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Typed segments with locale-aware placeholders instead of a button showing a `toLocaleDateString` string; calendar is an ARIA grid with full keyboard navigation (the handoff used plain buttons).
- Month and weekday names come from `Intl` through the locale, not hard-coded Portuguese arrays; the week start follows the locale.
- Day buttons have full-date names; `min` / `max` are enforced for typing too; today is a ring, the footer buttons ("Today", "Clear") come from messages.
- `Date` objects and `T12:00:00` tricks are gone; the value is an ISO string end to end.

components.name: Card
components.description:
A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region
(`section` named by its heading).

props.name: title
props.description:
Title shown as an uppercase mono caption. It is a real heading (see `headingLevel`) and
names the card region through `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls placed at the end of the header, next to the title (buttons, a menu).

props.name: variant
props.description:
`default` is a flat surface with a border. `raised` uses the raised surface, a stronger
border and the overlay shadow: use it only for a card that floats above the page (a
pinned panel, a detail popover shell), never for cards that sit in the normal flow.

props.name: padding
props.description: `md` applies the card padding token; `none` removes it (for full-bleed content such as a table). Default `md`.

items.name: PaperReceipt
items.description:
The paper scope (`data-theme="paper"`): the only light surface, for receipt and PDF previews.
Success, warning and danger use their darker paper twins (TOK-012), so badges, alerts and
tinted buttons keep 4.5:1 on the paper.

docs.summary: A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region.
whenToUse: Group a set of related fields, numbers or a list under one caption.
Put page sections side by side in a grid.
whenNotToUse: To wrap a whole page: use the page layout.
For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.
Do not nest a Card inside a Card; use a divider instead.
examples:
<Card title="Storage" actions={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>}>
  <Progress value={62} label="Used" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" />
</Card>

<Card title="Details" headingLevel={3}>…</Card>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Group a set of related fields, numbers or a list under one caption.
- Put page sections side by side in a grid.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To wrap a whole page: use the page layout.
- For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.
- Do not nest a Card inside a Card; use a divider instead.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
section (surface + 1px line, radius lg, padding)
  header (optional)
    h{headingLevel}  mono caption, uppercase by CSS
    actions          optional controls
  children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                         | Default     | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                  |             | Rendered as a heading styled as a mono caption                           |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2`         | Pick the level that fits the page outline                                |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                  |             | End of the header                                                        |
| `variant`      | `'default' \| 'raised'`      | `'default'` | `raised` only for a card that floats above the page                      |
| `padding`      | `'md' \| 'none'`             | `'md'`      | `none` for full-bleed content such as a table (the header keeps padding) |

Other `section` attributes (including `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`) and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Elevation
sections.content: Borders carry hierarchy, shadows are for overlays (AGENTS.md section 5). A `raised` card gets the raised surface, a stronger border **and** `--ds-shadow-overlay`, so use it only when the card really floats (a pinned side panel, the shell of a custom popover). A card in the normal flow stays `default`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The root is a `section`. With a `title`, the heading id is wired to `aria-labelledby`, so screen readers expose a named `region` landmark. Without a title or a label it is a plain generic container (no landmark), which is correct for decorative grouping.
- Give a title-less card an `aria-label` when it should be a landmark.
- The heading level is yours to choose: keep levels sequential (a Card inside a page with an `h1` usually uses `2`; inside another section use `3`).
- The caption uses `--ds-text-2` (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`, which drops below 4.5:1 on the raised surface).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Captions are sentence case in the source ("Storage"); uppercase is applied by CSS only.
- Keep captions to one to three words.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Card title="Storage" actions={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>}>
  <Progress value={62} label="Used" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" />
</Card>

<Card title="Details" headingLevel={3}>…</Card>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The title is a real heading with `aria-labelledby`, not a `span`.
- `raised` is the `variant` prop; the shadow applies only to it, and it is documented as floating only.
- Padding and gap are component tokens (`--ds-card-padding`, `--ds-card-gap`); `padding` is `'md' | 'none'` instead of a number.
- No `style` prop.

alternatives.reason: For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.

components.name: Chart
components.description:
A responsive bar or line chart for one series, drawn in SVG.

It is a single focusable image: `Tab` focuses it, the left and right arrow keys (and Home and
End) move between data points, and each point is announced politely ("Tue: 58. 2 of 7") and
shown in a label above it. Pointer users get the same label on hover. A visually hidden
`<table>` with a caption carries the same data for assistive technology.

Limits: one series, a value axis that always includes zero, categories spaced evenly, no
zoom, no stacked or grouped bars, no legend. The axis is not mirrored in right-to-left
languages (time reads left to right in charts).

props.name: data
props.description: The data, in display order (usually time). The chart does not sort.

props.name: type
props.description: `bar` (default) or `line`. One series per chart.

props.name: format
props.description:
Formats values on the axis, in the tooltip, in the announcement and in the data table.
Receives a number and returns text; use `formatCurrency` or `formatNumber` with the active
locale. Default: `formatNumber` (compact on the axis, full in the tooltip).

props.name: tone
props.description: Color of the active point and of the line: `accent` (default), `neutral`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`.

props.name: highlight
props.description:
Marks points by index with short text, for example `{ 29: 'Today', 12: 'Best day' }`. The
marked point is drawn in the strong ink color, and its text is printed above it and read
by screen readers, so the highlight never depends on color. Keep the texts short.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (a number is px, or any CSS length). Default `--ds-chart-height` (200px). The width is always 100% of the container.

props.name: description
props.description: Longer description of what the chart shows. Read after the name, together with the keyboard instructions.

props.name: categoryLabel
props.description: Header of the category column in the hidden data table. Default: the "Category" message.

props.name: valueLabel
props.description: Header of the value column in the hidden data table (for example "Sales"). Default: the "Value" message.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ instructions: (count: number, formatted: string) => string; point: (label: string, value: string, position: string, count: string, note?: string) => string; tableCaption: (name?: string) => string; category: string; value: string; note: string; empty: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the chart: what it shows ("Sales, last 30 days"). Required unless `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the chart (a visible heading).

keys.default: {formatted} data points. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for the first and last.
keys.description:
Instructions linked to the chart with `aria-describedby`. `count` is the number of data
points; `formatted` is the same number formatted for the locale.

keys.signature: (label: string, value: string, position: string, count: string, note?: string)
keys.description:
Announced (polite) when the user moves to a point. `value` is already formatted;
`note` is the highlight text of the point, if any ("Today").
Caption of the visually hidden data table. `name` is the accessible name of the chart, if it has a text one.
Header of the category column of the data table, unless `categoryLabel` is given.
Header of the value column of the data table, unless `valueLabel` is given.
Header of the note column of the data table (shown when a point is highlighted).
Text shown inside the plot when there is no data.

items.name: Highlight
items.description:
`highlight` marks points by index with text ("Today", "Best day"). The point is drawn in the
strong ink color with an outline, the text is printed above it and read by screen readers.

items.name: NegativeValues
items.description: The axis always includes zero and bars hang below it for negative values.

items.name: SmallValues
items.description: Tiny values still get a readable, round axis.

items.name: ManyPoints
items.description: With many points, category labels are skipped so they never overlap; the table keeps all of them.

items.name: KeyboardNavigation
items.description:
Tab focuses the chart; the arrow keys, Home and End move between points; each point is
announced politely and shown in a label. Escape clears it.

items.name: Hover
items.description: Hover shows the same label as the keyboard.

items.name: PortugueseBrazil
items.description: Instructions, announcements, the table caption and number formats follow the provider locale.

docs.summary: A small responsive bar or line chart for one series, drawn in SVG with no chart library. Grid and axis are quiet (dashed lines, mono labels); the data is reachable by keyboard and by a hidden table.
whenToUse: A trend or a comparison across a handful to a few dozen categories: sales per day, orders per week.
Next to the number it explains (a `StatCard`).
whenNotToUse: Several series, stacked or grouped bars, zoom, brushing, pie charts: not supported (see limits).
Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
Rankings with names: use `RankList`.
Exact values the user must read or compare: use `DataTable` (the chart is for shape).
keyboard: Keyboard: `Tab` focuses the chart (nothing announced yet). Left/Right (also Up/Down) move to the previous/next point, Home/End to the first/last, Escape clears the active point. The first Right arrow goes to the first point, the first Left arrow to the last. Movement stops at the ends.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A trend or a comparison across a handful to a few dozen categories: sales per day, orders per week.
- Next to the number it explains (a `StatCard`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Several series, stacked or grouped bars, zoom, brushing, pie charts: not supported (see limits).
- Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- Rankings with names: use `RankList`.
- Exact values the user must read or compare: use `DataTable` (the chart is for shape).

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  div[role=img][tabindex=0]   named by aria-label / aria-labelledby, described by the instructions
    svg[aria-hidden]          grid + tick labels, bars or line + area, category labels, highlight texts
    span                      value label of the active point (aria-hidden)
  span                        visually hidden description + keyboard instructions
  span[role=status]           visually hidden polite live region: "Tue: 58. 2 of 7"
  table (visually hidden)     caption, headers, one row per point
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                          | Type                    | Default  | Notes                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data`                        | `{ label, value }[]`    | -        | In display order; the chart never sorts                                           |
| `aria-label`                  | `string`                | -        | Required (or `aria-labelledby`): what the chart shows                             |
| `type`                        | `bar \| line`           | `bar`    |                                                                                   |
| `format`                      | `(value) => string`     | `Intl`   | Axis, label, announcement and table. Default: compact on the axis, full elsewhere |
| `tone`                        | `ChartTone`             | `accent` | Color of the active bar and of the line                                           |
| `highlight`                   | `Record<index, string>` |          | `{ 29: 'Today', 12: 'Best day' }`: ink fill + outline + text above + announced    |
| `height`                      | `number \| string`      | `200px`  | Width is always 100% of the container                                             |
| `description`                 | `string`                |          | Longer description, read before the keyboard instructions                         |
| `categoryLabel`, `valueLabel` | `string`                |          | Headers of the hidden table ("Day", "Sales")                                      |
| `messages`                    | `Partial<messages>`     |          | `instructions`, `point`, `tableCaption`, `category`, `value`, `note`, `empty`     |

`niceScale(min, max, tickCount?)` is exported: a pure helper that returns `{ min, max, step, ticks }` for a round axis. It always includes zero, handles all-zero data (0 to 1), tiny values (`0.00003`), huge values, negatives and non-finite input.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The plot is one `role="img"` with an accessible name and a description; the SVG inside is hidden. The visually hidden `<table>` with a `<caption>` is the text alternative and holds every value (and the highlight texts in a "Note" column).
- Keyboard: `Tab` focuses the chart (nothing announced yet). Left/Right (also Up/Down) move to the previous/next point, Home/End to the first/last, Escape clears the active point. The first Right arrow goes to the first point, the first Left arrow to the last. Movement stops at the ends.
- The active point is announced politely ("Tue: 58, Today. 2 of 7") and drawn as a label above it; hover shows the same label. The label is also in the SVG as text, never color-only.
- Highlights always carry text and a stronger shape (outline on bars, a ring marker on lines), so they do not depend on color. Active bars get a tone fill and outline.
- Bars use `line-control` (3:1 against the surface); tick labels use `text-3` (above 4.5:1 on `bg` and `surface`).
- Reduced motion: color transitions only apply when motion is allowed. Forced colors: bars, lines and labels switch to system colors (`GrayText`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight`).
- The chart does not mirror in right-to-left languages (time still runs left to right); the label position uses physical coordinates on purpose.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Name says what and when: "Sales, last 30 days". Labels are short ("Mon", "28") because they are printed under the plot.
- Highlight texts are one or two words ("Today", "Best day").
- Format money with `formatCurrency` (integer minor units) and the active locale; never hand-build strings.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.content:
- One series per chart. For two series use two charts side by side.
- Categories are spaced evenly (no time scale); labels are skipped when crowded (the table and the keyboard still reach every point).
- The value axis always includes zero. Up to about 100 ticks are generated at most (usually 4 to 7).
- Geometry (padding, bar width, label spacing) lives in `chartLayout.ts` as SVG units; every color, stroke, radius and font is a token.

sections.heading: Example
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The SVG has an accessible name, description and a visually hidden data table.
- Focusable with arrow-key traversal and polite announcements instead of a mouse-only tooltip.
- Negative values, all-zero data and tiny maxima work (nice-number axis instead of `log10`).
- `highlight` is `index -> text` (was `index -> color`): the highlight has a text and shape cue. `color` is now `tone`.
- Bars use `line-control` instead of `line-strong` so they reach 3:1.
- Responsive label skipping is tested; `height` can be any CSS length.

alternatives.name: ProportionBar
alternatives.reason: Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.

alternatives.name: RankList
alternatives.reason: Rankings with names: use `RankList`.

alternatives.name: DataTable
alternatives.reason: Exact values the user must read or compare: use `DataTable` (the chart is for shape).

components.name: ChatPanel
components.description:
A chat side panel for talking to an agent: header with Clear, a message log, suggested prompts
when empty, and a composer. Built for streaming replies.

Live-region approach: the message list is `role="log"` (a navigable transcript) with
`aria-live="off"`, so partial text never reaches a screen reader token by token. A separate
visually hidden `role="status"` region announces "Thinking…", "The assistant is responding",
and then the full reply once, when it is complete.

Message content is plain text. Pass `renderContent` to render sanitized markdown.

props.name: items
props.description: The conversation, oldest first. Update `content` and `status` of the last item as a reply streams in.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the panel. Defaults to the "Chat with the agent" message.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Default `2`.

props.name: busy
props.description: Waiting for the first part of a reply: shows a spinner with "Thinking…" and disables sending.

props.name: intro
props.description: Short text shown while the conversation is empty.

props.name: prompts
props.description: Suggested prompts shown while the conversation is empty. Pressing one sends it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder of the composer. Never a substitute for its label.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Called with the trimmed text when the user sends (Enter, or the send button) or presses a suggested prompt.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the user stops a reply that is being generated. Without it the button is disabled meanwhile.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Called with the failed message when the user presses Retry. Without it, failed messages have no Retry.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called when the user clears the conversation. Without it there is no Clear button.

props.name: renderContent
props.description:
Renders the content of a message. Use it to plug in a markdown renderer. Whatever it returns
is rendered as-is, so it must be **sanitized**: the design system never uses
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and ships no markdown library. Without it the content is plain
text with line breaks preserved.

props.name: sendVariant
props.description:
Visual weight of the send button: `secondary` (default) for a chat that sits beside the
page's main task, `primary` when the chat is the main task of the page. One primary per screen.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ title: string; clear: string; transcript: string; composerLabel: string; placeholder: string; send: string; stop: string; thinking: string; responding: string; you: string; assistant: string; ... 5 more ...; errorSaid: (text: string) => string; }>
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

docs.summary:
A chat panel for talking to an agent: header with a Clear action, a message log, suggested prompts when empty, and a composer. It supports streaming replies, Stop and Retry. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/agents/ChatPanel` (TODO `CMP-AGT-03`; groundwork for `AI-013`).
whenToUse: A side panel where the owner tests an agent, asks why it did something or asks for an adjustment.
Any short, owner-facing conversation with an assistant.
whenNotToUse: Customer-facing conversations: the chat is for the owner. Anything that goes to a customer must pass through an approval queue (`ApprovalCard`), never straight from the chat.
A one-shot prompt with a single answer: use a form.
Rich documents as replies: render those in the page and keep the chat short.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A side panel where the owner tests an agent, asks why it did something or asks for an adjustment.
- Any short, owner-facing conversation with an assistant.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Customer-facing conversations: the chat is for the owner. Anything that goes to a customer must pass through an approval queue (`ApprovalCard`), never straight from the chat.
- A one-shot prompt with a single answer: use a form.
- Rich documents as replies: render those in the page and keep the chat short.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
section (named by the heading)
  header          h{headingLevel} title + Clear (ghost, only with messages and onClear)
  viewport
    div[role=log][aria-live=off][tabindex=0]
      intro + suggested prompts (group)    only while empty
      message rows (user right, assistant left, error with Retry)
      "Thinking…" row                      while busy or a reply has no text yet
    Jump to latest                         only when scrolled away from the end
  div[role=status][aria-live=polite]       visually hidden announcer
  composer        Textarea (Enter sends) + one button: Send message | Stop generating
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                     | Type                       | Default                                                  | Notes                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`                                  | `ChatMessage[]`            | required                                                 | The conversation, oldest first. (Named `items` because `messages` overrides the catalog.) |
| `busy`                                   | `boolean`                  | `false`                                                  | Waiting for the first part of a reply.                                                    |
| `onSend`                                 | `(text: string) => void`   |                                                          | Trimmed text. Called from Enter, the button and the suggested prompts.                    |
| `onStop`                                 | `() => void`               |                                                          | Stop generating. The button is disabled while working without it.                         |
| `onRetry`                                | `(message) => void`        |                                                          | Shows Retry on failed messages.                                                           |
| `onClear`                                | `() => void`               |                                                          | Shows Clear when there are messages.                                                      |
| `intro` / `prompts`                      | `ReactNode` / `string[]`   |                                                          | Empty state.                                                                              |
| `renderContent`                          | `(message) => ReactNode`   | plain text                                               | Plug in a sanitized renderer (see below).                                                 |
| `sendVariant`                            | `'secondary' \| 'primary'` | `'secondary'`                                            | See "Send button".                                                                        |
| `title` / `headingLevel` / `placeholder` |                            | "Chat with the agent" / `2` / "Ask or request something" |                                                                                           |
| `messages`                               | partial catalog            |                                                          | Every string, including the announcements.                                                |

`ChatMessage`: `{ id: string; role: 'user' | 'assistant'; content: string; status?: 'complete' | 'streaming' | 'error' }`. Ids must be stable and unique; they are the React keys.

sections.heading: Streaming and live regions (research notes)
sections.content:
Sources: practitioner write-ups on accessible streaming chat UIs (azukiazusa.dev, tianpan.co), an IDE chat-panel pull request (TrixtyAI/ide#172) and the WAI-ARIA `log` role. There is no formal standard for streamed AI output; this is current practice, not tested with every screen reader.

- `role="log"` is the right role for a chat transcript (implicit polite live region, history in reading order). But a streamed reply rewrites one node many times, and a live region then reads it in fragments (or repeats it).
- Common practice (and what chat products do): keep the streaming text **out** of the live region, announce a short status while it generates, and announce the result once when complete.

What `ChatPanel` does:

1. The list is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"`: a labelled, focusable (`tabindex=0`, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard) transcript that screen reader users can read in order, without automatic announcements. It sets `aria-busy` while a reply is being produced.
2. A separate visually hidden `role="status"` (polite, atomic) announces: **"Thinking…"** while `busy`, **"The assistant is responding"** while a message is `streaming` (one announcement, not one per token), and **"Assistant: <full reply>"** once when the message becomes `complete` (or **"Error: …"** when it fails).
3. The user's own messages are never announced (they just typed them). Messages present on first render are history and are not announced.
4. The author ("You", "Assistant", "Error") is a visually hidden prefix of every message, since alignment and color are the only visual cue.

Not done: a "regenerate" action (only Retry for failed replies), and chunked announcements for very long replies.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- **Composer.** Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a new line. Enter is ignored while an **IME composition** is active (`isComposing`, and `keyCode 229` for Safari), so committing a CJK candidate never sends. Whitespace-only text is not sent. The field is not disabled while the assistant works, so the user can prepare the next message; sending is disabled meanwhile.
- **Send / Stop.** One button changes its label and action (Send message, Stop generating), so keyboard focus is not lost when a reply starts. With no `onStop` it is disabled while working.
- **Scroll anchoring.** The list follows new content only while the user is within a small distance of the bottom. If they scroll up to read, nothing moves, and "Jump to latest" appears. Sending a message returns to the bottom. No smooth scrolling is used, so `prefers-reduced-motion` needs no special handling; the spinner is already static under reduced motion.
- **Suggested prompts** send immediately. The chat is owner-facing and nothing leaves it.

sections.heading: Send button: secondary by default
sections.content: The panel normally sits beside the page's main task (an agent screen), and the screen already has its one primary action, so Send is `secondary`. When the chat is the main task of the page, pass `sendVariant="primary"`. One primary per screen.

sections.heading: Content policy: plain text by default
sections.content: Messages render as **plain text with line breaks**. The design system never uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and ships no markdown library. To show markdown, pass `renderContent` and return **React elements** from a renderer that sanitizes its input (a markdown-to-React library that does not allow raw HTML, with an allow-list of elements and URL schemes). `renderContent` runs for every message, including while it streams, so it must tolerate incomplete markdown. The story "CustomRenderer" shows the shape.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Region named by its heading; composer named "Message"; prompts in a group named "Suggested prompts"; Clear and Retry are real buttons.
- Keyboard: Tab order is header (Clear), the log (scroll with arrows and Page keys), Jump to latest when shown, composer, the Send/Stop button. Prompts are buttons in the log while empty.
- Error messages use text ("Error:" prefix, hidden), a danger border and danger text: color is never the only cue.
- Forced colors: the borders and focus use system colors through the shared tokens (outlines are transparent, not removed).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title and buttons are sentence case, verb plus object: "Clear conversation", "Send message", "Stop generating".
- Errors say how to fix: "The agent could not answer. Check your connection and try again."
- The agent never sends anything to a customer from this chat.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Messages are keyed by stable `id` instead of the array index; `status` adds streaming and error states.
- Enter ignores IME composition; Stop, Retry, scroll anchoring and Jump to latest are new.
- The log no longer announces every change: the live-region design above replaces `aria-live="polite"` on the list.
- Strings are in the catalog (including `pt-BR`); the composer is the design system `Textarea`; the Send button is the design system `Button` (secondary by default instead of a hand-made primary).
- `renderContent` is the markdown hook; no HTML injection.

components.description:
A checkbox with a native `<input type="checkbox">` (so `name` / `value` take part in form
submission), an 18px box and an optional description. The whole label row is the click target.

State props follow React Aria: `isSelected`, `defaultSelected` and `onChange(isSelected)`.
`isIndeterminate` is visual and semantic ("mixed") until the user toggles it.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.

props.name: errorMessage

Error text, for example "Accept the terms to continue". Shown while the checkbox is invalid
and the error is displayed (after a submit attempt with the default native validation).
Inside a `CheckboxGroup` put the error on the group instead.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`. Use `inputRef` for the `<input>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label

docs.summary: A checkbox with a native `<input type="checkbox">`, an 18px box and an optional description, plus a labelled group for several related checkboxes. Built on React Aria `CheckboxField` + `CheckboxButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description and an error outside the label) and `CheckboxGroup`. Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).
whenToUse: Independent yes/no choices, agreement ("I accept the terms"), selecting rows, picking several items from a list (`CheckboxGroup`).
`isIndeterminate` for a parent that summarizes partly selected children.
whenNotToUse: An on/off setting that applies at once: `Switch`.
One choice from several: `RadioGroup`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Independent yes/no choices, agreement ("I accept the terms"), selecting rows, picking several items from a list (`CheckboxGroup`).
- `isIndeterminate` for a parent that summarizes partly selected children.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- An on/off setting that applies at once: `Switch`.
- One choice from several: `RadioGroup`.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                      | Notes                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`                                                   | Visible label. Without it pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise).         |
| `description`                                             | Secondary text under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.              |
| `errorMessage`                                            | Error for a single checkbox (for example a required agreement). In a group, set it on the group. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)` | React Aria naming for controlled and uncontrolled use.                                           |
| `isIndeterminate`                                         | Shows a minus; the native input is `indeterminate` until toggled.                                |
| `name`, `value`                                           | Submitted with the form while checked (`value` defaults to `on`).                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`     | Standard states.                                                                                 |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                        | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                               |

`CheckboxGroup` takes `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`, `orientation` (`vertical` default, `horizontal`), `name`, `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange(values: string[])`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`. Each child `Checkbox` needs a `value`.

sections.heading: Look
sections.content:
- 18px box, radius from `--ds-checkbox-radius` (5px), `--ds-line-control` border (3:1 or better in every state), accent fill with a `--ds-text-inverse` check when selected, minus when indeterminate.
- Hover brightens the border; it never changes the fill.
- The whole row is the click target and is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8).
- A disabled group dims once as a whole; disabled single checkboxes use `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Space toggles the focused checkbox. Tab moves between checkboxes; each checkbox is a tab stop.
- Name comes from the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- Group: `role="group"` named by the label, with the group description and error.
- Forced colors: borders and the check glyph use system colors; the glyph (check or minus) carries the state.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Checkbox label="I accept the terms" name="terms" isRequired errorMessage="Accept the terms to continue." />

<CheckboxGroup label="Notify me about" name="topics" defaultValue={['orders']}>
  <Checkbox value="orders" label="New orders" />
  <Checkbox value="stock" label="Low stock" description="When a product drops below its minimum." />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A native input replaces `div role="checkbox"`; `name` and `value` take part in forms.
- Accessible name is required by the types; the label row is the click target.
- New: indeterminate, group, required, invalid, read-only, error text.
- Radius is a component token (the handoff hard-coded 5px); the fill is accent as in the handoff.
- Controlled props follow React Aria (`isSelected`, `onChange`) instead of `checked`/`onChange(checked)`.

components.name: ChoiceTiles
components.description:
Single-choice tiles: a `radiogroup` whose options are drawn as big buttons with a label and an
optional meta line. The group is one tab stop; arrow keys move focus and select, `Space`
selects (React Aria roving focus; arrows wrap at the ends like any radio group).
`value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(value)` follow React Aria. A group needs a name: pass
`label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

For a few short options drawn as one bar, use `SegmentedControl`; for a plain list of
options, use `RadioGroup`.

props.name: options
props.description: The tiles, in display order. Two to eight fit well.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the group is invalid.

props.name: columns
props.description:
Maximum number of columns. Default `2`. The grid collapses to fewer columns on narrow
containers so a tile never gets narrower than `--ds-choice-tiles-min-width`.

props.name: size
props.description: Tile height: `md` 40px or `lg` 48px (default).

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the group root.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).
