docs.summary:
Single-choice tiles: a labelled group where the options are drawn as large buttons with a label and an optional meta line. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` with custom radio buttons, so it is a real `radiogroup` with roving focus.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/ChoiceTiles.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-08`).
whenToUse: A choice with 2 to 8 short options where each option deserves weight: delivery method, plan, size, payment type.
When a secondary fact helps decide (a price, a duration, a code): use `meta`.
whenNotToUse: For a view mode or a small filter: use `SegmentedControl`.
For a long list of options or long descriptions: use `RadioGroup` (with descriptions) or `Select`.
For several selections at once: use `CheckboxGroup` or `TagGroup`.
keyboard: Keyboard: one tab stop; arrows (`←` `↑` previous, `→` `↓` next) move focus and select, wrapping at the ends; `Space` selects the focused tile. Disabled tiles are skipped.
examples:
<ChoiceTiles
  label="Delivery"
  columns={2}
  options={[
    { value: 'standard', label: 'Standard', meta: '3-5 days' },
    { value: 'express', label: 'Express', meta: '1 day' },
  ]}
  value={method}
  onChange={setMethod}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A choice with 2 to 8 short options where each option deserves weight: delivery method, plan, size, payment type.
- When a secondary fact helps decide (a price, a duration, a code): use `meta`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a view mode or a small filter: use `SegmentedControl`.
- For a long list of options or long descriptions: use `RadioGroup` (with descriptions) or `Select`.
- For several selections at once: use `CheckboxGroup` or `TagGroup`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=radiogroup] aria-labelledby=label
  label                      (group label, from `label`)
  div.grid                   (responsive grid, at most `columns` columns)
    div > label.tile         (one per option; hidden native radio inside)
      label text
      meta                   (optional, mono)
  description / error
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                                          | Type                   | Default      | Notes                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `options`                                                     | `ChoiceTilesOption[]`  | required     | `{ value, label, meta?, isDisabled? }`.                       |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                    | `ReactNode` / `string` | one required | Names the group. Enforced by the types.                       |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                  | `string`               | none         | Controlled / uncontrolled selection (React Aria names).       |
| `columns`                                                     | `number`               | `2`          | Maximum columns. Fewer on narrow containers (min tile 120px). |
| `size`                                                        | `'md' \| 'lg'`         | `'lg'`       | Minimum tile height: 40px or 48px.                            |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                                 | `ReactNode`            | none         | Linked with `aria-describedby`.                               |
| `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isReadOnly`, `name` | -                      | -            | Group state, forwarded to React Aria.                         |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Semantics: `radiogroup` of native radio inputs; the tile is the radio's label.
- Keyboard: one tab stop; arrows (`←` `↑` previous, `→` `↓` next) move focus and select, wrapping at the ends; `Space` selects the focused tile. Disabled tiles are skipped.
- State is not color alone: the selected tile has a doubled (2px) accent border, a soft fill and ink text, and screen readers get "checked".
- Boundaries: unselected tiles use `--ds-line-control` (3:1) and hover brightens the border instead of changing the fill, so the 3:1 holds in every state. The meta line uses `--ds-text-2` (`--ds-text-3` fails 4.5:1 on the selected fill).
- Focus: accent border plus ring. Forced colors: the selected border uses `Highlight`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels in sentence case, one to three words. Put the differentiating fact in `meta`, not in the label.
- Keep the same shape across tiles: avoid `meta` on some tiles only.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A `div role="radiogroup"` of `button role="radio"` had no roving focus or arrow keys; it is now React Aria `RadioGroup` (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`).
- The group is named with `label` (rendered and wired with `aria-labelledby`), `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; the handoff had no name.
- Columns are responsive: `columns` is a maximum and the grid collapses by minimum tile width. `size` is `md`/`lg` (tokens).
- Strings of options are plain props; `onChange` receives the value.
- Unselected borders are `--ds-line-control` instead of `--ds-line` (3:1), and the selected state adds a thicker border.

components.name: Citation
components.description:
An inline marker for a claim in an answer. It is a real link (`href="#..."`) that moves
focus to the matching source in the `SourceList`, so it works with a keyboard and a screen
reader: the name is "Source 2: Title", the visible text is the number.

props.name: number
props.description: Position of the source in the list, starting at 1. Shown as the marker text.

props.name: title
props.description: Title of the source. Part of the accessible name ("Source 2: Title").

props.name: listId
props.description: Id of the `SourceList` the source belongs to.

docs.summary: The numbered list of sources an answer is based on (`SourceList`) and the inline markers that point to it (`Citation`). Import both from `@loui/ds/patterns`.
whenToUse: An assistant answer that rests on documents, pages or records, and the owner should be able to check them.
whenNotToUse: Footnotes in long-form documents: use plain links.
A list of results the user searched for: use a table or a list of cards.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - An assistant answer that rests on documents, pages or records, and the owner should be able to check them.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Footnotes in long-form documents: use plain links.
- A list of results the user searched for: use a table or a list of cards.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: ``` p ... a claim [2] ... Citation: 2 section named by its heading ("Sources") ol li tabIndex=-1 (focus target) title (link when it has a url) · domain (mono) · snippet ```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`SourceList`

| Prop           | Type            | Default   | Notes                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | `string`        | -         | Required. Citations find their source through it.                            |
| `sources`      | `Source[]`      | -         | `{ id, title, url?, domain?, snippet? }`. The position is the source number. |
| `title`        | `string`        | "Sources" | Heading text.                                                                |
| `headingLevel` | `1`-`6`         | `3`       |                                                                              |
| `messages`     | partial catalog |           | `title`, `citation(number, title)`.                                          |

`Citation`: `number` (1-based, the visible text), `title`, `listId`, `sourceId`, plus anchor props. `getSourceElementId(listId, sourceId)` returns the DOM id when you need it.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A citation is a real link (`href="#..."`) named "Source 2: Title"; the visible text is the number, which the name contains.
- Activating it moves focus to the matching list item and scrolls it into view. It does not change the URL hash, so it does not fight your router. Without JavaScript the hash link still works.
- Source titles with a `url` are links that open in a new tab (with the external-link icon and a screen-reader note).
- The marker is 24 px square (WCAG 2.5.8).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Keep source order stable while the answer streams; append new sources at the end, so numbers already shown never change.
- Titles say what the page is, not "Click here". Snippets are short, plain text.

sections.content:

Orders move through four statuses .

```

components.name: ColorOption
components.description:
A selectable option that shows a color swatch and its name. It is a toggle button
(`aria-pressed`), so each option is chosen independently: put several in a
`role="group"` with an accessible name to pick any number of colors.
`isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)` follow React Aria.

Why a toggle and not a radio: the handoff uses it to pick several colors (a product's
available colors). To pick exactly one color, use `ChoiceTiles` or `RadioGroup` instead.

props.name: color
props.description: The color to show, as `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`.

props.name: label
props.description: Name of the color ("Navy"). It is the accessible name of the option and is always visible.

props.name: mark
props.description:
Optional short text after the label (a count, "Default", a code). It is part of the
accessible name. While the option is selected and no `mark` is given, a check is shown
instead.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the button.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<button>`.

items.name: InAGroup

docs.summary:
A selectable option that shows a color swatch and the color's name, with an optional short mark. It is a toggle button: each option is chosen on its own. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/ColorOption.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-04`).
whenToUse: Choose any number of colors from a list: the colors available for an item, the colors to filter by.
When the color name must be visible next to the swatch.
whenNotToUse: To choose exactly one color: use `ChoiceTiles` or `RadioGroup` (radio semantics).
A free-form color input: use a color field.
To display a color with no interaction: use `Swatch`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Choose any number of colors from a list: the colors available for an item, the colors to filter by.
- When the color name must be visible next to the swatch.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To choose exactly one color: use `ChoiceTiles` or `RadioGroup` (radio semantics).
- A free-form color input: use a color field.
- To display a color with no interaction: use `Swatch`.

sections.heading: Semantics decision: toggle, not radio
sections.content:
The option exposes `aria-pressed` (a toggle button), not a radio. The handoff uses it for multi-select ("which colors does this item come in?"), and a radio group would force a single answer and a roving tab stop. React Aria `ColorSwatchPicker` was evaluated and does not fit: it is a single-select listbox of bare swatches with generated color names and no room for a visible label or mark. For single choice, use `ChoiceTiles`.

Group several options in `role="group"` with an `aria-label` ("Available colors"); every option is its own tab stop.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
button[aria-pressed]
  Swatch (decorative)
  label
  mark | check            (mark text if given, otherwise a check while selected)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                          | Type                       | Default  | Notes                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `color`                                       | `string`                   | required | `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`.                                     |
| `label`                                       | `string`                   | required | Visible name; accessible name of the button.             |
| `mark`                                        | `ReactNode`                | none     | Short text after the label. Part of the accessible name. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange` | `boolean` / `(on) => void` | `false`  | React Aria names.                                        |
| `isDisabled`                                  | `boolean`                  | `false`  | Disabled opacity token and a dashed border.              |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `aria-pressed` states the selection; the selected look is also a doubled accent border, a soft fill and a check (not color alone).
- The swatch is decorative because the label names the color.
- Boundaries use `--ds-line-control` (3:1); hover brightens the border, never the fill. Focus: accent border and ring. Forced colors: `Highlight` border when selected.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Label is the color name in sentence case ("Brick red"); `mark` is two or three words at most.

```

- Built on React Aria `ToggleButton` (hover, press, focus and keyboard from RAC); no React hover state or inline styles.
- The swatch is decorative; the disabled opacity is `--ds-opacity-disabled` (handoff 0.45); the border is `--ds-line-control` instead of `--ds-line`.
- `selected` / `disabled` / `onClick` became `isSelected` / `isDisabled` / `onChange(isSelected)`. The mark ("✓" glyph) is an icon while selected, or your own `mark` text.

components.name: Combobox
components.description:
A text input with a filtered list of options in a popover (ARIA combobox pattern, built on
React Aria `ComboBox`): the input has `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`,
`aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`, so focus stays in
the input while the arrow keys move through the list.

Typing filters the options accent- and case-insensitively. `Enter` selects the highlighted
option, `Escape` closes the list and then restores the selected text, `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`
open the list and move, `Home` / `End` move the caret in the input (React Aria keeps them for
text editing). With `allowsCustomValue` the typed text itself is a valid value.

Use it for long lists (10 or more options); for fewer prefer `Select`.

props.name: options
props.description: The options, or groups of options. Keep the order you want users to see (see Combobox.md).

props.name: value
props.description: The selected option `value`; `null` means nothing is selected. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initially selected `value` when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the selected `value`, or `null` when the selection is cleared.

props.name: filter
props.description:
How options are matched against the typed text. Default: accent- and case-insensitive
"contains" on the label (`matchesSearch`), so `cafe` finds `Café`. Pass your own function,
or `false` to show `options` as given: use it when the list is loaded from a server as the
user types (listen to `onInputChange`, update `options`, set `isLoading` meanwhile).

props.name: isLoading
props.description:
Shows a spinner in the box and, when there are no options yet, a "Loading" row instead of
"No results". The consumer owns the data: see `filter={false}` and `onInputChange`.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the box is empty. Never a substitute for the label.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: popoverClassName
props.description: Class name for the popover that holds the options.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Class name for the `<input>` element.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ noResults: string; loading: string; showOptions: string; } & { requiredMark: string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `noResults`, `loading`, `showOptions`, `requiredMark`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

keys.description: Shown in the list when the typed text matches no option.
Shown in the list while options are loading and there are none yet; also names the spinner.
Accessible name of the button that opens the list.

docs.summary: A text input with a filtered list of options in a popover (ARIA combobox pattern). Built on React Aria `ComboBox` (`Input`, `Button`, `Popover`, `ListBox`). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md). Task: CMP-INP-01.
whenToUse: Choosing from a long list (10 or more options): customers, products, cities.
Choosing from a list or typing a new value (`allowsCustomValue`).
Options loaded from a server as the user types (see Async).
whenNotToUse: 2 to 4 options: `RadioGroup`. 4 to 9 options: `Select`.
Searching the whole app or a table: `SearchInput`.
Several selections: not supported yet (multiple selection is P3).

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Choosing from a long list (10 or more options): customers, products, cities.
- Choosing from a list or typing a new value (`allowsCustomValue`).
- Options loaded from a server as the user types (see Async).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- 2 to 4 options: `RadioGroup`. 4 to 9 options: `Select`.
- Searching the whole app or a table: `SearchInput`.
- Several selections: not supported yet (multiple selection is P3).

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                                                                | Notes                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                                          | One is required.                                                                                                                |
| `options`                                                                                                           | `ComboboxOption[]` (`value`, `label`, `description`, `meta`, `isDisabled`) or groups `{ id, label, options }`.                  |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                                                                        | The selected option `value`, `null` for none.                                                                                   |
| `inputValue` / `defaultInputValue` / `onInputChange`                                                                | The text in the box (React Aria props, passed through).                                                                         |
| `allowsCustomValue`                                                                                                 | The typed text is a valid value; the form then receives the text.                                                               |
| `filter`                                                                                                            | Default accent- and case-insensitive "contains" on the label (`matchesSearch`). A function, or `false` for no client filtering. |
| `isLoading`                                                                                                         | Spinner in the box; "Loading" row when there are no options yet.                                                                |
| `menuTrigger`                                                                                                       | `input` (default), `focus` or `manual`.                                                                                         |
| `description`, `errorMessage`, `size`, `placeholder`, `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | As in `Select`.                                                                                                                 |
| `messages`                                                                                                          | `noResults`, `loading`, `showOptions`, `requiredMark`.                                                                          |

Option order is yours (see `Select.md`): sort with `sortByText` unless the order carries meaning.

sections.heading: Async options (documented pattern; a full async list is P2)
sections.content: Set `filter={false}`, keep the query from `onInputChange`, fetch, and pass the result as `options` with `isLoading` meanwhile. The component never fetches and does not virtualize; for thousands of options filter on the server.

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                     | Behavior                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Typing                  | Opens the list and filters                                                                       |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Open the list (first / last option) and move; focus stays in the input (`aria-activedescendant`) |
| `Enter`                 | Select the highlighted option and close                                                          |
| `Escape`                | Close the list; pressed again, restore the selected text (clear with `allowsCustomValue`)        |
| `Home` / `End`          | Move the caret in the input (React Aria keeps them for text editing, not for the list)           |
| `Tab`                   | Commit and leave                                                                                 |

The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The chevron button ("Show options") is out of the tab order. While the list is open React Aria hides the rest of the page from assistive technology. An option's accessible name contains label, meta and description. The empty state is a single option-like row so screen readers announce it.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label with the noun ("Customer"). Empty state text is "No results" (sentence case, no punctuation); localize with `messages`.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Combobox
  label="Customer"
  name="customer"
  options={sortByText(customers, (c) => c.label, locale)}
  onChange={setCustomerId}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A real combobox: the search box is the field itself (the handoff had a button that opened a popover with an unlabelled search input), with ARIA wiring, `Escape` behavior and form submission of the option value.
- Filtering is accent-insensitive (the handoff used `toLowerCase`).
- `searchPlaceholder`, `emptyText` and `placeholder` strings became messages and `placeholder`; `meta` and `description` are kept/added; sections, custom values, loading, sizes and invalid/disabled/read-only states are new.
- The popover is limited to the viewport width: a full-width box on a narrow screen no longer overflows the page.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description:
A command palette: a modal with a search field and a grouped list of commands, opened with
`Mod+K` (configurable). Built on React Aria `Autocomplete`, `SearchField` and `ListBox` inside a
`ModalOverlay`: the search field is a combobox that keeps focus while the arrow keys move
through the commands (`aria-activedescendant`), `Enter` runs the highlighted command and
closes, `Escape` closes and focus returns to where it was.

Search ignores case and accents and matches label, keywords and group. With `includeHotkeys`
it also lists the shortcuts registered through `useHotkeys`.

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands. Search covers the label, the keywords and the group.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the palette opens (from the hotkey) or closes (Escape, outside press, a command ran).

props.name: hotkey
props.description:
The shortcut that opens the palette, registered in the hotkey registry. Default `'Mod+K'`.
It works while an input has focus. Pass `false` to open the palette only through `isOpen`.

props.name: includeHotkeys
props.description:
Also list every shortcut registered with `useHotkeys` that has a `description`, as a command
that runs its handler (grouped by the shortcut's `group`, or under "Shortcuts"). A registered
shortcut whose description equals a command's label is listed once. Default `false`.

props.name: recentIds
props.description:
Ids of recently run commands, most recent first, shown under "Recent" while the search is
empty. Persisting them is up to the app: collect them in `onRun`.

props.name: maxRecent
props.description: Most recent commands shown. Default `5`.

props.name: onRun
props.description: Called after a command was chosen, with its id, so the app can update `recentIds`.

props.name: sort
props.description:
Order of groups and commands. `alphabetical` (default) sorts both with the active locale,
ignoring accents; `given` keeps the order of `commands` and lists groups in order of first use.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search field. Default from messages: "Search or run a command".

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ title: string; placeholder: string; commands: string; recent: string; ungrouped: string; shortcuts: string; noResults: string; noResultsHint: string; openDescription: string; openGroup: string; resultCount: (n: number) => string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the palette panel.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the panel (`role="dialog"`).

keys.description: Accessible name of the palette dialog.
Placeholder and accessible name of the search field.
Accessible name of the list of commands.
Heading of the group of recently run commands.
Heading for commands that have no `group`.
Heading for registered shortcuts that have no `group` (when `includeHotkeys` is set).
Shown when no command matches the search.
Second line of the empty state: what to do next.
Description of the shortcut that opens the palette, listed by `ShortcutsHelp`.
Group of the shortcut that opens the palette.
Spoken after each search: how many commands match.

items.name: Default
items.description: The keyboard contract: open with Ctrl+K, type, arrows move, Enter runs and closes, focus returns.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: Filtered

docs.summary: A modal search box that finds and runs commands from the keyboard. It opens with `Mod+K` (Command K on Apple platforms, Control K elsewhere), filters a grouped list as you type and runs the chosen command. It is the "⌘K for everything" of AGENTS.md section 5.
whenToUse: An app with many actions or destinations that should all be reachable without the mouse: navigate, create, filter, switch.
Together with `useHotkeys`, so every shortcut is also discoverable by name (`includeHotkeys`).
whenNotToUse: Searching data (orders, customers): use `SearchInput` with suggestions, or a results page. The palette runs commands; a command may open that search.
Choosing a value in a form: use `Combobox` or `Select`.
A short list of actions on one object: use `Menu`.
keyboard: Keyboard: `Mod+K` opens, `↑ ↓` move, `Enter` runs, `Esc` closes. Hover highlights like the keyboard does.
examples:
<HotkeyProvider>
  <CommandPalette
    commands={[
      {
        id: 'orders',
        label: 'Go to orders',
        group: 'Navigation',
        shortcut: '1',
        onAction: () => navigate('/orders'),
      },
      {
        id: 'new',
        label: 'Create order',
        group: 'Orders',
        keywords: ['invoice'],
        shortcut: 'F2',
        onAction: createOrder,
      },
    ]}
    includeHotkeys
    recentIds={recent}
    onRun={(id) => setRecent((ids) => [id, ...ids.filter((x) => x !== id)].slice(0, 5))}
  />
</HotkeyProvider>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- An app with many actions or destinations that should all be reachable without the mouse: navigate, create, filter, switch.
- Together with `useHotkeys`, so every shortcut is also discoverable by name (`includeHotkeys`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Searching data (orders, customers): use `SearchInput` with suggestions, or a results page. The palette runs commands; a command may open that search.
- Choosing a value in a form: use `Combobox` or `Select`.
- A short list of actions on one object: use `Menu`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
ModalOverlay (dims the page, dialog layer)
  Modal
    Dialog  role="dialog"  aria-label="Command palette"
      SearchField / Input  role="combobox"  (focus stays here)
      ListBox  role="listbox"  aria-label="Commands"
        Section "Recent"                (only while the search is empty)
        Section <group>
          Option  icon · label (match highlighted) · shortcut (Kbd)
      status    "3 commands"            (visually hidden live region)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop             | Type                          | Default          | Notes                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `commands`       | `Command[]`                   | required         | `id`, `label`, `group`, `keywords`, `shortcut`, `icon`, `onAction`, `isDisabled`           |
| `isOpen`         | `boolean`                     | -                | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`                                            |
| `defaultOpen`    | `boolean`                     | `false`          | Initial state when uncontrolled                                                            |
| `onOpenChange`   | `(isOpen: boolean) => void`   | -                | Opens from the hotkey; closes on Escape, outside press or after a command                  |
| `hotkey`         | `string \| false`             | `'Mod+K'`        | Registered in the hotkey registry. Works from inside inputs. `false`: no hotkey            |
| `includeHotkeys` | `boolean`                     | `false`          | Also lists described shortcuts registered with `useHotkeys`; running one calls its handler |
| `recentIds`      | `string[]`                    | -                | Most recent first. The app stores them (collect with `onRun`)                              |
| `maxRecent`      | `number`                      | `5`              | Most recent commands shown                                                                 |
| `onRun`          | `(commandId: string) => void` | -                | Called when a command is chosen                                                            |
| `sort`           | `'alphabetical' \| 'given'`   | `'alphabetical'` | Groups and commands sorted with the locale, ignoring accents, or as given                  |
| `placeholder`    | `string`                      | message          | "Search or run a command"                                                                  |
| `messages`       | `Partial<messages>`           | -                | Per-instance overrides (see below)                                                         |

`Command.shortcut` is display only: a combo (`'Mod+Shift+P'`, `'F2'`) or `Kbd` keys (`['Mod', 'K']`). It does not bind the key.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- Search matches the label, the `keywords` and the group, ignoring case and accents (`cafe` finds "Open café report"). The matching part of the label is highlighted. Disabled commands stay searchable but cannot run.
- The first command is highlighted when the palette opens and after each typed character, so `Enter` runs it at once. `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` move the highlight; focus stays in the field.
- `Enter` (or a click) runs the command and closes the palette. The command runs once the palette has unmounted, so a dialog it opens is not fought over by focus restoration.
- `Escape` always closes, even when the field has text (no "clear first" step), and focus returns to the element that had it.
- The search text resets every time the palette opens.
- Shortcuts of the page do not fire while the palette is open (see `docs/architecture/hotkeys.md`).
- `includeHotkeys`: a registered shortcut whose description equals a command's label is listed once (the command wins); the palette's own shortcut is not listed.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A modal `dialog` named "Command palette". Focus is trapped, the page behind is inert, focus returns on close (React Aria).
- The field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox popup: `role="combobox"`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-activedescendant` for the highlighted option. React Aria delays moving `aria-activedescendant` by about 500 ms while typing so screen readers are not interrupted by the highlight change.
- Groups are `role="group"` named by their heading. Disabled options are `aria-disabled`.
- After each search a visually hidden `role="status"` says how many commands match ("3 commands", "No commands found").
- Shortcuts are drawn with `Kbd`, which adds spoken key names ("Control Shift O") to the option's name.
- Keyboard: `Mod+K` opens, `↑ ↓` move, `Enter` runs, `Esc` closes. Hover highlights like the keyboard does.
- Motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion`; `forced-colors` gets a system border and highlight outline.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are a verb plus an object in sentence case: "Create order", "Go to customers".
- Group names are nouns: "Navigation", "Orders". Use `keywords` for synonyms and other languages instead of long labels.
- Messages: `title`, `placeholder`, `commands`, `recent`, `ungrouped`, `shortcuts`, `noResults`, `noResultsHint`, `openDescription`, `openGroup`, `resultCount(n)`. English and pt-BR ship; override any of them per instance or through `DSProvider messages={{ CommandPalette: { ... } }}`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<HotkeyProvider>
  <CommandPalette
    commands={[
      {
        id: 'orders',
        label: 'Go to orders',
        group: 'Navigation',
        shortcut: '1',
        onAction: () => navigate('/orders'),
      },
      {
        id: 'new',
        label: 'Create order',
        group: 'Orders',
        keywords: ['invoice'],
        shortcut: 'F2',
        onAction: createOrder,
      },
    ]}
    includeHotkeys
    recentIds={recent}
    onRun={(id) => setRecent((ids) => [id, ...ids.filter((x) => x !== id)].slice(0, 5))}
  />
</HotkeyProvider>
```

Open it from a button instead of (or as well as) the hotkey:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
<Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Commands</Button>
<CommandPalette commands={commands} isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The handoff had no command palette; the ERP bound F2/F9/N/Enter/Esc/1-4 directly. Here those keys are ordinary `useHotkeys` registrations and the palette lists them.
- Size, list height and offset are tokens (`--ds-command-palette-*`).

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.description:
A destructive-action confirmation: an `alertdialog` with the question as the title, the
consequence in one sentence, a Cancel button and a confirm button that names the action.

Initial focus is on **Cancel**, so pressing Enter or Space right after the dialog opens never
confirms. Outside presses do not dismiss it (`Escape` and Cancel do), because the user has to
answer. Follow a confirmed delete with a `Toast` that offers Undo when the data can come back.

props.name: title
props.description:
The question, naming the object: "Delete order #1048?". Not "Are you sure?" and not
"Confirm".

props.name: description
props.description:
The consequence, in one sentence: "The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't
be undone." Required, because a confirmation without a consequence is only a speed bump.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description:
Label of the confirming button. Names the action, verb plus object: "Delete order". Never
"OK", "Yes" or "Confirm".

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the user confirms. The dialog closes afterwards unless `closeOnConfirm` is `false`.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional extra content between the description and the buttons (for example a list of affected items).

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` (default): red `danger-solid` button for a destructive action. `neutral`: the `primary` button.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
Which button gets the initial focus. `cancel` (default) is the safe choice and the
product principle for destructive actions; `confirm` is for non-destructive confirmations.

props.name: closeOnConfirm
props.description: Keep the dialog open after `onConfirm`, for example while an async request runs. Default `true` closes it.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Shows a spinner on the confirm button and ignores presses while a request runs.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: size
props.description: Maximum width: `sm` 420px (default), `md` 540px, `lg` 680px. Narrower on small screens.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
The element that opens the dialog (a `Button`). Optional: omit it and control the dialog
with `isOpen`. Focus returns to the element that was focused when the dialog opened.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog opens or closes.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Whether pressing the overlay closes the dialog. Default `true`; `ConfirmDialog` sets `false`.

props.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
props.description: Disables closing with `Escape`. Use it only while a request is running.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the dialog panel.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the dialog panel.

keys.description: Label of the button that dismisses a `ConfirmDialog` without doing anything.

items.name: Default
items.description: Initial focus is on Cancel, so Enter right after opening cancels instead of deleting.

items.name: ConfirmFlow
items.description:
The whole destructive flow with a pointer: opening lands focus on Cancel (not on the red
button), and the focus ring is part of the visual baseline. TEST-012.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: Neutral
items.description: A non-destructive confirmation: primary button, focus on the action.

items.name: Default
items.description: The keyboard contract: open, focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, focus returns.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: InsideSheet
items.description: A Dialog opened from a Sheet. Escape closes the Dialog first and leaves the Sheet open.

docs.summary:
A modal dialog, and `ConfirmDialog` for destructive confirmations. Built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Dialog` (CMP-FBK-03). Overlay management: ARCH-005.
whenToUse: A short task or decision that blocks the page: edit a record in a small form, confirm a deletion.
`ConfirmDialog`: every deletion. "Deleting always asks for confirmation" (AGENTS.md section 5).
whenNotToUse: Reversible actions (mark, link, change status): do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`. Do not confirm.
Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
A message about the page: use `Alert`.
Nesting dialogs more than two deep.
keyboard: `Escape` closes **only the top-most layer**. A `Dialog` opened from a `Sheet` closes first and the Sheet stays (tested). Every overlay uses React Aria's shared layer stack instead of its own window listener (ARCH-005).
examples:
<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  title="Delete order #1048?"
  description="The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete order"
  onConfirm={() => deleteOrder(1048)}
/>

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit customer</Button>}
  title="Edit customer"
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save customer</Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Name" autoFocus />
</Dialog>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A short task or decision that blocks the page: edit a record in a small form, confirm a deletion.
- `ConfirmDialog`: every deletion. "Deleting always asks for confirmation" (AGENTS.md section 5).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Reversible actions (mark, link, change status): do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`. Do not confirm.
- Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
- Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
- A message about the page: use `Alert`.
- Nesting dialogs more than two deep.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
DialogTrigger
  trigger            Button                                (optional when controlled)
  ModalOverlay       --ds-overlay, z dialog
    Modal            raised surface, strong line, radius lg, dialog shadow, width sm | md | lg
      Dialog         role=dialog | alertdialog, aria-labelledby = title, aria-describedby = description
        header       h2 title (17/24, 600) · description (14/22, text-2)
        body         scrolls
        footer       actions aligned to the end; divider when there is a body
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`Dialog`

| Prop                                      | Type                                    | Default  | Notes                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                   | `ReactNode` (required)                  | none     | Heading and accessible name.                            |
| `description`                             | `ReactNode`                             |          | Linked with `aria-describedby`.                         |
| `children`                                | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |          | Body.                                                   |
| `footer`                                  | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |          | Actions.                                                |
| `size`                                    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                  | `sm`     | Max width 420 / 540 / 680 px (`--ds-dialog-width-*`).   |
| `role`                                    | `'dialog' \| 'alertdialog'`             | `dialog` |                                                         |
| `trigger`                                 | `ReactElement`                          |          | Optional when controlled.                               |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                         |          | Controlled / uncontrolled open state.                   |
| `isDismissable`                           | `boolean`                               | `true`   | Press on the overlay closes it.                         |
| `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`               | `boolean`                               | `false`  | Disables `Escape`; use only while a request is running. |

`ConfirmDialog` adds: `confirmLabel` (required, names the action), `onConfirm` (required), `tone` (`danger` | `neutral`), `initialFocus` (`cancel` | `confirm`, default `cancel`), `closeOnConfirm`, `isPending`, `messages` (`cancel`). `description` is required: it is the consequence. `isDismissable` defaults to `false`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Focus is **trapped** while open, **restored** to the element that opened it, the page behind is `inert`/`aria-hidden` and does not scroll (all React Aria).
- **Initial focus.** Plain `Dialog`: the dialog itself, or the child with `autoFocus` (put it on the first field). `ConfirmDialog`: **Cancel**, so pressing Enter or Space as soon as it opens never confirms. The handoff focused nothing.
- `Escape` closes **only the top-most layer**. A `Dialog` opened from a `Sheet` closes first and the Sheet stays (tested). Every overlay uses React Aria's shared layer stack instead of its own window listener (ARCH-005).
- Named by the title (`aria-labelledby`, from the `h2`) and described by the description (`aria-describedby`; not linked in the handoff).
- `ConfirmDialog` uses `alertdialog`, which screen readers announce with its description. A press outside does not dismiss it.
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade and 8 px rise are removed. Forced colors: border in `CanvasText`.
- 320 px reflow: the dialog shrinks to the viewport less the 24 px gutter and the body scrolls.

### Layers

Overlays are portaled to `body`, each with its own layer: sheet (40) < dialog (45) < dropdown (50) < popover (55) < toast (58) < tooltip (60). A `Select`, `Menu`, `Popover` or `Combobox` opened from inside a Dialog or Sheet therefore renders **above** it. This is safe because a modal blocks page-level popovers while it is open. Tests assert the order.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: a question for confirmations that names the object ("Delete order #1048?"), otherwise verb plus object or a noun phrase ("Edit customer"). Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
- Description: the consequence in one sentence ("The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone.").
- Buttons: Cancel (secondary) then the action, verb plus object ("Save customer", "Delete order"). Never "OK" or "Yes". One primary action.
- After a confirmed delete show a `Toast` with **Undo** when the data can come back.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  title="Delete order #1048?"
  description="The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete order"
  onConfirm={() => deleteOrder(1048)}
/>

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit customer</Button>}
  title="Edit customer"
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save customer</Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Name" autoFocus />
</Dialog>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Focus trap, restore, initial focus, scroll lock and inert background from React Aria; the handoff had none.
- `aria-labelledby` and a linked `aria-describedby` instead of `aria-label={title}`.
- No window-level `Escape` listener per dialog; stack-aware.
- `width` (420 / 440) became `size` (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) with component tokens; `contained` mode is not ported (a story frame hosts open dialogs in the docs).
- New: `ConfirmDialog` implementing the destructive-confirmation principle, controlled and uncontrolled state, messages (English and pt-BR).

for no maximum. Default is the page content maximum (`--ds-content-max`, 1200px).

props.name: gutter

docs.summary: Centers page content and limits its line length: a maximum inline size and a side gutter.
whenToUse: Inside the `main` of a page to keep content readable on wide screens.
Settings pages and forms (`size="sm"` or `"md"`), dashboards (`"lg"`).
whenNotToUse: Inside `Card`, `Dialog` or `Sheet`: those set their own padding.
For full-bleed content such as a table: use `size="full"` or skip the container.
examples:
<main id="main">
  <Container size="md">
    <Heading level={1}>Settings</Heading>…
  </Container>
</main>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Inside the `main` of a page to keep content readable on wide screens.
- Settings pages and forms (`size="sm"` or `"md"`), dashboards (`"lg"`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Inside `Card`, `Dialog` or `Sheet`: those set their own padding.
- For full-bleed content such as a table: use `size="full"` or skip the container.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (max-inline-size, margin-inline: auto, padding-inline: gutter)
  children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop     | Type                                | Default              | Notes                                                               |
| -------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`   | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'full'`    | content max (1200px) | 640 / 960 / 1200px (`--ds-container-*`); `full` removes the maximum |
| `gutter` | `boolean`                           | `true`               | Adds `--ds-content-gutter` (24px) inline padding                    |
| `as`     | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'article' …` | `'div'`              | Element to render                                                   |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Responsive behavior
sections.content: The container is `inline-size: 100%` up to its maximum, so it narrows with the viewport and keeps its gutter down to 320px.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Carries no landmark role. The page's single `main` comes from `AppShell` (or your own `<main>`); put the container inside it.
- Logical properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-inline`) make it direction-neutral.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<main id="main">
  <Container size="md">
    <Heading level={1}>Settings</Heading>…
  </Container>
</main>
```

Inside `AppShell`, which already pads `main`, use `<Container gutter={false}>` or `<AppShell padded={false}>`.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff laid screens out at a fixed 1180px minimum. The container gives a maximum, never a minimum.

components.name: CurrencyInput
components.description:
A money field. The value is an integer in minor units (ADR-0006) plus an ISO `currency`, never
a float. It uses the **digits-only typing model**: every digit you type shifts in from the
right (typing `1`, `2`, `3` gives `1.23`), separators are ignored, Backspace shifts the last
digit out, and the caret always stays at the end. Pasting is smarter: `12.50` and `12,50` both
paste as 12.50, read against the locale (see CurrencyInput.md). The box is mono and
right-aligned; the currency symbol is part of the text, where the locale puts it, so screen
readers announce it with the amount.

The form receives the integer minor units under `name`.

props.name: currency
props.description:
ISO 4217 code of the currency (`'USD'`, `'BRL'`, `'JPY'`). It decides the number of fraction
digits (JPY has 0, KWD has 3), the symbol and where the locale places it.

props.name: value
props.description:
The amount in **integer minor units** (ADR-0006): `123456` is `$1,234.56` in USD and
`¥123456` in JPY. `null` is an empty field (nothing entered), which is different from `0`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial amount when uncontrolled. Defaults to empty (`null`).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new amount in minor units, or `null` when the field is emptied.

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: Accepts negative amounts. Type `-` anywhere to flip the sign. Default `false`.

props.name: maxDigits
props.description:
Most digits the amount may have, fraction digits included (`15` is the maximum, the
largest count that is always a safe integer). Typing beyond it is ignored. Default `15`.

props.name: name
props.description:
Name for form submission. The form receives the **integer minor units** (`123456`), or an
empty string when the field is empty, never the formatted text.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the field is empty.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Class name for the `<input>` element.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

docs.summary: A money field. The value is an **integer in minor units** plus an ISO 4217 `currency` (ADR-0006), never a float. Built on [Input](../Input/Input.md); the formatting comes from `Intl` through `formatCurrency`-style helpers and `parseCurrencyInput` (see `docs/architecture/utilities.md`). Task: CMP-INP-05.
whenToUse: Prices, totals, payments, adjustments: anywhere a person types an amount of money.
whenNotToUse: Quantities or measures: `NumberField`.
Showing an amount (not editing it): `formatCurrency(minorUnits, currency, locale)` from `@loui/ds`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Prices, totals, payments, adjustments: anywhere a person types an amount of money.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Quantities or measures: `NumberField`.
- Showing an amount (not editing it): `formatCurrency(minorUnits, currency, locale)` from `@loui/ds`.

sections.heading: Editing model: digits shift in from the right (decision)
sections.content:
Two models were considered:

1. **React Aria `NumberField` with `style: 'currency'`**. Reuses its parsing and stepping, but its editing model is "type a number, format on blur": locale decimal marks must be typed, the caret and text change on blur, and the value is a JS `number` in major units, so every boundary needs `Math.round(x * 100)` and float drift (`0.1 + 0.2`) becomes a bug source. Money in the handoff is also typed without separators.
2. **Digits-only typing** (the handoff model, implemented by `parseCurrencyInput`). Typing `1`, `2`, `3` gives `$1.23`; `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6` gives `$1,234.56`. Separators and symbols are ignored, `Backspace` shifts the last digit out, the caret always stays at the end. The state is an integer from the first keystroke to the form value, so there is no floating point anywhere; the same code serves JPY (0 digits) and KWD (3 digits); no locale decimal mark has to be known to type.

**Decision: digits-only typing**, with a smarter **paste** (below). The trade-off: a person who types `12.5` gets `$1.25`, not `$12.50`. That is the point of the model (type `1250`), the field always shows what it will submit, and paste covers the decimal-writing habit.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange` are **integer minor units** or `null` (empty, which is not `0`). `onChange` receives `null` when the field is emptied (select all, then `Delete`).
- Display: the currency's own format with the symbol where the locale puts it (`$1,234.56`, `R$ 1.234,56`, `1.234,56 €`, `¥1,234`), mono, tabular, right-aligned. The symbol is part of the text, so screen readers announce it with the amount.
- Caret: always moved to the end after every edit and whenever you click or arrow into the text. A range selection (Ctrl+A) is allowed so you can clear the field.
- `allowNegative`: type `-` anywhere to flip the sign; a lone `-` shows `-$0.00` (negative zero) and the next digit keeps the sign. Without it, minus signs are ignored.
- `maxDigits` (default and maximum 15, the largest count that is always a safe integer): typing beyond it is ignored. Large amounts are exact (`$9,999,999,999,999.99` is `999999999999999`).
- **Paste** reads the text against the locale: `12.50` and `12,50` both paste as 12.50; `1,234.56` in en-US and `1.234,56` in pt-BR are grouped thousands; a lone separator followed by exactly three digits is a thousands group (`1.234` is 1234 in pt-BR but 1.23 in en-US because `.` is the en-US decimal mark); extra fraction digits are rounded half up; symbols and spaces are dropped; text without digits is ignored.
- **Form**: `name` submits the **integer minor units** (`123456`) or an empty string, through a hidden input; it is not sent while the field is disabled. The visible text is never submitted.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                                                                | Notes                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `currency`                                                                                                          | Required ISO 4217 code.          |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`                                                                               | `number \| null` in minor units. |
| `allowNegative`, `maxDigits`                                                                                        | See above.                       |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                                          | One is required.                 |
| `description`, `errorMessage`, `size`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `placeholder`, `name` | As in `Input`.                   |
| `inputRef`, `ref`, `className`, `inputClassName`, `messages`                                                        | As in `Input`.                   |

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content: A text input (`inputmode="numeric"`, or `text` with `allowNegative` so a minus can be typed on mobile) named by the label, described by the description and the error. Digits type, `Backspace` removes the last digit, `-` flips the sign when allowed. There is no live region; the value is announced as typed. The border stays 3:1 in every state (shared Input styling).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label the thing being priced ("Price per unit"). The currency symbol is automatic, never part of the label. Errors say how to fix: "Enter a price above zero."

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<CurrencyInput
  label="Price per unit"
  currency="BRL"
  name="price"
  value={priceMinor}
  onChange={setPriceMinor}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The value is integer minor units (the handoff used a `number` in major units), the currency is an ISO code (the handoff took a `"R$"` string), and the format comes from `Intl` (the handoff hard-coded `pt-BR`).
- Negative amounts, `maxDigits`, paste handling, `null`, caret stability, form submission of the integer, description and error, and sizes are new.

components.name: DataTable
components.description:
A data table with locale-aware sorting, row selection with a bulk action bar, client-side
pagination, loading and empty states. Built on React Aria `Table` (a real `<table>` with
grid keyboard navigation): the header cell of a sortable column is a press target with
`aria-sort`, and the selection checkboxes are labelled.

Sorting cycles ascending, descending, none, and is stable: rows that compare equal keep the
order you passed. Strings compare with the active locale (accent- and case-insensitive,
natural number order), numbers numerically. The table never reorders rows on its own;
lists are alphabetical by default in this design system, so pass sorted rows or `defaultSort`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions, in display order.

props.name: rows
props.description:
The rows, in the order you want them shown until the user sorts. Lists are alphabetical by
default in this design system (AGENTS.md rule 5b): sort the rows before passing them, or
pass `defaultSort` for a text column. The table never reorders rows on its own.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Property of a row that holds its unique id. Default `id`. The value is converted to a string.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: `none` (default), `single` or `multiple`. Selecting adds a checkbox column.

props.name: selectedKeys
props.description: Selected row ids (controlled). Selection survives page changes; "select all" applies to the rows of the current page.

props.name: defaultSelectedKeys
props.description: Selected row ids when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Called with the new set of selected row ids.

props.name: bulkActions
props.description: Content of the bulk action bar, shown while rows are selected: usually small `Button`s. `clear` empties the selection.

props.name: sort
props.description: Current sort (controlled). `null` means no sort.

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: Sort applied first when uncontrolled, for example `{ key: 'customer', direction: 'asc' }`.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called when the user changes the sort. Header presses cycle ascending, descending, none.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page; `false` shows all rows without pagination. Default `10`. Pagination appears only when there is more than one page.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, 1-based (controlled).

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: Page shown first when uncontrolled. Default `1`. The page returns to 1 when the sort or the set of rows changes.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Called with the new page.

props.name: onRowAction
props.description: Called when the user activates a row (click, or Enter on the focused row). Adds a pointer cursor and hover style.

props.name: activeKey
props.description: Id of the active row (for example the one open in a side sheet). It gets the raised background and the ink bar.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Replaces the rows with skeleton rows and announces "Loading rows".

props.name: loadingRowCount
props.description: Number of skeleton rows while loading. Default `5`.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content when there are no rows. Default: an `EmptyState` with built-in text.

props.name: reserveBulkBarSpace
props.description:
Keeps the space of the bulk action bar free while nothing is selected, so the table does not
jump down when the first row is selected (fixed positions). Turn off to let the table move
up. Default `true`; only applies when `selectionMode` is not `none`.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Keeps the header visible while the body scrolls. Set `maxHeight` to scroll inside the table; without it the header sticks to the page scroll.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the table area before it scrolls (a number is px, or any CSS length).

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ selectRow: string; selection: string; selectAll: string; selectedCount: (count: number, formatted: string) => string; clearSelection: string; bulkActions: string; loading: string; emptyTitle: string; emptyDescription: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is set.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the table (a visible heading).

keys.description: Accessible name of the checkbox that selects one row. React Aria appends the row name (see `getRowLabel`): "Select row ORD-1001".
Hidden header text of the selection column in `single` mode, where there is no select-all checkbox.

keys.default: Select all rows on this page
keys.description: Accessible name of the header checkbox. It selects the rows on the current page.
Visible and announced selection summary. `formatted` is `count` formatted for the locale.
Button of the bulk action bar that clears the selection.
Accessible name of the bulk action bar.
Announced while the table shows loading rows.
Title of the default empty state.

keys.default: Try another filter or search term.
keys.description: Description of the default empty state.

items.name: Default
items.description: Rows appear in the order given; the table never reorders on its own.

items.name: AlphabeticalByDefault
items.description:
Lists are alphabetical by default (AGENTS.md rule 5b). `defaultSort` applies a locale-aware
sort (accent- and case-insensitive) on first render; the user can still change it.

items.name: Sorting
items.description: Pressing a header cycles ascending, descending, none.

items.name: KeyboardSort
items.description: Tab enters the grid on the first row; Arrow Up reaches the headers; Enter or Space sorts.

items.name: SelectAllOnPage
items.description: The header checkbox selects the rows of the current page; selection survives page changes.

items.name: KeyboardSelection
items.description: Space toggles the focused checkbox.

items.name: Paginated
items.description: Client-side pagination with the `Pagination` component; it returns to page 1 when the sort changes.

items.name: SortSelectPaginate
items.description: Sort, select and paginate in one flow: the selection and the sort survive the page change. TEST-012.

items.name: ClickableRows
items.description: Clickable rows (`onRowAction`) and the active row, for a list that opens a detail panel.

items.name: SelectionAndRowAction
items.description: Selected and clickable rows together: the checkbox selects, the row opens.

items.description: The header stays visible while the body scrolls inside `maxHeight`.

items.description: Long text is truncated with an ellipsis; fixed-width columns keep their size.
