items.description: Text, plurals, numbers and the sort order follow the provider locale.

docs.summary: A table of records with locale-aware sorting, row selection with a bulk action bar, clickable rows, client-side pagination, loading and empty states. Built on React Aria `Table`: a real `<table>` with grid keyboard navigation, `aria-sort` on sortable headers and labelled selection checkboxes.
whenToUse: Lists of records the user scans, sorts and acts on: orders, customers, invoices.
Several columns of comparable data. For one line per record with a menu of actions use `ActionList`.
whenNotToUse: Fewer than three columns, or content that is mostly text: use `ActionList` or a plain list.
Server-side sorting and paging over very large data sets: control `sort` and `page` yourself and pass the page rows with `pageSize={false}` (virtualization is not provided).
Layout: this is a data grid, not a layout table.
keyboard: Grid keyboard model from React Aria: `Tab` enters the table (first row), arrow keys move between cells, rows and the header (Arrow Up from the first row), `Enter` or `Space` on a sortable header sorts, `Space` on a selection checkbox toggles, `Enter` on a row runs `onRowAction`, `Tab` leaves the table.
examples:
<DataTable
  aria-label="Orders"
  rows={orders}
  rowKey="id"
  defaultSort={{ key: 'customer', direction: 'asc' }}
  selectionMode="multiple"
  columns={[
    { key: 'id', label: 'Order', width: '120px', mono: true, muted: true },
    { key: 'customer', label: 'Customer', isRowHeader: true },
    {
      key: 'status',
      label: 'Status',
      width: '120px',
      render: (r) => <Badge tone="success">{r.status}</Badge>,
    },
    {
      key: 'total',
      label: 'Total',
      width: '120px',
      align: 'end',
      mono: true,
      render: (r) => formatCurrency(r.total, 'USD', locale),
    },
  ]}
  bulkActions={(keys, clear) => (
    <Button
      size="sm"
      onPress={() => {
        archive(keys);
        clear();
      }}
    >
      Archive orders
    </Button>
  )}
  onRowAction={(row) => openOrder(row.id)}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Lists of records the user scans, sorts and acts on: orders, customers, invoices.
- Several columns of comparable data. For one line per record with a menu of actions use `ActionList`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Fewer than three columns, or content that is mostly text: use `ActionList` or a plain list.
- Server-side sorting and paging over very large data sets: control `sort` and `page` yourself and pass the page rows with `pageSize={false}` (virtualization is not provided).
- Layout: this is a data grid, not a layout table.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  div[role=group]        bulk action bar (while rows are selected): "N selected", bulkActions, Clear selection
  div.scroll
    table[role=grid]     named by aria-label / aria-labelledby
      thead  th[aria-sort] caption-mono header per column (+ selection checkbox column)
      tbody  tr > td      row height --ds-row-h; active/selected: raised bg + 2px ink bar
  nav                    Pagination (only when there is more than one page)
  span[role=status]      visually hidden live region: "N selected" / "Loading rows"
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                         | Type                                          | Default | Notes                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                                                    | `DataTableColumn<T>[]`                        | -       | `key`, `label`, `width`, `align` (`start`/`end`), `mono`, `muted`, `sortable`, `sortValue`, `render`    |
| `rows`                                                       | `T[]`                                         | -       | Shown in the order given until the user sorts                                                           |
| `rowKey`                                                     | `keyof T`                                     | `id`    | Unique id property; converted to a string                                                               |
| `aria-label`                                                 | `string`                                      | -       | Required (or `aria-labelledby`)                                                                         |
| `selectionMode`                                              | `none \| single \| multiple`                  | `none`  | Adds a checkbox column                                                                                  |
| `selectedKeys` / `defaultSelectedKeys` / `onSelectionChange` | `ReadonlySet<string>`                         |         | Controlled / uncontrolled. Selection survives page changes                                              |
| `bulkActions`                                                | `(keys, clear) => ReactNode`                  |         | Content of the bar shown while rows are selected                                                        |
| `sort` / `defaultSort` / `onSortChange`                      | `{ key, direction: 'asc' \| 'desc' } \| null` | `null`  | Controlled / uncontrolled sort                                                                          |
| `pageSize`                                                   | `number \| false`                             | `10`    | `false` disables pagination                                                                             |
| `page` / `defaultPage` / `onPageChange`                      | `number`                                      | `1`     | Controlled / uncontrolled page                                                                          |
| `onRowAction`                                                | `(row) => void`                               |         | Row click or Enter. Adds hover style and pointer cursor                                                 |
| `activeKey`                                                  | `string`                                      |         | Row open elsewhere (raised background + ink bar)                                                        |
| `isLoading`                                                  | `boolean`                                     | `false` | Skeleton rows (`loadingRowCount`, default 5) and a live "Loading rows"                                  |
| `emptyState`                                                 | `ReactNode`                                   |         | Default: `EmptyState` with built-in text                                                                |
| `reserveBulkBarSpace`                                        | `boolean`                                     | `true`  | Keeps the bulk bar space free so the table does not jump when the first row is selected                 |
| `stickyHeader`, `maxHeight`                                  | `boolean`, `number \| string`                 |         | With `maxHeight` the body scrolls and the header stays; without it the header sticks to the page scroll |
| `messages`                                                   | `Partial<messages>`                           |         | Per-instance text overrides                                                                             |

sections.heading: Sorting
sections.content:
- Pressing a sortable header cycles **ascending, descending, none**. `aria-sort` is `ascending`, `descending` or `none` on the header cell.
- Strings use `compareText` for the active locale: accent- and case-insensitive, natural number order (`Item 2` before `Item 10`). Numbers, booleans and dates compare numerically; numbers come before strings.
- The sort is **stable in both directions**: equal rows keep the order you passed (descending is not a reversed array). Empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `NaN`, invalid dates) always come last.
- Sorting covers all rows, not just the current page; the page returns to 1 when the sort or the set of rows changes (a new array with the same row ids does not reset the page).
- Use `sortValue` when the displayed text differs from the value to sort by, `sortable: false` for columns that are not a property of the row.

### Alphabetical by default

Lists are alphabetical by default in this design system (AGENTS.md rule 5b; exceptions: tasks by urgency, dated records newest first). The table does not reorder rows on its own. Either pass rows already ordered, or set `defaultSort={{ key: 'customer', direction: 'asc' }}` (see the `AlphabeticalByDefault` story).

sections.heading: Selection
sections.content:
- Checkboxes are named "Select row {row header text}" and "Select all rows on this page"; the row header is the column marked `isRowHeader` (default: the first column), so choose the most descriptive one.
- "Select all" applies to the rows on the current page. Selection of other pages is kept. `bulkActions` receives only ids that still exist in `rows`.
- The bulk bar shows "N selected" (plural-aware) and a "Clear selection" button. A visually hidden polite `status` announces the count as it changes.
- `single` mode shows a checkbox per row but no select-all.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Grid keyboard model from React Aria: `Tab` enters the table (first row), arrow keys move between cells, rows and the header (Arrow Up from the first row), `Enter` or `Space` on a sortable header sorts, `Space` on a selection checkbox toggles, `Enter` on a row runs `onRowAction`, `Tab` leaves the table.
- Sortable headers expose `aria-sort`; the sort icon is decorative. Active sorted headers also use a stronger color, never color alone.
- Selection state is `aria-selected` on rows and the checked state of the checkboxes; the count is text.
- While loading the root has `aria-busy`, skeleton rows are not selectable and the first cell of each carries visually hidden "Loading rows".
- Forced colors: selected and active rows keep the bar (system `Highlight`); focus rings are outlines.
- Not provided: `aria-rowcount`/`aria-rowindex` for the rows of other pages (React Aria derives them from the rendered page). Pagination announces the range ("11–20 of 42").

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Column labels in sentence case; CSS applies the uppercase mono caption style.
- Bulk actions are verb + object ("Archive orders"); destructive ones still confirm in a dialog.
- Empty text says what happened and what to do ("No records found. Try another filter or search term.").

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A real `<table>` (React Aria `Table`) instead of a CSS grid of `div`s: proper `rowgroup`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `aria-sort`, `aria-selected`; no `role` override on a button.
- Sorting is locale-aware and stable; cycling ends in "none"; `useMemo` dependencies are complete.
- `defaultSort` takes `{ key, direction }` (was `{ key, dir }`); `onRowClick` is `onRowAction`; `selectable` is `selectionMode`; `align` is `start`/`end` (logical, RTL-safe); `bulkActions` receives a `Set`.
- Selection and sort/page state are controllable; selection persists across pages; the page resets on sort or data change.
- Checkboxes are labelled from messages; selection count is a live region with plural messages.
- Loading (skeleton rows), empty (default `EmptyState`) and sticky header are built in.
- Column visibility, column resizing and virtualization are not included.

alternatives.reason: Fewer than three columns, or content that is mostly text: use `ActionList` or a plain list.

components.name: DatePicker
components.description:
A date field with a calendar popover (React Aria `DatePicker`). The value is a
`YYYY-MM-DD` string (no time zone, so the day never shifts); the typed segments, the
placeholder, month and weekday names and the first day of the week all follow the
`DSProvider` locale. Type the date (arrows or digits per segment) or open the calendar;
"Today" and "Clear" sit under the grid.

The form receives the ISO date under `name`. Range selection is not part of this component.

props.name: value
props.description: The date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (no time zone), or `null` for none. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial date when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new date as `YYYY-MM-DD` once every segment is filled, or `null` from the Clear button. An incomplete date is not reported.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Typing an earlier date makes the field invalid.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: popoverClassName
props.description: Class name for the popover that holds the calendar.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ today: string; clear: string; openCalendar: string; } & { requiredMark: string; } & Partial<{ previousMonth: string; nextMonth: string; }>>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `today`, `clear`, `openCalendar`, `previousMonth`, `nextMonth`, `requiredMark`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

keys.description: Footer button that picks today's date.
Footer button that empties the field.
Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.

items.name: Open
items.description: The calendar open under the field, for the visual review (TEST-020).

items.name: PickDate
items.description: Pointer path: open the calendar, click a day, the popover closes and the field shows the date. TEST-012.

docs.summary: `DatePicker` is a date field (typed segments) with a calendar popover and "Today" / "Clear" buttons. `Calendar` is the standalone month grid. Built on React Aria `DatePicker`, `DateInput`, `DateSegment`, `Calendar`, `CalendarGrid`, `CalendarCell`, `Popover`. Task: CMP-INP-02.
whenToUse: A single calendar date: delivery, due date, birthday.
`Calendar` alone for inline planners and for composing your own picker.
whenNotToUse: A date range: not supported yet (range picker is P2).
A time of day or a timestamp: the value has no time and no time zone.
Dates years away from now: typing the segments is faster than the grid.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A single calendar date: delivery, due date, birthday.
- `Calendar` alone for inline planners and for composing your own picker.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A date range: not supported yet (range picker is P2).
- A time of day or a timestamp: the value has no time and no time zone.
- Dates years away from now: typing the segments is faster than the grid.

sections.heading: Value contract
sections.content: `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `min` and `max` are **ISO strings `YYYY-MM-DD`** (the `ISODate` type of `src/utils/date`), never `Date`. Conversion to React Aria's `CalendarDate` happens inside the component (`@internationalized/date`, see below), so the day cannot shift with the viewer's time zone. Invalid strings are treated as "no date". `onChange` receives a string only once every segment is filled, or `null` from the Clear button; an incomplete date is not reported. The form receives the ISO string under `name`.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                           | One is required.                                                                                                                |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`                                                                | ISO string or `null`.                                                                                                           |
| `min`, `max`                                                                                         | ISO strings. Outside days are disabled in the grid; typed dates outside are invalid. "Today" is disabled when today is outside. |
| `description`, `errorMessage`, `size`, `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | As in `Select`.                                                                                                                 |
| `messages`                                                                                           | `today`, `clear`, `openCalendar`, `previousMonth`, `nextMonth`, `requiredMark`.                                                 |

`Calendar` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange(iso)`, `min`, `max`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `autoFocus`, `messages`, and requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

sections.heading: Locale
sections.content: Segment order and separators, placeholders (`dd/mm/aaaa`), month names, weekday letters and the first day of the week come from the `DSProvider` locale through React Aria; there are no hard-coded names. Only the button texts are in the message catalog (`Calendar` key for the month buttons, `DatePicker` for the rest).

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key (calendar grid)               | Behavior                                                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrows                            | Previous / next day, previous / next week                     |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`             | Previous / next month                                         |
| `Shift+PageUp` / `Shift+PageDown` | Previous / next year                                          |
| `Home` / `End`                    | First / last day of the **month** (React Aria; APG says week) |
| `Enter` / `Space`                 | Select the focused day                                        |
| `Escape`                          | Close the popover, focus returns to the button                |

In the field: digits fill the segment and move to the next; arrows change a segment's value; `Backspace` clears a segment; `Tab` moves between segments. Each day is named with its full date ("Wednesday, October 28, 2026", "Today, ..."), so the grid is usable without sight. Today has a ring (`--ds-text-3`), the selected day an accent fill with `--ds-text-inverse`; disabled days are dimmed and `aria-disabled`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label with the date's role ("Delivery date"). Errors say how to fix: "Choose a date after today."

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<DatePicker
  label="Delivery date"
  name="delivery"
  min="2026-10-30"
  value={date}
  onChange={setDate}
/>
```

sections.heading: Dependency note
sections.content: The component imports `@internationalized/date`, which React Aria already depends on. It is not a direct dependency of this package yet, so under pnpm's strict layout it must be added to `package.json` (`pnpm add @internationalized/date@^3.12.4`, already in the lockfile as a transitive dependency).

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Typed segments with locale-aware placeholders instead of a button showing a `toLocaleDateString` string; calendar is an ARIA grid with full keyboard navigation (the handoff used plain buttons).
- Month and weekday names come from `Intl` through the locale, not hard-coded Portuguese arrays; the week start follows the locale.
- Day buttons have full-date names; `min` / `max` are enforced for typing too; today is a ring, the footer buttons ("Today", "Clear") come from messages.
- `Date` objects and `T12:00:00` tricks are gone; the value is an ISO string end to end.

components.name: Description
components.description:
Helper text under a field (the handoff `hint`). Linked to the control with
`aria-describedby` by the surrounding React Aria field. It stays visible when an error shows.

items.name: Anatomy
items.description: The building blocks composed by hand inside a React Aria field. Prefer the ready-made fields.

items.name: ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt
items.description:
Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

items.name: RealtimeValidation
items.description: The alternative: `validationBehavior="aria"` reports problems while the user types. Use sparingly.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

components.name: Dialog
components.description:
A modal dialog built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`.

React Aria traps focus, restores it to the trigger on close, locks page scroll, hides the
rest of the page from assistive technology and closes only the top-most layer on `Escape`
(a Dialog opened from a Sheet closes first). Initial focus goes to the dialog itself unless
a child has `autoFocus`; for destructive confirmations use `ConfirmDialog`, which focuses
Cancel.

props.name: title
props.description:
Heading of the dialog and its accessible name. A question for a confirmation ("Delete
order #1048?"), otherwise a noun phrase or a verb plus object ("Edit customer").

props.name: description
props.description:
One or two sentences under the title. It is linked to the dialog with `aria-describedby`,
so screen readers read it right after the title.

props.name: children
props.description: Body of the dialog. A function receives `close`.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Actions, aligned to the end of the footer. Cancel (secondary) before the confirming action;
one primary action at most. A function receives `close`.

props.name: size
props.description: Maximum width: `sm` 420px (default), `md` 540px, `lg` 680px. Narrower on small screens.

props.name: role
props.description:
`dialog` (default), or `alertdialog` for a message that needs an answer before the user
continues, such as a destructive confirmation. `ConfirmDialog` uses `alertdialog`.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
The element that opens the dialog (a `Button`). Optional: omit it and control the dialog
with `isOpen`. Focus returns to the element that was focused when the dialog opened.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog opens or closes.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Whether pressing the overlay closes the dialog. Default `true`; `ConfirmDialog` sets `false`.

props.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
props.description: Disables closing with `Escape`. Use it only while a request is running.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the dialog panel.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the dialog panel.

keys.description: Label of the button that dismisses a `ConfirmDialog` without doing anything.

items.name: Default
items.description: Initial focus is on Cancel, so Enter right after opening cancels instead of deleting.

items.name: ConfirmFlow
items.description:
The whole destructive flow with a pointer: opening lands focus on Cancel (not on the red
button), and the focus ring is part of the visual baseline. TEST-012.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: Neutral
items.description: A non-destructive confirmation: primary button, focus on the action.

items.name: Default
items.description: The keyboard contract: open, focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, focus returns.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: InsideSheet
items.description: A Dialog opened from a Sheet. Escape closes the Dialog first and leaves the Sheet open.

docs.summary:
A modal dialog, and `ConfirmDialog` for destructive confirmations. Built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `ModalOverlay`, `Modal` and `Dialog`.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Dialog` (CMP-FBK-03). Overlay management: ARCH-005.
whenToUse: A short task or decision that blocks the page: edit a record in a small form, confirm a deletion.
`ConfirmDialog`: every deletion. "Deleting always asks for confirmation" (AGENTS.md section 5).
whenNotToUse: Reversible actions (mark, link, change status): do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`. Do not confirm.
Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
A message about the page: use `Alert`.
Nesting dialogs more than two deep.
keyboard: `Escape` closes **only the top-most layer**. A `Dialog` opened from a `Sheet` closes first and the Sheet stays (tested). Every overlay uses React Aria's shared layer stack instead of its own window listener (ARCH-005).
examples:
<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  title="Delete order #1048?"
  description="The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete order"
  onConfirm={() => deleteOrder(1048)}
/>

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit customer</Button>}
  title="Edit customer"
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save customer</Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Name" autoFocus />
</Dialog>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A short task or decision that blocks the page: edit a record in a small form, confirm a deletion.
- `ConfirmDialog`: every deletion. "Deleting always asks for confirmation" (AGENTS.md section 5).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Reversible actions (mark, link, change status): do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`. Do not confirm.
- Viewing or editing a record next to its list: use `Sheet`.
- Interactive content anchored to a control: use `Popover`.
- A message about the page: use `Alert`.
- Nesting dialogs more than two deep.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
DialogTrigger
  trigger            Button                                (optional when controlled)
  ModalOverlay       --ds-overlay, z dialog
    Modal            raised surface, strong line, radius lg, dialog shadow, width sm | md | lg
      Dialog         role=dialog | alertdialog, aria-labelledby = title, aria-describedby = description
        header       h2 title (17/24, 600) · description (14/22, text-2)
        body         scrolls
        footer       actions aligned to the end; divider when there is a body
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`Dialog`

| Prop                                      | Type                                    | Default  | Notes                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                   | `ReactNode` (required)                  | none     | Heading and accessible name.                            |
| `description`                             | `ReactNode`                             |          | Linked with `aria-describedby`.                         |
| `children`                                | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |          | Body.                                                   |
| `footer`                                  | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |          | Actions.                                                |
| `size`                                    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                  | `sm`     | Max width 420 / 540 / 680 px (`--ds-dialog-width-*`).   |
| `role`                                    | `'dialog' \| 'alertdialog'`             | `dialog` |                                                         |
| `trigger`                                 | `ReactElement`                          |          | Optional when controlled.                               |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                         |          | Controlled / uncontrolled open state.                   |
| `isDismissable`                           | `boolean`                               | `true`   | Press on the overlay closes it.                         |
| `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`               | `boolean`                               | `false`  | Disables `Escape`; use only while a request is running. |

`ConfirmDialog` adds: `confirmLabel` (required, names the action), `onConfirm` (required), `tone` (`danger` | `neutral`), `initialFocus` (`cancel` | `confirm`, default `cancel`), `closeOnConfirm`, `isPending`, `messages` (`cancel`). `description` is required: it is the consequence. `isDismissable` defaults to `false`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Focus is **trapped** while open, **restored** to the element that opened it, the page behind is `inert`/`aria-hidden` and does not scroll (all React Aria).
- **Initial focus.** Plain `Dialog`: the dialog itself, or the child with `autoFocus` (put it on the first field). `ConfirmDialog`: **Cancel**, so pressing Enter or Space as soon as it opens never confirms. The handoff focused nothing.
- `Escape` closes **only the top-most layer**. A `Dialog` opened from a `Sheet` closes first and the Sheet stays (tested). Every overlay uses React Aria's shared layer stack instead of its own window listener (ARCH-005).
- Named by the title (`aria-labelledby`, from the `h2`) and described by the description (`aria-describedby`; not linked in the handoff).
- `ConfirmDialog` uses `alertdialog`, which screen readers announce with its description. A press outside does not dismiss it.
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade and 8 px rise are removed. Forced colors: border in `CanvasText`.
- 320 px reflow: the dialog shrinks to the viewport less the 24 px gutter and the body scrolls.

### Layers

Overlays are portaled to `body`, each with its own layer: sheet (40) < dialog (45) < dropdown (50) < popover (55) < toast (58) < tooltip (60). A `Select`, `Menu`, `Popover` or `Combobox` opened from inside a Dialog or Sheet therefore renders **above** it. This is safe because a modal blocks page-level popovers while it is open. Tests assert the order.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: a question for confirmations that names the object ("Delete order #1048?"), otherwise verb plus object or a noun phrase ("Edit customer"). Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
- Description: the consequence in one sentence ("The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone.").
- Buttons: Cancel (secondary) then the action, verb plus object ("Save customer", "Delete order"). Never "OK" or "Yes". One primary action.
- After a confirmed delete show a `Toast` with **Undo** when the data can come back.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<ConfirmDialog
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  title="Delete order #1048?"
  description="The order and its 14 lines will be removed. This can't be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete order"
  onConfirm={() => deleteOrder(1048)}
/>

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit customer</Button>}
  title="Edit customer"
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save customer</Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Name" autoFocus />
</Dialog>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Focus trap, restore, initial focus, scroll lock and inert background from React Aria; the handoff had none.
- `aria-labelledby` and a linked `aria-describedby` instead of `aria-label={title}`.
- No window-level `Escape` listener per dialog; stack-aware.
- `width` (420 / 440) became `size` (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) with component tokens; `contained` mode is not ported (a story frame hosts open dialogs in the docs).
- New: `ConfirmDialog` implementing the destructive-confirmation principle, controlled and uncontrolled state, messages (English and pt-BR).

components.name: Divider
components.description:
A 1px line that separates groups of content, built on React Aria `Separator`
(`<hr>`, or `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` when vertical). Prefer spacing to
separate related things; use a divider where the content changes topic.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (default) separates stacked content; `vertical` separates items in a row and needs a parent with a height.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Line weight by token: `subtle` (`--ds-line-subtle`, internal dividers), `default`
(`--ds-line`, between cards and sections) or `strong` (`--ds-line-strong`, around controls
and overlays). Default `default`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the separator element.

items.name: Vertical
items.description: A vertical divider stretches to the height of a row.

items.name: Weights
items.description: All three weights together, to compare.

docs.summary: A 1px line that separates groups of content. Built on React Aria `Separator`.
whenToUse: Between sections of a panel or a menu-like list where the topic changes.
Vertically, between inline groups in a toolbar.
whenNotToUse: To separate closely related items: use spacing.
Around every field or row: borders-first hierarchy comes from surfaces, not a line between everything.
To wrap a Card in a Card: use a divider inside one card instead.
examples:
<Stack gap={4}>
  <Section />
  <Divider />
  <Section />
</Stack>

<Inline>
  <Button>Bold</Button>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <Button>Link</Button>
</Inline>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Between sections of a panel or a menu-like list where the topic changes.
- Vertically, between inline groups in a toolbar.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To separate closely related items: use spacing.
- Around every field or row: borders-first hierarchy comes from surfaces, not a line between everything.
- To wrap a Card in a Card: use a divider inside one card instead.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
hr (1px line)          horizontal
div[role=separator]    vertical, with aria-orientation
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop          | Type                                | Default        | Notes                                                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`        | `'horizontal'` | Vertical needs a parent with a height (it stretches in a flex row)               |
| `variant`     | `'subtle' \| 'default' \| 'strong'` | `'default'`    | `--ds-line-subtle` (internal), `--ds-line` (cards, sections), `--ds-line-strong` |

React Aria separator props (`aria-label`, …) and `ref` pass through.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Rendered by React Aria: a horizontal divider is an `<hr>`; a vertical one has `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="vertical"`.
- It is a thematic break for assistive technology, so do not use it as a pure visual rule between unrelated things.
- Line colors are borders, not text; `forced-colors` paints them with `CanvasText`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Stack gap={4}>
  <Section />
  <Divider />
  <Section />
</Stack>

<Inline>
  <Button>Bold</Button>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" />
  <Button>Link</Button>
</Inline>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff drew dividers with `border-top` on a wrapper; this is a real separator with three line weights from tokens.

components.name: DonutMeter
components.description:
A circular meter for one proportion: how much of a whole is used, done or filled (storage
used, goal reached, stock level). The percentage is printed in the center, formatted with
`Intl` for the active locale. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"` with
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`).

It needs an accessible name: a visible `label` (printed under the ring), `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`. For a task that makes progress use `Progress`; for a bar use `Meter`;
for one proportion among several use `ProportionBar`.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Color of the ring: `accent` (default), `neutral`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`. Color
is never the only signal: the percentage is printed in the center and the label says what
it is.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter token: `sm` 48px, `md` 72px (default), `lg` 96px.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Prints the percentage in the center. On by default. Turn it off when the center is empty on purpose.

props.name: centerLabel
props.description:
Replaces the percentage in the center ("12" over "days"). Visual only: screen readers get
`valueLabel` (or the percentage) as the value of the meter.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the meter element.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

docs.summary:
A circular meter for one proportion: how much of a whole is used, done or filled (storage used, goal reached, stock level). The percentage is printed in the center, formatted with `Intl` for the active locale. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"`). It is a separate component from `Progress`/`Meter`, in its own folder, and does not change them.

- TODO `GAP-007`.
whenToUse: One share of a known total, as a compact visual in a card or a table cell.
When the center number is the main message and the ring supports it.
whenNotToUse: Progress of a task that is running: use `Progress`.
A bar in a column or a row: use `Meter` (`Progress` module).
Several parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
A trend over time: use `Sparkline` or `Chart`.
examples:
<DonutMeter label="Storage used" value={62} />

<DonutMeter
  label="Storage"
  value={6.2}
  maxValue={10}
  valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"
  tone="warning"
  size="lg"
/>

<DonutMeter aria-label="Trial" value={40} centerLabel="12 d" valueLabel="12 days left" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- One share of a known total, as a compact visual in a card or a table cell.
- When the center number is the main message and the ring supports it.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Progress of a task that is running: use `Progress`.
- A bar in a column or a row: use `Meter` (`Progress` module).
- Several parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- A trend over time: use `Sparkline` or `Chart`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=meter] aria-valuenow/min/max/valuetext
  div.ring
    svg[aria-hidden]   (track circle + filled circle)
    span.center        (percentage or centerLabel)
  label                (optional, under the ring)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                    | Type                                                          | Default     | Notes                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                 | `number`                                                      | `0`         | Within `minValue` and `maxValue`; clamped.                                                |
| `minValue` / `maxValue` | `number`                                                      | `0` / `100` |                                                                                           |
| `label`                 | `ReactNode`                                                   | none        | Visible name under the ring. One of `label`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` is required. |
| `valueLabel`            | `string`                                                      | percentage  | What screen readers hear ("6.2 of 10 GB"). The center still shows the percentage.         |
| `tone`                  | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'accent'`  | Color of the ring. Never the only signal.                                                 |
| `size`                  | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                        | `'md'`      | Diameter 48 / 72 / 96px (`--ds-donut-meter-size-*`).                                      |
| `showValue`             | `boolean`                                                     | `true`      | Prints the percentage in the center.                                                      |
| `centerLabel`           | `ReactNode`                                                   | none        | Replaces the percentage in the center (visual only; pair with `valueLabel`).              |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` from React Aria. An accessible name is required (types and a development warning). The drawing is hidden from assistive technology; the center text is covered by `aria-valuetext`.
- Color is never the only signal: the percentage is printed in the center. The ring and track keep 3:1 against the surface in every tone.
- Motion: the ring animates 300ms; none under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Forced colors: track `GrayText`, ring `CanvasText`.
- Not interactive and not focusable.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Label: what is measured, in sentence case ("Storage used"). The unit and total belong in `valueLabel` ("6.2 of 10 GB").
- Pair a tone change with text that says why ("Almost full").

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<DonutMeter label="Storage used" value={62} />

<DonutMeter
  label="Storage"
  value={6.2}
  maxValue={10}
  valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"
  tone="warning"
  size="lg"
/>

<DonutMeter aria-label="Trial" value={40} centerLabel="12 d" valueLabel="12 days left" />
```

components.name: Drawer
components.description:
A non-modal side panel for filters, inspectors and secondary navigation. It sits next to the
content in the page flow: there is no scrim, the page stays interactive, focus is not trapped
and the page is not made inert. Place it as a sibling of the main content inside a flex or grid
container; it renders nothing while closed.

Use `Sheet` instead when the panel is a task that must be finished or dismissed first
(editing one record): that one is modal.

`Escape` closes the drawer while focus is inside it and returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the drawer and its accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: Body of the drawer; it scrolls when it is taller than the drawer. A function receives `close`.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer actions, aligned to the end. A function receives `close`.

props.name: placement
props.description: Edge the drawer sits against: `end` (default) or `start`. Both follow the writing direction.

props.name: size
props.description: Width: `sm` 280px, `md` 320px (default), `lg` 400px. It never exceeds its container.

props.name: padded
props.description: Pads the body. Turn it off for a table or a full-bleed list. Default `true`.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer opens or closes through the user (close button or `Escape`).

props.name: autoFocus
props.description:
Moves focus into the drawer when it opens after the first render. A drawer that is open on
first render never takes focus. Default `true`; turn it off for a panel that should stay
beside the page without interrupting what the user is doing.

props.name: role
props.description:
Landmark role. `complementary` (default) for content that supports the page (filters,
inspectors); `region` for a section the user may want to find in the landmark list.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Level of the title heading. Default `2`.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the drawer panel.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the drawer panel.

keys.description: Name of the close button in the Drawer header.

docs.summary: A non-modal side panel that sits next to the content, for filters, inspectors and secondary navigation. There is no scrim, the page stays interactive and focus is not trapped. Generic: it lives in the core entry point.
whenNotToUse: A short confirmation or form: `Dialog`.
A few controls anchored to a button: `Popover`.
Top-level navigation: `Sidebar`.
keyboard: `Escape` closes the drawer when focus is inside it (and when no inner overlay handled it) and focus returns to the element that had it before the drawer opened, normally the trigger. Closing from the close button does the same.

sections.heading: Drawer or Sheet
sections.content:
|          | Drawer                                                                   | Sheet                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Modality | Non-modal: page stays usable                                             | Modal: page is `inert`, scroll locked                      |
| Layout   | In the page flow, beside the content                                     | Overlay above the page, with a scrim                       |
| Focus    | Not trapped; Tab leaves the drawer                                       | Trapped and restored                                       |
| Use for  | Filters, inspector for the current selection, secondary navigation, help | Viewing or editing one record, a task to finish or dismiss |

Rule of thumb: if the user should keep working in the page while the panel is open, use a `Drawer`. If the panel is a task that needs a decision before going back, use a `Sheet`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A short confirmation or form: `Dialog`.
- A few controls anchored to a button: `Popover`.
- Top-level navigation: `Sidebar`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
aside (role complementary | region, aria-labelledby = title)
  header     --ds-topbar-h tall: heading + close IconButton
  body       scrolls; padded or not
  footer     optional, end-aligned actions
```

Place the drawer as a sibling of the main content in a flex or grid container. It renders nothing while closed and does not animate out.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                      | Type                                    | Default         | Notes                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                   | `ReactNode` (required)                  | none            | Heading and accessible name.                                                        |
| `children` / `footer`                     | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |                 | Body and end-aligned actions.                                                       |
| `placement`                               | `'start' \| 'end'`                      | `end`           | Edge it sits against; follows the writing direction.                                |
| `size`                                    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                  | `md`            | 280 / 320 / 400 px (`--ds-drawer-width-*`).                                         |
| `padded`                                  | `boolean`                               | `true`          | Off for a table or list.                                                            |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                         | closed          | Controlled / uncontrolled. `onOpenChange` fires for user closes (button, `Escape`). |
| `autoFocus`                               | `boolean`                               | `true`          | Moves focus to the panel when it opens after first render.                          |
| `role`                                    | `'complementary' \| 'region'`           | `complementary` | Landmark role.                                                                      |
| `headingLevel`                            | `1`-`6`                                 | `2`             | Level of the title.                                                                 |
| `messages`                                | `{ close }`                             |                 | "Close panel" (pt-BR "Fechar painel").                                              |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A named landmark (`complementary` by default, `region` on request) labelled by its title.
- Not modal: nothing is hidden from assistive technology and Tab moves freely between the drawer and the page.
- When the drawer opens after first render, focus moves to the panel (it is programmatically focusable, `tabIndex=-1`), so the next Tab reaches its first control. A drawer that is open on first render never takes focus; set `autoFocus={false}` to keep focus where it is.
- `Escape` closes the drawer when focus is inside it (and when no inner overlay handled it) and focus returns to the element that had it before the drawer opened, normally the trigger. Closing from the close button does the same.
- If the consumer closes a controlled drawer from outside (for example a toolbar toggle), focus is left where the user put it.
- Slide-in is a short fade plus 16 px move (`--ds-drawer-shift`); it is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion` and mirrors in right-to-left layouts (`:dir(rtl)`). Borders and padding use logical properties.
- The width is capped by its container (`max-inline-size: 100%`), so on narrow containers it fills the width instead of overflowing.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: the purpose in sentence case ("Filters", "Order details").
- Footer buttons are verb plus object ("Apply filters", "Clear filters"). Use one primary action.

Differences from the handoff
sections.content: New component (GAP-006): the handoff only has the modal `Sheet`.

components.name: DueIndicator
components.description:
A due date with a status in words: "Mar 9  Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due in 5 days",
"Paid". A dot and the text color follow the tone (`danger` overdue, `warning` within a week,
`neutral` later, `success` paid), but the status is always text, never color alone.

The urgency comes from `dueStatus`, the wording from messages and `Intl` (`formatRelativeDays`),
the date from `formatDate`. Day arithmetic is calendar-based, so daylight-saving changes never
shift the count.

props.name: date
props.description: The due date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (`ISODate`). Invalid values throw in development.

props.name: today
props.description:
The current day as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to the user's local day at render time. Pass it
to make output deterministic (tests, stories, server rendering with a known day).

props.name: paid
props.description: The item is settled: shows "Paid" in the success tone, whatever the date.

props.name: showDate
props.description: Shows the formatted date before the status. Default `true`.

props.name: dateStyle
props.description: Format of the date (`formatDate` styles). Default `monthDay` ("Mar 9").

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ overdue: (days: number) => string; due: (relative: string) => string; paid: string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

keys.description: Status of a date in the past. `days` is a positive whole number.

Status of a date today or later. `relative` is the locale's relative time from
`formatRelativeDays` ("today", "tomorrow", "in 3 days").
Status of a settled item: the due date no longer matters.

items.name: AcrossDaylightSaving
items.description: Calendar-day arithmetic: the daylight-saving change does not shift the count.

docs.summary:
A due date with a status in words and a tone dot: "Mar 9 Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due in 5 days", "Paid". Color reinforces the status; the text always states it.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/DueIndicator.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-07`).
whenToUse: A deadline in a list row, a card or a detail header (invoice due, task due, renewal).
When urgency should be readable at a glance without relying on color.
whenNotToUse: A timestamp of something that already happened: format it with `formatDate` / `formatRelativeDays`.
A workflow status that is not date-driven: use `Badge`.
examples:
<DueIndicator date={invoice.dueISO} paid={invoice.paid} />

// Deterministic output
<DueIndicator date="2026-03-14" today="2026-03-10" dateStyle="long" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A deadline in a list row, a card or a detail header (invoice due, task due, renewal).
- When urgency should be readable at a glance without relying on color.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A timestamp of something that already happened: format it with `formatDate` / `formatRelativeDays`.
- A workflow status that is not date-driven: use `Badge`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span[data-tone=danger|warning|neutral|success]
  span.dot          (aria-hidden)
  time[datetime]    formatDate(date, locale, dateStyle)     (showDate)
  span.status       "Overdue by 3 days" | "Due today" | "Due in 5 days" | "Paid"
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                     | Default       | Notes                                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `date`      | `ISODate`                | required      | `YYYY-MM-DD`. Malformed values throw in development. |
| `today`     | `ISODate`                | local day now | Inject for tests, stories and deterministic output.  |
| `paid`      | `boolean`                | `false`       | Shows "Paid" in the success tone, ignoring the date. |
| `showDate`  | `boolean`                | `true`        | Shows the formatted date before the status.          |
| `dateStyle` | `DateStyle`              | `'monthDay'`  | Any `formatDate` style.                              |
| `messages`  | `{ overdue, due, paid }` | none          | Overrides the texts for this instance.               |

Tone comes from `dueStatus`: overdue is `danger`, 0 to 7 days `warning`, later `neutral`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The status is text (`Overdue by 3 days`), so color is never the only signal; the dot is `aria-hidden`.
- The date is a `<time datetime>` element.
- Contrast: the status uses `--ds-danger`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-success` or `--ds-text-2` on the page background, all above 4.5:1.
- Forced colors: the dot and the text fall back to `CanvasText`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- "Overdue by 3 days", "Due today", "Due tomorrow", "Due in 5 days", "Paid". Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
- Dates and relative wording come from `Intl` for the active locale; never build them by hand.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<DueIndicator date={invoice.dueISO} paid={invoice.paid} />

// Deterministic output
<DueIndicator date="2026-03-14" today="2026-03-10" dateStyle="long" />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `dueInfo` left the component: urgency is the tested `dueStatus` utility and day arithmetic is `daysBetween` (UTC calendar math, no `T12:00:00` trick), so daylight-saving changes never shift the count. Component tests cover US and EU transitions and a leap day.
- Month names are no longer a table: dates come from `formatDate`; wording and plurals come from messages (`en`, `pt-BR`) and `formatRelativeDays`.
- Texts are English by default ("Overdue by 3 days"), not hard-coded Portuguese; `paidText` is now the `paid` message.
- `today` stays injectable; the default is the local day of the system clock. Colors and sizes are tokens.

alternatives.reason: A workflow status that is not date-driven: use `Badge`.

components.name: EmptyState
components.description:
Tells the user that there is nothing to show, why, and what to do next. The copy follows
"what happened + what to do".

props.name: title
props.description:
What happened, in one short sentence: "No orders found". Rendered as a heading
(see `headingLevel`).

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`.

props.name: description
props.description: What the user can do about it: "Try another filter or search term."

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon above the title. Decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology. No illustrations.

props.name: action
props.description: The primary action, usually a `Button`. Rendered after the secondary action.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.description: A second, lower-emphasis action.

props.name: compact
props.description: Less padding and a smaller title, for use inside a card, a panel or a table.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Dashed border. Set to `false` when the empty state already sits inside a bordered container. Default `true`.

docs.summary: A typographic placeholder for a list, table or panel that has nothing to show. It says what happened and what the user can do about it.
whenToUse: A list, table or search has no results.
A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.
whenNotToUse: While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.
examples:
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A list, table or search has no results.
- A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
- For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root (dashed border, centered)
  span[aria-hidden]  icon (optional)
  h{headingLevel}    title
  p                  description (optional)
  div                secondaryAction, action
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop              | Type                         | Default | Notes                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`           | `ReactNode`                  | -       | What happened. Rendered as a heading                               |
| `headingLevel`    | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2`     | Match the page outline (inside a `Card` titled with `h2`, use `3`) |
| `description`     | `ReactNode`                  |         | What to do next. Max width 360 px                                  |
| `icon`            | `ReactNode`                  |         | Optional, decorative. No illustrations                             |
| `action`          | `ReactNode`                  |         | Primary action (usually `Button`)                                  |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode`                  |         | Lower emphasis; shown before the primary action                    |
| `compact`         | `boolean`                    | `false` | Less padding, smaller title. For cards, panels, table bodies       |
| `bordered`        | `boolean`                    | `true`  | Dashed border. Turn off inside an already bordered container       |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Copy: what happened + what to do
sections.content:
Title: say what is missing, in sentence case, without apologies or exclamation marks. Description: tell the user the next step, in one sentence.

| Situation        | Title             | Description                                              | Action        |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Filtered to zero | No orders found   | Try another filter or search term.                       | Clear filters |
| First use        | No orders yet     | Orders created here or in the store appear in this list. | Create order  |
| Cleared inbox    | Nothing to review | New approvals appear here as they arrive.                | (none)        |

Avoid "Oops", "Sorry", blame ("You have no orders") and filler ("There is nothing to show here at the moment").

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The title is a real heading: choose `headingLevel` so the outline stays sequential. The heading lets screen reader users find the empty region by navigating headings.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the text carries the meaning.
- The component does not announce itself. If the empty state replaces content after a user action (for example a search), announce the result count in your own live region.
- Actions are ordinary buttons or links with their own names; order in the DOM is secondary then primary, matching the visual order.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The title is a heading (`<h2>` by default) instead of a `span`; the level is configurable.
- Optional decorative `icon` slot (no illustrations, per the visual foundations).
- The handoff Portuguese sample copy is gone; the guidance above replaces it.
- Padding, description width and the compact padding are component tokens (`--ds-empty-state-*`). No `style` prop.

alternatives.name: Skeleton
alternatives.reason: While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
