alternatives.reason: When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.

components.name: FieldError
components.description:
Error text of a field. Renders only while the field is invalid and the error is *displayed*:
with the default `validationBehavior="native"` that is after a submit attempt (see Field.md).
The message sits in a `role="alert"` element so it is announced when it appears; on submit focus also
moves to the first invalid field, which reads it again through `aria-describedby`.

props.name: children
props.description:
The message. A function receives the validation result and decides everything. A static
message replaces only the browser's own constraint text; an error the app supplied (a
`validate` rule, or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead of it. Without
children, the validation errors are shown (the browser's message for native constraints).

items.name: Anatomy
items.description: The building blocks composed by hand inside a React Aria field. Prefer the ready-made fields.

items.name: ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt
items.description:
Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

items.name: RealtimeValidation
items.description: The alternative: `validationBehavior="aria"` reports problems while the user types. Use sparingly.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

components.name: FieldSet
components.description:
Groups related fields under a caption: a real `fieldset` with a `legend`, an optional
description, and disabled propagation. Use it for a set of fields that answer one question
(an address, notification channels), not for every section of a form.

props.name: legend
props.description:
Caption of the group, required. It is the `legend`: screen readers announce it before each
field in the group ("Billing address, Street"). Write it in sentence case; CSS makes it a
mono caption.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional help for the whole group, linked to the fieldset with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description:
Disables every native control inside (inputs, selects, textareas, buttons), the way
`<fieldset disabled>` does: they cannot be focused or submitted and dim together.
Controls that are not native elements (menus, custom widgets) are not affected: disable
those individually.

items.name: Disabled
items.description: Every native control inside is disabled together.

docs.summary: A group of related fields under a caption: a real `fieldset` with a `legend`, an optional description and disabled propagation.
whenToUse: A set of fields that answer one question: an address, a date range, notification channels.
A group that should be disabled together.
whenNotToUse: For every section of a form: a heading is enough to organize a long form.
For a single `RadioGroup` or `CheckboxGroup`: they already render a labelled group.
examples:
<FieldSet legend="Billing address" description="Shown on every invoice.">
  <Input label="Street" name="street" />
  <Input label="City" name="city" />
</FieldSet>

<FieldSet legend="Shipping address" isDisabled>…</FieldSet>

sections.content:
- A set of fields that answer one question: an address, a date range, notification channels.
- A group that should be disabled together.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For every section of a form: a heading is enough to organize a long form.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
fieldset
  legend        mono caption, uppercase by CSS
  p             description (optional)
  div           the fields, stacked with --ds-field-set-gap
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop          | Type        | Default | Notes                                                                     |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `legend`      | `ReactNode` | —       | Required. The group's accessible name                                     |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |         | Linked with `aria-describedby`; a consumer `aria-describedby` is kept     |
| `isDisabled`  | `boolean`   | `false` | `fieldset disabled`: native controls inside are disabled and dim together |

Other `fieldset` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A `fieldset` + `legend` is announced as a named group; screen readers read the legend before each field ("Billing address, Street").
- `isDisabled` uses the native attribute, so inputs, selects, textareas and buttons inside cannot be focused or submitted, and are skipped by constraint validation. Controls that are not native elements (menus, custom widgets) are **not** affected: disable those yourself.
- The legend uses `--ds-text-2` (the faint `--ds-text-3` is too low-contrast for a name).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Legends are short nouns in sentence case ("Billing address"); CSS uppercases them. Descriptions say what the group is for, not how to fill each field.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<FieldSet legend="Billing address" description="Shown on every invoice.">
  <Input label="Street" name="street" />
  <Input label="City" name="city" />
</FieldSet>

<FieldSet legend="Shipping address" isDisabled>…</FieldSet>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff had no group component; fields were laid out in plain divs. FieldSet adds the group semantics and shared disabling.

components.name: FileUpload
components.description:
A drop zone with a "Choose files" button and the list of added files (React Aria `DropZone`
and `FileTrigger`). Dragging is a pointer shortcut; the button is the keyboard and click way
in. Files are validated (type, size, count) as they arrive and the errors are shown under the
zone; added, removed and rejected files are announced politely. The component keeps no upload
state: pass `progress` to show a bar per file.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the drop zone, for the rules: "PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB". Linked to the zone.

props.name: accept
props.description:
Accepted types: MIME types (`image/png`), wildcards (`image/*`) or extensions (`.pdf`).
Files of other types are rejected with an error message. Also filters the file dialog.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Largest file in bytes. Larger files are rejected with an error message.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description:
Most files in the list. `1` switches to single-file mode: choosing or dropping a file
replaces the current one. Default: no limit.

props.name: value
props.description: The files, when controlled. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial files when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the full list after files are added or removed.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Called with the files that were not added and why (wrong type, too large, too many).

props.name: progress
props.description:
Upload progress per file, 0 to 100, supplied by you (the component uploads nothing and
never invents progress). A file with a value under 100 shows a progress bar; 100 shows
"Done"; a file without an entry shows only its size.

props.name: name
props.description:
Name for form submission: the selected files are submitted as `File` entries under this name
(multiple entries when several files).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables choosing, dropping and removing.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the root.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ dropZone: string; dropLabel: (multiple: boolean) => string; choose: (multiple: boolean) => string; listLabel: string; remove: (name: string) => string; uploading: (name: string) => string; ... 9 more ...; removed: (name: string) => string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

keys.description: Accessible name of the drop target itself (React Aria adds a keyboard stop on it that accepts pasted files).
Text of the drop target, which names it for assistive technology.
The button that opens the file dialog (the keyboard and click alternative to dragging).
Accessible name of the list of added files.
Accessible name of the remove button of a file.
Accessible name of the progress bar of a file that is uploading.
Status text of a file whose progress reached 100.
Size units shown after the number.

keys.default: "{name}" is not an accepted file type.
keys.description: Error: the file type is not accepted.
Error: the file is larger than the limit (already formatted, e.g. "10 MB").

keys.default: Only 2 files can be added. 2 not added.

Live announcement after files were added.

docs.summary: A drop zone with a "Choose files" button and the list of added files. Built on React Aria `DropZone` and `FileTrigger`; progress bars use [Progress](../Progress/Progress.md). The component validates and lists files; it uploads nothing. Task: CMP-INP-03.
whenToUse: Attaching one or several files to a record or form.
whenNotToUse: Image galleries, cropping or previews: a product pattern.
A hidden uploader inside a button: use `FileTrigger` from React Aria directly.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Attaching one or several files to a record or form.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Image galleries, cropping or previews: a product pattern.
- A hidden uploader inside a button: use `FileTrigger` from React Aria directly.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`   | One is required. The root is a `group` named by it.                                                                                                         |
| `description`                                | The rules in words ("PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB"), linked to the zone.                                                                                     |
| `accept`                                     | MIME types, wildcards (`image/*`) or extensions (`.pdf`). Also filters the file dialog.                                                                     |
| `maxSize`                                    | Bytes. Larger files are rejected.                                                                                                                           |
| `maxFiles`                                   | Count. `1` is single-file mode: a new file replaces the current one.                                                                                        |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(files)` | The full `File[]` after every add or remove.                                                                                                                |
| `onReject(rejections)`                       | `{ file, reason: 'type' \| 'size' \| 'count' }[]` for files not added.                                                                                      |
| `progress`                                   | `Map<File, number>` (0 to 100), yours. Under 100 shows a bar, 100 shows "Done", no entry shows only the size.                                               |
| `name`                                       | Submits the files with the form (`FormData.getAll(name)` returns `File`s) through a hidden file input.                                                      |
| `isDisabled`, `className`, `ref`, `messages` | `messages`: `dropZone`, `dropLabel`, `choose`, `listLabel`, `remove`, `uploading`, `done`, `unit*`, `wrongType`, `tooLarge`, `tooMany`, `added`, `removed`. |

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- Errors are listed under the zone and replaced on the next add or removal. Sizes are formatted with `formatNumber` for the locale and unit messages (`1.5 MB`, pt-BR `1,5 MB`; steps of 1024).
- Polite live region (`role="status"`) announces "2 files added" (with the error texts), "Removed name.pdf". Pluralized per locale.
- Each file row: name (truncated), size or "Done · size", and a ghost button "Remove {name}".
- `progress` is never simulated by the component. The handoff's random progress exists only in the "WithProgress" story, driven by a timer.

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                         | Behavior                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                       | Zone (React Aria's own stop: `Ctrl/Cmd+V` pastes files there), Choose button, Remove buttons |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Choose | Opens the file dialog: the keyboard and click alternative to dragging                        |
| `Enter` / `Space` on Remove | Removes the file                                                                             |

Dragging is only a pointer shortcut; nothing depends on it. While files are dragged over it the zone gets an accent border and soft fill (also an outline in forced colors). The list is a `ul` named "Added files".

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: `description` states the limits in one sentence. Error texts name the file and the limit and are produced from messages ("\"big.pdf\" is larger than 1 MB.").

sections.heading: Example
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Real validation (type, size, count) with messages, a keyboard-operable button instead of a `div role="button"`, live announcements, controlled value, form submission, and consumer-supplied progress.
- Sizes and messages come from `Intl` and the catalog (the handoff hard-coded pt-BR and a comma).

sections.heading: Manual verification
sections.content:
Dropping files is automated: `FileUpload.test.tsx` performs a native drag of real files through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`commands.dropFiles`, defined in `tests/browser-commands`), because React Aria rejects synthetic `DragEvent`s. Pasting is not automatable, so check it by hand before a release that touches this component (TEST-017):

1. Copy a file in the operating system file manager (Explorer, Finder), or copy an image.
2. Tab to the drop zone (the first stop, named "Drop zone") so it has focus.
3. Press `Ctrl+V` (`Cmd+V` on macOS). The file should be added to the list and announced ("1 file added.").
4. Repeat with Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Record any browser where the file is not added.

Why it cannot be automated: the paste handler of React Aria reads each item through `webkitGetAsEntry()`, which returns `null` for a synthetic `DataTransfer` and for an image written to the clipboard by a script (verified in Chromium: `kind: file`, `type: image/png`, entry `null`), so the item is skipped. Only a file copied by the operating system can be tested, and no browser API can put one on the clipboard.

components.name: Form
components.description:
A form built on React Aria `Form`: native validation by default, server errors through
`validationErrors`, a vertical rhythm of `--ds-form-gap` between its children, and an
optional error summary. Fields inside inherit the form's `validationBehavior`.

Put exactly one primary action in it, at the end ("Save changes"), and keep submit enabled:
a disabled submit gives no way to learn what is wrong.

props.name: validationBehavior
props.description:
Native validation (default) uses the browser's constraint validation: a failed submit
focuses the first invalid field. `aria` marks fields invalid with ARIA only and never blocks
the submit; use it when the server is the only validator.

props.name: validationErrors
props.description:
Errors from the server, keyed by the field `name`. The matching fields become invalid and
show the message; the first one takes focus (or the summary does, with `errorSummary`).
Clear them (pass `undefined`) when the user edits the field or submits again.

props.name: errorSummary
props.description:
Shows a `FormErrorSummary` at the top of the form. After a failed submit it takes focus and
lists the invalid fields as links. Default `false`. To place the summary elsewhere, leave
this off and render `FormErrorSummary` inside the form yourself.

props.name: children
props.description: The fields and actions of the form.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the `<form>` element.

keys.description: Title of the error summary shown after a failed submit. `count` is the number of invalid fields.

items.name: Default
items.description: A failed submit focuses the first invalid field, which reads its error.

items.name: WithErrorSummary
items.description: The summary takes focus after a failed submit and links to each invalid field by its label.

items.name: ServerErrors
items.description: Errors from the server, keyed by the field name.

items.name: ServerRoundTrip
items.description: Server errors set by a submit handler, the way an app does it.

items.name: WithFieldSets
items.description: FieldSet groups related fields; the form keeps one rhythm between groups and fields.

items.name: AriaValidation
items.description: With aria validation the browser never blocks the submit.

docs.summary: A form built on React Aria `Form`: native validation by default, server errors, a consistent vertical rhythm and an optional error summary.
whenToUse: Any set of fields submitted together: create or edit a record, settings, sign-in.
When you want a failed submit to move focus to the first problem and to list all problems.
whenNotToUse: A single search box or an auto-saving inline edit: use the field alone.
A filter bar that updates as you type: no submit, no form.
examples:
<Form aria-label="Profile" errorSummary onSubmit={save} validationErrors={errors}>
  <Input label="Full name" name="name" isRequired />
  <FieldSet legend="Contact">
    <Input label="Email" name="email" type="email" isRequired />
  </FieldSet>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
    Save changes
  </Button>
</Form>

sections.content:
- Any set of fields submitted together: create or edit a record, settings, sign-in.
- When you want a failed submit to move focus to the first problem and to list all problems.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A single search box or an auto-saving inline edit: use the field alone.
- A filter bar that updates as you type: no submit, no form.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
form (flex column, gap --ds-form-gap)
  FormErrorSummary   (errorSummary prop, or placed by hand)
  children           fields, FieldSets, actions
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                               | Type                                 | Default    | Notes                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `validationBehavior`               | `'native' \| 'aria'`                 | `'native'` | Form level; fields inherit it. `aria` marks fields invalid but never blocks the submit |
| `validationErrors`                 | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` |            | Server errors keyed by field `name`                                                    |
| `errorSummary`                     | `boolean`                            | `false`    | Shows `FormErrorSummary` at the top                                                    |
| `onSubmit`, `onReset`, `action`, … |                                      |            | As on a `form`                                                                         |
| `messages`                         | `{ summaryTitle(n) }`                |            | Per-instance message overrides                                                         |

`ref` points at the `<form>`. `FormErrorSummary` takes `className` and must be rendered inside a `Form`.

sections.heading: Validation flow
sections.content:
1. The user presses the submit button. With native validation the browser blocks an invalid submit and fires `invalid` on each invalid field.
2. React Aria displays the errors (`FieldError`) and focuses the **first invalid field**, whose error is read through `aria-describedby`.
3. With `errorSummary`, focus goes to the **summary** instead: a `role="alert"` box, "Fix 2 fields before saving", listing each invalid field as a link that focuses it.
4. Fixing a field (on blur, when React Aria commits the edit) updates the summary; it disappears when nothing is left.
5. Server errors: set `validationErrors` after the request; the matching fields show their message and the summary (if on) lists them and takes focus. Clear them on the next submit or edit.

Keep the submit button enabled: a disabled submit gives no way to learn what is wrong.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The summary is `role="alert"` with `tabindex="-1"`, so it is announced and can take focus programmatically. The links use the field label (the required marker is excluded) and the field's error text.
- Radio and checkbox groups count once, under the group's label.
- Give the form a name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) when it should be a landmark.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- The summary title is "Fix {n} fields before saving" (pluralized; "Fix 1 field before saving"). `pt-BR` has "Corrija {n} campos antes de salvar".
- Field messages say how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). A static `errorMessage` text replaces only the browser's own constraint text ("Please fill out this field"); a server error from `validationErrors` (or a `validate` message) is shown instead of it. Use the function form when you need full control: `errorMessage={(v) => v.validationDetails.valueMissing ? 'Enter a name.' : v.validationErrors.join(' ')}`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Form aria-label="Profile" errorSummary onSubmit={save} validationErrors={errors}>
  <Input label="Full name" name="name" isRequired />
  <FieldSet legend="Contact">
    <Input label="Email" name="email" type="email" isRequired />
  </FieldSet>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
    Save changes
  </Button>
</Form>
```

sections.content: - The handoff had no form-level validation; each field validated itself. Validation behavior is set once on the form, server errors are first-class, and the summary is new (GAP-003).

components.name: Grid
components.description:
A CSS grid with equal columns: a fixed `columns` count, or an auto-fill grid that keeps each
item at least `minItemWidth` wide (the responsive choice for card grids). Gaps are space
token keys.

props.name: columns
props.description: A fixed number of equal columns (1 to 12). Items can shrink below their content width.

props.name: minItemWidth
props.description:
Fills the row with as many equal columns as fit, each at least this wide: `sm` 160px,
`md` 240px, `lg` 320px (`--ds-grid-min-item-*`). Collapses to one column on narrow screens.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between rows and columns, as a key of the space scale. Default `4`.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render, `div` by default. Use `ul` or `ol` for a list of `li` children: the
list reset is applied and `role="list"` keeps the list semantics in Safari.

items.name: AutoFillMedium
items.description: As many columns as fit, each at least 240px wide. Resize the canvas to see it reflow.

items.name: NarrowContainer
items.description: In a container narrower than the minimum item width the grid is one column and never overflows.

docs.summary: A grid of equal columns: either a fixed number, or as many as fit with a minimum item width.
whenToUse: A page of cards or stats: `minItemWidth` reflows from many columns to one without media queries.
A form laid out in two or three equal columns: `columns`.
whenNotToUse: For one column of content: use `Stack`.
For a row that wraps and does not need aligned columns: use `Inline`.
For tabular data: use `DataTable`.
examples:
<Grid minItemWidth="md" gap={4}>
  <StatCard … />
  <StatCard … />
  <StatCard … />
</Grid>

<Grid columns={2} gap={4}>
  <Input label="First name" />
  <Input label="Last name" />
</Grid>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A page of cards or stats: `minItemWidth` reflows from many columns to one without media queries.
- A form laid out in two or three equal columns: `columns`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For one column of content: use `Stack`.
- For a row that wraps and does not need aligned columns: use `Inline`.
- For tabular data: use `DataTable`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (grid, gap)
  children (one per cell)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                                          | Default | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `columns`      | `1` to `12`                                   |         | Fixed equal columns. Pass this **or** `minItemWidth`                     |
| `minItemWidth` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                        |         | Auto-fill; items are at least 160 / 240 / 320px (`--ds-grid-min-item-*`) |
| `gap`          | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 8 \| 12 \| 16` | `4`     | Space token key, used for rows and columns                               |
| `as`           | `'div' \| 'ul' \| 'ol' …`                     | `'div'` | Lists get the reset and `role="list"`                                    |

The types make `columns` and `minItemWidth` exclusive. Item widths are tokens, not pixels, like the gap.

sections.heading: Responsive behavior
sections.content:
- `minItemWidth` uses `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(<width>, 100%), 1fr))`: in a container narrower than the minimum, the grid is one column and never overflows.
- `columns` does not collapse by itself. For a layout that changes by screen size, prefer `minItemWidth`, or switch `columns` from the app with a media query or `useMediaQuery`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- No semantics of its own; use `as="ul"` when the cells are list items.
- Source order is visual order for the row-first reading direction. Do not rely on CSS placement to reorder content.
- Cells can shrink (`minmax(0, 1fr)`), so long words wrap instead of widening a column.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Grid minItemWidth="md" gap={4}>
  <StatCard … />
  <StatCard … />
  <StatCard … />
</Grid>

<Grid columns={2} gap={4}>
  <Input label="First name" />
  <Input label="Last name" />
</Grid>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff hard-coded `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, 1fr)` per screen with raw pixel gaps and a 1180px minimum width. Here the minimum item width is a token and nothing needs a minimum viewport.

alternatives.name: Stack
alternatives.reason: For one column of content: use `Stack`.

alternatives.name: Inline
alternatives.reason: For a row that wraps and does not need aligned columns: use `Inline`.

alternatives.name: DataTable
alternatives.reason: For tabular data: use `DataTable`.

components.name: Heading
components.description:
A heading whose semantic level and visual size are separate choices, so the document outline
stays correct while the design picks the size.

props.name: level
props.description:
Semantic level, `h1` to `h6`. It sets the page outline for assistive technology and has
nothing to do with how big the text looks: keep levels sequential and use one `h1` per
page. Default `2`.

props.name: size
props.description:
Visual size, independent of `level`: `display` (34px, page hero), `title` (22px) or
`heading` (17px). Default: `title` for level 1, `heading` for the others.

items.name: LevelIndependentOfSize
items.description: The level is the outline, the size is the look: an h2 can be small and an h3 can be big.

docs.summary: A heading whose semantic level (`h1` to `h6`) and visual size are separate choices.
whenToUse: Any heading in page content. The level builds the outline; the size is chosen for the design.
whenNotToUse: For the page title inside the header: `TopBar` renders its own heading.
For a card caption: `Card` renders its title as a mono caption heading.
For bold text that is not a heading: use `Text`.
examples:
<Heading level={1} size="display">Orders</Heading>
<Heading level={2}>Recent</Heading>
<Heading level={3} size="title">Details</Heading>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Any heading in page content. The level builds the outline; the size is chosen for the design.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For the page title inside the header: `TopBar` renders its own heading.
- For a card caption: `Card` renders its title as a mono caption heading.
- For bold text that is not a heading: use `Text`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
h{level}  (semibold, size from the type scale)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop    | Type                                | Default                                  | Notes                                                     |
| ------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6`        | `2`                                      | Semantic level only                                       |
| `size`  | `'display' \| 'title' \| 'heading'` | `title` for level 1, `heading` otherwise | 34/40 · 22/30 · 17/24 px; display and title have tracking |

Other heading attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Keep levels sequential and use one `h1` per page. Pick the level for the outline, then the size for the look: an `h1` can use `size="heading"`, an `h4` can use `size="display"`.
- Headings use `text-wrap: balance` and break long words, so they wrap at 320px.
- Color is `--ds-text` (≥ 4.5:1 on every base surface).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Sentence case. Short and specific ("Recent orders"), no trailing punctuation.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Heading level={1} size="display">Orders</Heading>
<Heading level={2}>Recent</Heading>
<Heading level={3} size="title">Details</Heading>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff styled headings with inline font sizes tied to the element. Level and size are independent and use the type tokens.

components.name: Icon
components.description:
An inline SVG icon (Lucide, bundled) that inherits the text color and draws a 1.5px stroke.
Decorative by default; pass `label` to make it a meaningful image.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon to draw, one of the curated set exported from this package (for example `SearchIcon`).

props.name: size
props.description: Size token: `xs` 12px, `sm` 14px, `md` 18px (default), `lg` 20px.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name. Omit it when the icon only decorates text that already names the
control (the icon is then hidden from assistive technology). Set it only when the icon
carries meaning on its own, outside a control that has its own name.

props.name: directional
props.description:
Mirror the icon horizontally in right-to-left languages. Set it for icons that point in a
reading direction (chevrons, arrows); leave it off for symmetric or universal icons.

items.name: WithLabel
items.description: The icon carries meaning on its own, so it is an image with an accessible name.

items.name: InheritsColor
items.description: Inherits the text color. Color never carries meaning alone: the text says what happened.

items.name: DirectionalRtl
items.description: Directional icons mirror in right-to-left languages; the second one does not.

items.name: Gallery
items.description: Every icon of the curated set.

docs.summary:
An inline SVG icon from the curated Lucide set. It inherits the text color, draws a 1.5px stroke and is hidden from assistive technology unless you give it a `label`.

- Replaces: the runtime `unpkg.com/lucide-static` CSS-mask loading (ICON-001), text glyphs used as icons (ICON-002) and the ad hoc icon rules (ICON-003).
- Built on: `lucide-react`, bundled and tree-shakeable. No network access, no CDN.
whenToUse: Next to a text label to reinforce it (button leading slot, menu item, alert, input affordance).
Inside `IconButton`, which supplies the accessible name.
On its own only when it carries meaning that no nearby text states. Then set `label`.
whenNotToUse: As the only carrier of meaning or status. Color and shape never replace text.
For filled, colored or multi-color icons, emoji or Unicode glyphs. Use the set below.
For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
For an icon that is not in the set. Add it to `icons.ts` with a documented use first.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Next to a text label to reinforce it (button leading slot, menu item, alert, input affordance).
- Inside `IconButton`, which supplies the accessible name.
- On its own only when it carries meaning that no nearby text states. Then set `label`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- As the only carrier of meaning or status. Color and shape never replace text.
- For filled, colored or multi-color icons, emoji or Unicode glyphs. Use the set below.
- For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
- For an icon that is not in the set. Add it to `icons.ts` with a documented use first.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: A single `<svg>` (24x24 viewBox) with a `currentColor` stroke and no fill. Size and stroke come from tokens: `--ds-icon-xs|sm|md|lg` and `--ds-icon-stroke-width`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop          | Type                           | Default | Notes                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `icon`        | `IconComponent` (required)     | none    | One of the exports of the set, such as `SearchIcon`.                       |
| `size`        | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`  | 12, 14, 18, 20 px. Inside buttons use `sm`.                                |
| `label`       | `string`                       | none    | Makes the icon `role="img"` with this name. Without it the icon is hidden. |
| `directional` | `boolean`                      | `false` | Mirrors the icon in RTL. Set it for chevrons and arrows.                   |
| `className`   | `string`                       | none    | Merged with the component class.                                           |

Other SVG attributes and `ref` pass through to the `<svg>`.

sections.heading: The curated set
sections.content:
Import icons from the package, not from `lucide-react`: `import { Icon, SearchIcon } from '@loui/ds'`.

`iconSet` maps the kebab-case names below to the components and `iconNames` documents the use of each. Both are the source of the allow-list in the manifest (AI-002).

arrow-down, arrow-left, arrow-right, arrow-up, calendar, check, chevron-down, chevron-left, chevron-right, chevron-up, chevrons-up-down, circle-alert, circle-check, circle-x, ellipsis, external-link, info, loader, minus, plus, search, star, triangle-alert, x.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Decorative by default: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`.
- With `label`: `role="img"` and `aria-label`. Use short, specific names ("Saved", not "check icon").
- An icon inside a control never names the control. Put the name on the control (`IconButton label`).
- Forced colors: the stroke is `currentColor`, so it follows the system text color.
- Contrast: icons that convey meaning need 3:1 against their background (WCAG 1.4.11).
- Reduced motion: icons do not animate.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are sentence case and describe the meaning ("Saved"), never the picture ("Green check").
- No emoji or text glyphs as icons (AGENTS.md section 7).

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Bundled SVG instead of `unpkg.com/lucide-static@0.400.0` loaded through CSS `mask` at runtime.
- Decorative by default; `label` is the only way to expose an icon.
- Sizes are the `--ds-icon-*` tokens; the stroke is a token (1.5px, non-scaling) instead of the Lucide default.
- A curated, documented set replaces free-form icon names.

alternatives.name: Spinner
alternatives.reason: For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.

components.name: IconButton
components.description:
A square button with a single icon and a required accessible name.

The `label` becomes `aria-label`; there is no `title` (it would duplicate the name and is
not keyboard accessible). Set `tooltip` to show the label in a `Tooltip` on hover and focus.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name, required. Say what the button does, as a verb plus object when there is
one ("Add order", "Close dialog"), not what it looks like ("Plus").

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon to draw: one of the curated set (for example `PlusIcon`). Decorative inside the button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style: `secondary` (default, bordered) or `ghost` (no border at rest).

props.name: size
props.description: Square size token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
Shows `label` in a `Tooltip` on hover and keyboard focus. Pass `true`, or an object to add a
shortcut or change the side. Off by default. The `label` stays the accessible name; the
tooltip only repeats it visually for sighted mouse users.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<button>` element.

items.name: Toolbar
items.description: Typical toolbar: every button is named, none shows a visible label.

items.name: AccessibleName
items.description: The name is the `label`, there is no `title` attribute.

items.name: KeyboardActivation
items.description: Keyboard: Tab focuses, Enter and Space press.

docs.summary:
A square button that holds one icon and has a required accessible name. Built on React Aria's `Button`.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/IconButton` (CMP-FRM-02).
whenToUse: A compact action whose meaning is clear from context and icon: close, add, more actions, search.
Toolbars and card headers where a text button would not fit.
whenNotToUse: When there is room for a text label: use `Button` with a `leading` icon. A visible word is clearer than any icon.
For navigation: use `Link`.
For an action whose icon is ambiguous: write the label out in a `Button`.
keyboard: The name is `aria-label` only. The handoff set `title` too, which duplicated the name and was not available to keyboard or touch users. Set `tooltip` to show the label (and an optional shortcut) in a `Tooltip` on hover **and** focus, dismissible with `Esc`.
Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A compact action whose meaning is clear from context and icon: close, add, more actions, search.
- Toolbars and card headers where a text button would not fit.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- When there is room for a text label: use `Button` with a `leading` icon. A visible word is clearer than any icon.
- For navigation: use `Link`.
- For an action whose icon is ambiguous: write the label out in a `Button`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: One native `<button>` containing a decorative `Icon`. No visible text, no `title`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                       | Default                    | Notes                                                              |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`      | `string` (required)        | none                       | Accessible name, set as `aria-label`. Omitting it is a type error. |
| `icon`       | `IconComponent` (required) | none                       | One of the curated set, such as `PlusIcon`.                        |
| `variant`    | `'secondary' \| 'ghost'`   | `'secondary'`              | Bordered, or borderless at rest.                                   |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`     | `'md'`                     | 32, 40, 48 px square (`--ds-control-h-*`); icon 14, 18, 20 px.     |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                  | `false`                    | Native `disabled`, 35% opacity.                                    |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`  | none                       | React Aria press event.                                            |
| `tooltip`    | `boolean                   | { shortcut?, placement? }` | `false`                                                            | Shows `label` in a `Tooltip` on hover and focus. |
| `className`  | `string`                   | none                       | Merged with the component class.                                   |

Other React Aria `Button` props and `ref` pass through. `children`, `style`, `isPending`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` are not accepted: the label is the single source of the name.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `label` is required by the type (`label: string`), which enforces AGENTS.md section 8.
- The name is `aria-label` only. The handoff set `title` too, which duplicated the name and was not available to keyboard or touch users. Set `tooltip` to show the label (and an optional shortcut) in a `Tooltip` on hover **and** focus, dismissible with `Esc`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden` and `focusable="false"`; the button is never named by its glyph.
- Target size: 32 / 40 / 48 px, above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8 (`--ds-target-min` is also enforced as `min-inline-size` and `min-block-size`).
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press.
- Focus: accent border plus 3px ring on keyboard focus; forced-colors mode repaints the transparent outline.
- Contrast: the icon uses `--ds-text` (secondary) or `--ds-text-2` (ghost) on the surface, both above 4.5:1 and well above the 3:1 needed for graphics.
- Reduced motion: only a 150ms background transition, neutralized by the global rule.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- `label`: verb plus object in sentence case, without the word "button" or "icon": "Add order", "Close dialog", "More actions".
- Translate it like any other text; `IconButton` has no built-in strings.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `label` is enforced by types; `title` is removed.
- Children are no longer text glyphs (`+`, `...`): pass an `icon` from the set.
- Hover is CSS, not JS state; sizes use control tokens; `style` is gone.
- `disabled` is `isDisabled`, and `onPress` replaces `onClick`.
- Tooltip support is deferred to the `Tooltip` component.

alternatives.reason: When there is room for a text label: use `Button` with a `leading` icon. A visible word is clearer than any icon.

alternatives.reason: For navigation: use `Link`.

components.name: Inline
components.description:
Lays its children out in a horizontal row with a consistent gap. It wraps by default.
Direction follows the writing mode, so it mirrors in right-to-left languages.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, as a key of the space scale (`2` = `--ds-space-2` = 8px). Default `2`.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis (vertical) alignment. Default `center`.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis (horizontal) distribution. `between` pushes the first and last child to the edges. Default `start`.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Whether children wrap onto the next line when they do not fit. Default `true`, so a row never overflows a narrow screen.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render, `div` by default. Use `ul` or `ol` for a list of `li` children: the
list reset is applied and `role="list"` keeps the list semantics in Safari.

items.name: Wrapping
items.description: Wraps onto a second line in a narrow container: a row never overflows a phone.

items.name: NoWrap
items.description: With wrap off, children stay on one line and the row scrolls or clips: use it only for short rows.

items.name: RightToLeft
items.description: The row mirrors: the first child sits at the right in right-to-left text.

docs.summary: A horizontal row of children with one consistent gap. It wraps by default, so a row never overflows a narrow screen.
whenToUse: Buttons in a footer, chips, a number and its caption, a toolbar of controls.
Anything that should flow left to right (right to left in RTL) and wrap when out of room.
whenNotToUse: For a column: use `Stack`.
For equal columns that must line up across rows: use `Grid`.
For a form row where fields share the width: use `Grid` with `columns`.
examples:
<Inline justify="end">
  <Button>Cancel</Button>
  <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
</Inline>

<Inline gap={3} align="baseline">
  <Text size="body" mono>1,240</Text>
  <Text tone="secondary">orders this month</Text>
</Inline>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Buttons in a footer, chips, a number and its caption, a toolbar of controls.
- Anything that should flow left to right (right to left in RTL) and wrap when out of room.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a column: use `Stack`.
- For equal columns that must line up across rows: use `Grid`.
- For a form row where fields share the width: use `Grid` with `columns`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (flex row, wrap, gap)
  children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop      | Type                                                      | Default    | Notes                                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gap`     | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 8 \| 12 \| 16`             | `2`        | Space token key (8px by default)                                 |
| `align`   | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'baseline' \| 'stretch'` | `'center'` | Vertical alignment. Use `baseline` for a number beside its label |
| `justify` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'between'`               | `'start'`  | `between` pushes the first and last child to the edges           |
| `wrap`    | `boolean`                                                 | `true`     | Turn off only for short, fixed rows                              |
| `as`      | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'ul' \| 'ol' …`                    | `'div'`    | Lists get the reset and `role="list"`                            |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- No semantics of its own: choose `as` for meaning.
- Source order is visual order, so keyboard and reading order match. Do not reorder children with CSS.
- Wrapping keeps content reachable at 320px and 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10 reflow).
- Direction follows the writing mode, so the row mirrors in RTL.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Put the primary action last in a footer row (`justify="end"`), after the secondary action.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Inline justify="end">
  <Button>Cancel</Button>
  <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
</Inline>

<Inline gap={3} align="baseline">
  <Text size="body" mono>1,240</Text>
  <Text tone="secondary">orders this month</Text>
</Inline>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - Replaces ad hoc inline-flex styles with a typed component using space tokens.

components.name: InlineConfirm
components.description:
A two-step confirmation without a dialog: the trigger button turns into a question with
Cancel and a confirm button, in place. For a destructive action in a dense row or toolbar
where a `ConfirmDialog` would be heavy.

Focus moves to **Cancel** when the prompt opens (configurable), so Enter right after the
click cannot confirm. `Escape` cancels, but only while focus is inside the prompt (it is not a
window listener, so it does not close a surrounding `Dialog` first). When the prompt closes,
focus returns to the trigger.

props.name: label
props.description: Label of the trigger button: verb plus object ("Delete order").

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the user confirms. The prompt closes afterwards.

props.name: prompt
props.description:
The question, ideally with the consequence ("Remove this line? This can't be undone.").
Default from messages: "Are you sure?".

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Label of the confirming button. Defaults to `label`, which already names the action.

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` (default): destructive styling. `neutral`: secondary trigger, primary confirm.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
Which button gets the focus when the prompt opens. `cancel` (default) is the safe choice
and the product principle for destructive actions.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size, `md` by default.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled state: whether the prompt is showing. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the prompt opens or closes.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the trigger.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the root element.

keys.description: Label of the button that backs out of the confirmation.
Default question shown next to the buttons. State the consequence when you can.

items.name: Default
items.description: Enter on the trigger opens the prompt with focus on Cancel; Enter again cancels, it never confirms.

docs.summary:
A two-step confirmation in place: a button that turns into a question with Cancel and a confirm button. No dialog.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/InlineConfirm` (CMP-FBK-07).
whenToUse: A destructive action in a dense row, toolbar or card where a `ConfirmDialog` would be heavy ("Delete line", "Remove member").
whenNotToUse: Deleting something important or large (a customer, an order): use `ConfirmDialog`, which can show the consequence in full.
Reversible actions: do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`.
Anything that needs more input: use `Dialog`.
keyboard: Cancel and confirm are normal buttons in the tab order: `Tab` from Cancel reaches confirm.
examples:
<InlineConfirm
  label="Delete line"
  prompt="Remove this line? This can't be undone."
  onConfirm={() => removeLine(line.id)}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - A destructive action in a dense row, toolbar or card where a `ConfirmDialog` would be heavy ("Delete line", "Remove member").

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Deleting something important or large (a customer, an order): use `ConfirmDialog`, which can show the consequence in full.
- Reversible actions: do them and offer **Undo** in a `Toast`.
- Anything that needs more input: use `Dialog`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span                       (inline-flex)
  Button                   trigger: variant danger | secondary          (idle)
─ or ─
span[role=group]           aria-labelledby = prompt                    (asking)
  span                     prompt (text-2)
  Button ghost             Cancel                                       <- initial focus
  Button danger-solid | primary   confirm
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                      | Type                    | Default         | Notes                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                   | `string` (required)     | none            | Trigger text: verb plus object ("Delete line"). |
| `onConfirm`                               | `() => void` (required) | none            |                                                 |
| `prompt`                                  | `string`                | "Are you sure?" | State the consequence when you can.             |
| `confirmLabel`                            | `string`                | `label`         |                                                 |
| `tone`                                    | `'danger' \| 'neutral'` | `danger`        | `neutral`: secondary trigger, primary confirm.  |
| `initialFocus`                            | `'cancel' \| 'confirm'` | `cancel`        | Cancel is the safe default.                     |
| `size`                                    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`  | `md`            |                                                 |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                         |                 | Controlled / uncontrolled prompt state.         |
| `isDisabled`                              | `boolean`               | `false`         | Disables the trigger.                           |
| `messages`                                | `{ cancel, prompt }`    |                 | Per-instance overrides (pt-BR ships).           |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- **Initial focus is Cancel** by default, so Enter or Space pressed right after the click cannot confirm. The handoff auto-focused the confirm button.
- **Escape cancels, scoped.** The handler is on the prompt, not on `window`. It only fires while focus is inside the prompt, and it stops propagation, so an enclosing `Dialog` or `Sheet` stays open (tested); a second Escape closes the dialog. The handoff attached a window listener (ARCH-005).
- **Focus returns to the trigger** after Cancel, Escape or confirm.
- The prompt is a `group` named by the question; screen readers hear it when focus lands on Cancel. Button names are real text; color (red) is never the only signal.
- Cancel and confirm are normal buttons in the tab order: `Tab` from Cancel reaches confirm.
- With `defaultOpen`, focus moves to Cancel on mount; avoid it on page load.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Trigger and confirm: verb plus object, sentence case ("Delete line"). Not "Yes" or "OK".
- Prompt: a short question; add the consequence ("Remove this line? This can't be undone.").

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<InlineConfirm
  label="Delete line"
  prompt="Remove this line? This can't be undone."
  onConfirm={() => removeLine(line.id)}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Initial focus on Cancel (configurable) instead of confirm.
- Scoped Escape instead of a window listener; focus restored to the trigger.
- `danger` boolean became `tone`; `cancelLabel` and the default prompt come from the message catalog (English and pt-BR).
- Controlled and uncontrolled state; `isDisabled`; the prompt is a labelled group.

alternatives.name: ConfirmDialog
alternatives.reason: Deleting something important or large (a customer, an order): use `ConfirmDialog`, which can show the consequence in full.

alternatives.name: Dialog
alternatives.reason: Anything that needs more input: use `Dialog`.

components.name: Input
components.description:
Single-line text field: label, control, description and error wired together
(`for`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`), built on React Aria `TextField`.

Consumer `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown` etc. are composed with the internal handlers, so
they never break the focus ring (a defect of the handoff).

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control (handoff `hint`). Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description:
Error text (handoff `error`). Shown while the field is invalid *and* the error is displayed:
after a submit attempt with the default `validationBehavior="native"`, or at once when you
control `isInvalid`. A function receives the validation result.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for the label.

props.name: mono
props.description: Geist Mono with tabular figures, for codes, identifiers and numbers.

props.name: leading
props.description: Decoration before the text, usually an `Icon`. Keep it decorative or give it its own name.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Content after the text: a unit, a shortcut hint (`Kbd`), or an `IconButton`.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root (label, control and messages).

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Class name for the `<input>` element.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

docs.summary: Single-line text field with a label, helper text and error text wired together. Built on React Aria `TextField` + `Input`; see [Field](../Field/Field.md) for the shared states, spacing and validation timing.
whenToUse: Short free text, codes, emails, search terms, numbers typed as text.
Use `mono` for codes and identifiers (`ORD-1048`).
whenNotToUse: Several lines of text: `Textarea`.
A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
Currency or quantity entry that needs masking: a dedicated field (`CurrencyInput`, planned).
keyboard: Keyboard: standard text editing. `Enter` submits the surrounding form. Focus is visible as the accent border plus ring; in forced-colors mode it is a system outline.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Short free text, codes, emails, search terms, numbers typed as text.
- Use `mono` for codes and identifiers (`ORD-1048`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Several lines of text: `Textarea`.
- A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
- Currency or quantity entry that needs masking: a dedicated field (`CurrencyInput`, planned).

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
Label *                          required marker (aria-hidden)
[ leading  value / placeholder  trailing ]
Description
Error
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                | Notes                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                             | Visible label. Without it you must pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise). |
| `description`                                                       | Helper text (handoff `hint`).                                                                     |
| `errorMessage`                                                      | Error text (handoff `error`), node or function of the validation result. Needs an invalid state.  |
| `isInvalid` / `isRequired` / `isReadOnly` / `isDisabled`            | Standard states. `isInvalid` shows the error at once.                                             |
| `size`                                                              | `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.                                                        |
| `mono`                                                              | Geist Mono with tabular figures.                                                                  |
| `leading` / `trailing`                                              | Adornments inside the box: an `Icon`, a unit, a `Kbd` hint, an `IconButton`.                      |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                        | Controlled and uncontrolled, React Aria naming (`onChange` receives the string, not the event).   |
| `name`, `type`, `autoComplete`, `inputMode`, `maxLength`, `pattern` | Passed to the `<input>`; `name` and the value take part in form submission.                       |
| `validate`, `validationBehavior`                                    | See Field.md.                                                                                     |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                                  | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                                |
| `messages`                                                          | `requiredMark` override.                                                                          |

All other props of React Aria `TextField` are accepted (`onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown`, `autoFocus`, `form`, ...). They are composed with the internal handlers, never replacing them.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Native `<input>` named by `<label for>`; description and error are in `aria-describedby`; `aria-invalid` when invalid; `required` when required.
- Keyboard: standard text editing. `Enter` submits the surrounding form. Focus is visible as the accent border plus ring; in forced-colors mode it is a system outline.
- The placeholder never replaces the label.
- Click anywhere in the box (including padding) focuses the input. Clicking a decorative adornment does not; make interactive adornments real buttons with their own names.

sections.heading: Content
sections.content:
- Label: sentence case noun ("Workspace name"). Error: how to fix it ("Enter a complete email address.").
- Description: one short sentence, no exclamation marks.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Input label="Workspace name" placeholder="e.g. Northwind" description="Visible to everyone." isRequired />
<Input label="Email" type="email" name="email" errorMessage="Enter a complete email address." isRequired />
<Input aria-label="Search orders" leading={<Icon icon={SearchIcon} />} trailing={<Kbd>/</Kbd>} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Focus styling is CSS (`:focus-within`), not React state, and consumer `onFocus`/`onBlur` no longer break it (regression test).
- `hint` is `description`, `error` is `errorMessage`; the error is only shown for an invalid field.
- Ids are generated; `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `required` and `readOnly` are wired.
- Disabled uses the shared opacity and a dashed border; read-only is new.
- The handoff `style` / `inputStyle` escape hatches are replaced by `className` and `inputClassName`.
