components.name: Kbd
components.description:
A keyboard shortcut hint in mono type. With `keys` it renders `Mod` as the command symbol
on Apple platforms and as Ctrl elsewhere, and gives screen readers the spoken key names.

props.name: keys
props.description:
The keys of one shortcut, in order: `['Mod', 'K']`, `['Shift', 'Enter']`, `['Esc']`.
Recognized names (case-insensitive): `Mod` (Command on Apple, Control elsewhere), `Cmd`,
`Meta`, `Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Option`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`,
`Space`, arrows (`Up`, `ArrowUp`, ...), `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`. Anything
else is shown as typed (`K`, `/`, `1`). Symbols are hidden from assistive technology and
replaced by the spoken name.

props.name: children
props.description: Free content shown as is (for example `⌘K`). Prefer `keys`, which is accessible and platform-aware.

props.name: platform
props.description:
Forces the platform used to render `Mod` and the modifier symbols. By default it is
detected in the browser; during server rendering and the first client render it is
`other` (Ctrl), then switches to `apple` (the command symbol) after hydration.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ name: (key: KbdKeyId) => string; label: (key: KbdKeyId) => string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the spoken key names and short key labels.

items.name: Default
items.description: `Mod` follows the platform of the browser that views the story.

items.name: PortugueseLocale
items.description: Spoken names come from the `Kbd` message catalog and follow the `DSProvider` locale.

docs.summary: A keyboard shortcut hint in mono type. It renders a real `<kbd>` element.
whenToUse: Next to a command, menu item or button to show its shortcut: "Search `Ctrl K`".
In help text and tooltips that name a key.
whenNotToUse: To register the shortcut: use `useHotkey`. `Kbd` only displays it.
For code or file names: use `<code>`.
keyboard: When the visible text already is the name (`Enter`, `Tab`) nothing is duplicated.
examples:
<Kbd keys={['Mod', 'K']} />
<Kbd keys={['Shift', 'Enter']} />
<Kbd keys={['Esc']} />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Next to a command, menu item or button to show its shortcut: "Search `Ctrl K`".
- In help text and tooltips that name a key.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To register the shortcut: use `useHotkey`. `Kbd` only displays it.
- For code or file names: use `<code>`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
kbd.root (border, mono)
  kbd.key   symbol or text   (aria-hidden when a spoken name replaces it)
            VisuallyHidden   spoken name ("Command")
  kbd.key   K
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop       | Type                       | Default  | Notes                                                                     |
| ---------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keys`     | `readonly string[]`        | -        | The keys of one shortcut, in order (`['Mod', 'K']`). Use this or children |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                | -        | Free content shown as is. No accessible expansion                         |
| `platform` | `'apple' \| 'other'`       | detected | Forces how `Mod` and the modifier symbols render (tests, docs)            |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ name; label }>` |          | Overrides the spoken names (`name(key)`) and short labels (`label(key)`)  |

Recognized names in `keys` (case-insensitive): `Mod`, `Cmd`/`Meta`, `Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`/`Option`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Space`, `Up`/`ArrowUp` (and Down, Left, Right), `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`. Anything else (`K`, `/`, `1`) is shown as typed; single letters are upper-cased with the active locale.

sections.heading: Platform awareness
sections.content:
`Mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Control elsewhere. The server and the first client render use `other` (Ctrl) so hydration matches; the component then reads the real platform (`useSyncExternalStore`) and re-renders with the command symbol on Apple devices. Pass `platform` to pin it. The same detection backs `useHotkey`, so the hint always matches the key that works.

On Apple platforms modifiers use symbols (`⌘ ⌃ ⇧ ⌥ ↵ ⎋ ⇥ ⌫ ⌦`); elsewhere they are short text (`Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Esc`, `Del`). Command and the arrows use their symbol everywhere.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Screen readers do not reliably read symbols such as `⌘`. Every symbol or abbreviation is `aria-hidden` and followed by a visually hidden spoken name from the message catalog: "Command K", "Control Shift Escape".
- When the visible text already is the name (`Enter`, `Tab`) nothing is duplicated.
- The element has no role and is not focusable: it is text. The shortcut itself must be announced where it works (for example `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control, which is the control's responsibility).
- Text is `--ds-text-2`, which keeps at least 4.5:1 on the surface (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Write the logical key (`Mod`), not the platform one.
- One `Kbd` per shortcut. A sequence ("G then I") is two `Kbd`s with the word between them from your own copy; sequences are not a built-in prop.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Kbd keys={['Mod', 'K']} />
<Kbd keys={['Shift', 'Enter']} />
<Kbd keys={['Esc']} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `keys` replaces hand-typed `⌘K`; the platform decides the modifier.
- Symbols are expanded for assistive technology with messages (English and pt-BR shipped).
- Height and padding are tokens (`--ds-kbd-*`). No `style` prop.

components.name: Label
components.description:
The visible label of a field. Must be rendered inside a React Aria field (TextField, Select,
CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, ...), which wires `for` / `aria-labelledby`.
With `isRequired` it appends a visible marker (text from messages) that is hidden from
assistive technology: screen readers get "required" from the control itself (`required` /
`aria-required`), so announcing the marker too would repeat it.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Adds the required marker after the text. The control itself must also be required.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

keys.description: Visible marker after the label of a required field. Hidden from assistive technology.

items.name: Anatomy
items.description: The building blocks composed by hand inside a React Aria field. Prefer the ready-made fields.

items.name: ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt
items.description:
Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

items.name: RealtimeValidation
items.description: The alternative: `validationBehavior="aria"` reports problems while the user types. Use sparingly.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

components.name: LedgerList
components.description:
A list of signed ledger entries: date, title, optional sub line, a signed amount and an
optional running balance. The sign is text (`+` / `−`) as well as color. Built as a `ul`.

Amounts are integers in minor units (ADR-0006) formatted with `Intl`: pass `currency` for
money, `format` for anything else, or neither for plain quantities.

Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

props.name: entries
props.description: The entries, in display order (usually newest first).

props.name: currency
props.description:
ISO 4217 currency code ("USD"). When set, amounts and balances are formatted as money with
`formatCurrency` (minor units). Ignored when `format` is given.

props.name: format
props.description:
Custom formatter for amounts and balances, receiving a number in the same unit as `delta`.
The amount of an entry is passed as an absolute value (the sign is shown separately).
Without `currency` or `format`, numbers are formatted for the locale.

props.name: negativeTone
props.description:
Color of negative amounts: `neutral`, `success`, `warning` or `danger` (default). The `-`
sign is always shown too. Pick the tone by what the subtraction means (an expense is
`danger`, a payment out of a balance owed may be `success`).

props.name: dateStyle
props.description: Format of each entry's date (`formatDate` styles). Default `monthDay`.

props.name: onDelete
props.description:
Adds a "Delete entry" button to each row and calls this with the entry. Deleting must be
confirmed by the consumer (dialog or inline confirmation) before data is removed.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ balance: (amount: string) => string; deleteEntry: (title: string) => string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

keys.description: Label of the running balance after an entry. `amount` is already formatted.
Accessible name of the delete button of an entry; `title` is the entry's title.

items.name: Quantities
items.description: Plain quantities: no currency, numbers formatted for the locale.

items.name: CustomFormat
items.description: A custom formatter receives the absolute amount in the same unit as `delta`.

items.name: Deletable
items.description: The consumer is responsible for confirming before data is removed.

docs.summary:
A list of signed entries: date, title, optional sub line, a signed amount and an optional running balance, with an optional delete button per row. The sign is shown as text and color. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/LedgerList.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-12`).
whenToUse: A short history of changes to a balance or a quantity: account activity, wallet movements, stock adjustments.
When the running balance after each entry matters.
whenNotToUse: Large, sortable or filterable data: use `DataTable`.
A feed of events with no amounts: use a plain list.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A short history of changes to a balance or a quantity: account activity, wallet movements, stock adjustments.
- When the running balance after each entry matters.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Large, sortable or filterable data: use `DataTable`.
- A feed of events with no amounts: use a plain list.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
ul aria-label
  li[data-direction=positive|negative|zero]
    time[datetime]                 formatDate(date, locale, dateStyle)
    title · sub
    amount                         "+" | "−" text sign + number   (color by negativeTone)
    balance                        "Balance $125.00"              (optional)
    button "Delete entry …"        (only with onDelete)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                                              | Default      | Notes                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entries`      | `LedgerEntry[]`                                   | required     | `{ id, date, title, sub?, delta, balance? }`; `delta` and `balance` are integers. |
| `currency`     | `string`                                          | none         | ISO 4217 code: amounts are minor units formatted with `formatCurrency`.           |
| `format`       | `(value: number) => string`                       | none         | Custom formatter; wins over `currency`. Amounts are passed as absolute values.    |
| `negativeTone` | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'danger'`   | Color of negative amounts; the minus sign is always shown.                        |
| `dateStyle`    | `DateStyle`                                       | `'monthDay'` | Any `formatDate` style.                                                           |
| `onDelete`     | `(entry) => void`                                 | none         | Adds a delete button to each row.                                                 |
| `messages`     | `{ balance, deleteEntry }`                        | none         | Overrides the texts for this instance.                                            |

With neither `currency` nor `format`, numbers are formatted for the locale (plain quantities).

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A `ul` of `li`; the list should be named with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- The sign is text (`+` or the minus sign U+2212), so meaning never depends on color. Positive amounts use ink, negative ones the chosen tone, zero uses secondary text.
- Dates are `<time datetime>`. The balance is labelled by text ("Balance $125.00"), not by position.
- Delete buttons are `IconButton`s named "Delete entry {title}" (one per row, distinguishable); they are 32px.
- Deleting must ask for confirmation (AGENTS.md): do it in `onDelete` with a dialog or inline confirmation, then offer Undo.
- Text truncates with an ellipsis; long titles do not push the amounts out.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Titles say what happened in sentence case ("Payment received"); the sub line holds the reference.
- Amounts are integers in minor units (ADR-0006); never pre-format them.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A `div` of `div`s becomes a `ul` / `li` list; dates are `time` elements formatted with `formatDate` (the handoff printed a raw string).
- Amounts go through `Intl` (`formatCurrency` or `formatNumber`) from minor units, or a `format` prop; there is no hand-built number formatting.
- "saldo" and "Excluir lançamento" were hard-coded Portuguese; they are messages (`en`, `pt-BR`), and the delete label includes the entry title.
- `negativeTone` defaults to `danger` (the handoff defaulted to `success`, which is product specific) and takes `neutral | success | warning | danger`.
- The delete button is the shared `IconButton` (focus ring, 32px target) instead of a styled `×` glyph; layout values are tokens (`--ds-ledger-list-*`).

components.name: Legend
components.description:
A list of the series of a chart: swatch, name and, optionally, a value. With `interactive`
each item is a toggle button that hides or shows its series, and the legend reports the
hidden ids so the chart can leave those series out (`StackedBar` does this itself; with
`Chart` keep `hiddenIds` in state and filter your data).

The swatch is never the only identification: every item has its text label, a hatch pattern
tells apart series beyond the fourth, and a hidden series shows a hollow swatch and a struck
label in addition to the pressed state read by screen readers.

props.name: items
props.description: The series, in the same order as in the chart (the order sets the swatch of items without `color`).

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (default) wraps items in a row; `vertical` stacks them, one per line.

props.name: interactive
props.description:
Turns each item into a toggle button (`aria-pressed`: pressed means the series is shown),
so readers can hide series in the chart that consumes the legend. Off by default: a plain list.

props.name: hiddenIds
props.description: Controlled list of hidden series ids (interactive legends).

props.name: defaultHiddenIds
props.description: Initial hidden series ids when uncontrolled.

props.name: onHiddenIdsChange
props.description: Called with the new list of hidden ids whenever the user toggles an item.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Accessible name of the legend list, unless the consumer passes `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

keys.default: Press a series to show or hide it.
keys.description: Accessible description of an interactive legend: what pressing an item does. Read after the name of the list.

items.name: Default
items.description: A plain list: swatch, name and an optional value.

items.name: EightSeries
items.description: Beyond four series the ramp repeats with a hatch, so no two swatches look alike.

items.name: ExplicitColors
items.description: Explicit colors are for when the neutral ramp is not enough; the label still names every series.

items.name: Interactive
items.description:
Interactive items are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`: pressed means shown). A hidden series
shows a hollow swatch and a struck label, not only a color change.

items.name: WithChart
items.description: The legend is not tied to a chart: keep the hidden ids in state and filter your data.

docs.summary: A list of the series of a chart: swatch, name and, optionally, a value. With `interactive` each item is a toggle button that hides or shows its series, and the legend reports which ones are hidden so the chart can leave them out.
whenToUse: Naming the series of a multi-series chart (`StackedBar` renders one itself).
Letting readers hide series to compare the rest.
Next to a `Chart` when you plot one series at a time and let the reader pick which.
whenNotToUse: One series: name the chart instead.
Choosing between views or filters unrelated to a chart: use `SegmentedControl`, `ToggleGroup` or `Tabs`.
Showing the parts of a single bar with percentages: `ProportionBar` has its own legend.
keyboard: Interactive items are native buttons (React Aria `ToggleButton`): `Tab` moves between them, `Space` and `Enter` toggle. `aria-pressed="true"` means the series is **shown**. The list is described by a hint ("Press a series to show or hide it.").

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Naming the series of a multi-series chart (`StackedBar` renders one itself).
- Letting readers hide series to compare the rest.
- Next to a `Chart` when you plot one series at a time and let the reader pick which.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- One series: name the chart instead.
- Choosing between views or filters unrelated to a chart: use `SegmentedControl`, `ToggleGroup` or `Tabs`.
- Showing the parts of a single bar with percentages: `ProportionBar` has its own legend.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
ul[aria-label="Legend"]
  li  swatch (aria-hidden) · name · value (optional)
  li  button[aria-pressed] (interactive)  swatch · name · value
VisuallyHidden  hint, linked with aria-describedby (interactive only)
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                | Type                              | Default        | Notes                                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`             | `{ id, label, value?, color? }[]` | -              | Same order as the chart: the position sets the swatch |
| `orientation`       | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`      | `'horizontal'` | Row that wraps, or one item per line                  |
| `interactive`       | `boolean`                         | `false`        | Items become toggle buttons                           |
| `hiddenIds`         | `readonly string[]`               |                | Controlled hidden series                              |
| `defaultHiddenIds`  | `readonly string[]`               | `[]`           | Initial hidden series when uncontrolled               |
| `onHiddenIdsChange` | `(ids: string[]) => void`         |                | Called on every toggle                                |
| `messages`          | `Partial<messages>`               |                | `label` (list name), `toggleHint`                     |

sections.heading: Telling series apart without color
sections.content:
The swatch follows the same neutral ramp as `StackedBar` and `ProportionBar` (`--ds-chart-series-1` to `-4`, which are `text`, `text-2`, `text-3` and `line-control`). From the fifth series on the ramp repeats with a hatch pattern, so up to eight series look different. Beyond that, pass `color` or group the tail into "Other". The text label always identifies the series; the swatch only helps sighted users.

A hidden series is shown with a hollow swatch and a struck-through label, in addition to `aria-pressed="false"`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A real list named "Legend" (override with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
- Interactive items are native buttons (React Aria `ToggleButton`): `Tab` moves between them, `Space` and `Enter` toggle. `aria-pressed="true"` means the series is **shown**. The list is described by a hint ("Press a series to show or hide it.").
- Toggle buttons are at least 24 px tall (target size 2.5.8) and have a visible focus ring; forced colors use system colors for swatches and focus.
- The chart that consumes the legend must update visibly when a series is toggled. If it can end up with nothing to show, say so in text (`StackedBar` does).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Series names are short nouns in sentence case ("Online", "Store").
- Values are formatted text; use `Intl` helpers for the locale.

components.name: Link
components.description:
A link built on React Aria's `Link`. With `href` it renders a real `<a>` and uses the router
set on `DSProvider` for client-side navigation. Links that open a new tab (`target="_blank"`)
get `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external-link icon and a hidden note for screen readers.

props.name: variant
props.description:
- `inline` (default): underlined, for links inside running text. Color alone does not
  identify a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so the underline is part of the design.
- `standalone`: no underline at rest (underlined on hover and focus). Only where the context
  makes it obvious that it is a link: a navigation list, a "View all" line under a heading.

props.name: children
props.description: Link text. Describe the destination or action ("Pricing details"), never "click here".

props.name: messages
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<a>` element.

props.name: render
props.type: (props: DetailedHTMLProps<LinkWithRequiredHref, HTMLAnchorElement> | DetailedHTMLProps<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, HTMLSpanElement>, renderProps: LinkRenderProps) => ReactElement<...>

items.name: InText
items.description: In running text the underline is part of the design: color alone does not identify a link.

items.name: Standalone
items.description: No underline at rest. Use it only where the context makes the link obvious.

items.name: External
items.description: Opens a new tab: `rel` is set, an icon shows it, and screen readers hear it.

items.name: KeyboardActivation
items.description: Keyboard: Tab focuses, Enter follows the link through the router set on DSProvider.

docs.summary:
A link to another page, section or site. Built on React Aria's `Link`: a real `<a href>` that uses the router set on `DSProvider` for client-side navigation.

- Handoff source: none (the handoff only had underlined `<a>` styles); part of GAP-002.
whenToUse: To go somewhere: another route, a section (`#id`), a document or an external site.
Inside running text (`inline`), or as a quiet navigation line such as "View all orders" (`standalone`).
whenNotToUse: To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
For a styled call to action that happens to navigate: still a link semantically, but use a `Button` with `href` when it is the primary action of the screen (planned with the button-as-link variant).
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` follows. (`Space` does not activate a link, by design.)
examples:
Read the pricing details before you change a plan.

View all orders Documentation

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- To go somewhere: another route, a section (`#id`), a document or an external site.
- Inside running text (`inline`), or as a quiet navigation line such as "View all orders" (`standalone`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
- For a styled call to action that happens to navigate: still a link semantically, but use a `Button` with `href` when it is the primary action of the screen (planned with the button-as-link variant).

sections.heading: Variants
sections.content:
| Variant      | At rest   | Hover and keyboard focus | Use                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inline`     | underline | thicker underline        | Links inside sentences. Default.                                         |
| `standalone` | none      | underline                | Navigation lists, "View all" lines. Only where context makes it obvious. |

Color alone never identifies a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so inline links are always underlined. The accent color (`--ds-accent`) is reserved for focus, selection and links.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                         | Default    | Notes                                                                       |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`       | `string`                     | none       | Destination. Without it the element is a non-navigating `role="link"` span. |
| `variant`    | `'inline' \| 'standalone'`   | `'inline'` | See above.                                                                  |
| `target`     | `string`                     | none       | `_blank` adds `rel`, the icon and the screen reader note.                   |
| `rel`        | `string`                     | none       | Merged with `noopener noreferrer` for `_blank`.                             |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                    | `false`    | `aria-disabled`, 35% opacity, presses ignored.                              |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`    | none       | React Aria press event, fired before navigation.                            |
| `messages`   | `{ opensInNewTab?: string }` | none       | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                   |
| `className`  | `string`                     | none       | Merged with the component class.                                            |

Other React Aria `Link` props (`download`, `routerOptions`, `hrefLang`, `aria-*`, ...) and `ref` pass through.

sections.heading: Routing
sections.content: Wrap the app once: `<DSProvider navigate={router.push} useHref={router.resolve}>`. Links with a relative `href` then navigate without a page reload; modified clicks (Ctrl/Cmd, middle button) and `target="_blank"` keep the browser behavior.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Real `<a href>`: opens in a new tab with the context menu, can be copied, works without JavaScript.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` follows. (`Space` does not activate a link, by design.)
- Focus: 3px accent ring through `data-focus-visible`; forced-colors mode repaints the transparent outline and system link colors apply.
- Links that open a new tab: the name ends with "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers (hidden text from the `Link` messages) and a decorative icon shows it visually. `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is added automatically.
- Contrast: accent `#8AB4FF` on the dark surfaces is well above 4.5:1.
- Target size: inline links in text are exempt from WCAG 2.5.8; standalone links should sit in a 24px-high row.
- Reduced motion: hover changes decoration thickness only, no animation.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Link text describes the destination or action and makes sense out of context: "Pricing details", "Download invoice". Never "click here" or "read more".
- Sentence case, no trailing punctuation inside the link, no emoji.
- Do not repeat the word "link". The role is announced.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx

Read the pricing details before you change a plan.

View all orders Documentation ```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- New component (GAP-002 part); there was no handoff `Link`. Unstyled `<a>` underlines in the handoff foundation are now this component.
- Adds the external-link behavior (`rel`, icon, screen reader note) and a standalone variant.

components.name: MatrixGrid
components.description:
A matrix of toggle cells: rows by columns, each cell linking or unlinking one row with one
column. It is an ARIA `grid` with roving focus: the grid is one tab stop, the arrow keys move
between cells (`Home` / `End` within a row, `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` to the first / last
cell), and `Space` or `Enter` toggles. Arrow keys follow the reading direction.

Each cell is a button named "{row} · {column}: linked" / "not linked" (messages). The grid
scrolls horizontally inside a labelled, focusable region.

Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the grid ("Product colors"). The scroll region around it is named from it too.

props.name: rows
props.description: The rows, in display order. Sort them yourself (alphabetically by default).

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns, in display order.

props.name: isLinked
props.description: Whether a row and a column are linked. Called for every cell on each render; keep it cheap.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Called with the row and column ids when the user toggles a cell. Update your state in it.

props.name: cornerLabel
props.description: Caption of the first (row header) column. Without it a visually hidden "Row" is used.

props.name: countLabel
props.description: Adds a last column with the number of linked cells per row; this is its header ("Linked").

props.name: hint
props.description: Help text under the grid, linked to it with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ cell: (row: string, column: string, linked: boolean) => string; scrollRegion: (name: string) => string; rowHeader: string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

keys.description: Accessible name of a toggle cell: the row, the column and the state of the link.
Accessible name of the focusable scroll region around the grid. `name` is the grid's name.
Hidden header text of the first column when no `cornerLabel` is given.

items.name: CheckContrast
items.description: Bright, dark and mid-tone colors: the check mark switches by WCAG contrast.

items.name: ManyColumns
items.description: The region scrolls horizontally and is focusable and labelled.

items.name: KeyboardNavigation
items.description: One tab stop for the grid; arrows, Home/End and Ctrl+Home/End move; Space and Enter toggle.

docs.summary:
A rows-by-columns matrix of toggle cells, where each cell links or unlinks one row with one column (for example which colors a product comes in). It is an ARIA `grid` with roving focus and full arrow-key navigation. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/MatrixGrid.jsx` (TODO `CMP-PAT-11`).
whenToUse: Editing many-to-many relations where seeing the whole matrix helps (items by options, users by roles, products by regions).
When every cell is a quick on/off decision.
whenNotToUse: Reading or sorting data: use a table (`DataTable`).
One list of independent switches: use `CheckboxGroup` or `Switch`.
Very large matrices (hundreds of rows): this component renders every cell.
keyboard: Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop (roving tabindex; the scroll region is the stop before it). `←` `→` `↑` `↓` move one cell (horizontal arrows follow the reading direction and stop at the edges); `Home` / `End` go to the first / last cell of the row; `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` to the first / last cell of the grid; `Space` and `Enter` toggle.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Editing many-to-many relations where seeing the whole matrix helps (items by options, users by roles, products by regions).
- When every cell is a quick on/off decision.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Reading or sorting data: use a table (`DataTable`).
- One list of independent switches: use `CheckboxGroup` or `Switch`.
- Very large matrices (hundreds of rows): this component renders every cell.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  div[role=region] aria-label="… scrollable" tabindex=0      (horizontal scroll)
    div[role=grid] aria-label aria-describedby=hint
      div[role=row]
        columnheader (corner caption) · columnheader (swatch + label) × N · columnheader (count)
      div[role=row] × rows
        rowheader (label + meta) · gridcell > button "{row} · {column}: linked" × N · gridcell (count)
  p.hint
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop          | Type                           | Default      | Notes                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-label`  | `string`                       | required     | Names the grid; the scroll region is named "{label}, scrollable".     |
| `rows`        | `{ id, label, meta? }[]`       | required     | Display order is yours (sort alphabetically by default).              |
| `columns`     | `{ id, label, color? }[]`      | required     | `color` is `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`; fills linked cells and shows a swatch. |
| `isLinked`    | `(rowId, columnId) => boolean` | required     | Source of truth is yours.                                             |
| `onToggle`    | `(rowId, columnId) => void`    | required     | Update your state here.                                               |
| `cornerLabel` | `string`                       | hidden "Row" | Caption of the row header column.                                     |
| `countLabel`  | `string`                       | none         | Adds a count column ("Linked") with the per-row number of links.      |
| `hint`        | `ReactNode`                    | none         | Help text under the grid, linked with `aria-describedby`.             |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Semantics: `region` (focusable scroll container) > `grid` > `row` > `columnheader` / `rowheader` / `gridcell`. Each cell holds a native button named "{row} · {column}: linked" or "not linked" (messages, `en` and `pt-BR`); the state is in the name, so there is no separate `aria-pressed`.
- Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop (roving tabindex; the scroll region is the stop before it). `←` `→` `↑` `↓` move one cell (horizontal arrows follow the reading direction and stop at the edges); `Home` / `End` go to the first / last cell of the row; `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` to the first / last cell of the grid; `Space` and `Enter` toggle.
- Linked state is not color alone: linked cells are solid with a check, unlinked cells are dashed with a plus; the name says it too.
- The check color is chosen with `readableTextOn` (WCAG relative luminance) on the column color, and the choice is tested at 3:1 for a set of colors.
- Targets are 40x40px (the minimum is 24px). Unlinked cell borders use `--ds-line-control` (3:1).
- Motion: the hover scale (1.06) exists only inside `@media (hover: hover) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.
- Forced colors: borders use `ButtonText`, linked cells `Highlight`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Row and column labels are short nouns in sentence case; they are read in every cell name, so keep them unique within their axis.
- `countLabel` names what is counted ("Linked", "Colors").

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Plain `div`s with `aria-pressed` buttons become an ARIA grid with arrow-key navigation and roving focus; the handoff had only Tab through every cell.
- The mouse-only Portuguese `title` tooltip is replaced by an accessible name from messages.
- The 0.299/0.587/0.114 luma shortcut is replaced by `readableTextOn` (WCAG 2.x contrast).
- The scroll container is a labelled, focusable region.
- Sizes (cell 40, column 64, label 220, count 64, row 60) are tokens `--ds-matrix-grid-*`; `labelWidth` and `cell` props are gone. Column colors are applied via the `--ds-matrix-grid-color` custom property, not inline fills.
- The hover scale respects reduced motion. Column headers use a decorative `Swatch`.

docs.summary:
A menu of commands that opens from a trigger. Built on React Aria `MenuTrigger`, `Popover` and `Menu`. Exports `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSection`, `MenuSeparator`, `SubMenu` and `MoreActionsMenu`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Menu` (CMP-NAV-02).
whenToUse: Row, card or toolbar actions that do not deserve their own button.

whenNotToUse: Choosing a value for a field: use `Select` or `Combobox`.

The only way to reach an important action: keep primary actions visible.
examples:
<MoreActionsMenu onAction={(key) => run(String(key))}>
  <MenuItem id="edit" shortcut="Ctrl+E">Edit order</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="duplicate">Duplicate order</MenuItem>
  <MenuSeparator />
  <MenuItem id="delete" tone="danger">Delete order</MenuItem>
</MoreActionsMenu>

<Menu trigger={<Button>View</Button>} selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['id']}>
  <MenuItem id="id">Show ID</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="status">Show status</MenuItem>
</Menu>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Row, card or toolbar actions that do not deserve their own button.
- View options with check or radio items (columns shown, sort order, density).

sections.heading: When not to use

- Choosing a value for a field: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Content the user types into or operates (filters, forms): use `Popover`.
- Navigation between pages: use `Tabs`, `Sidebar` or `Breadcrumb`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
MenuTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton    aria-haspopup=true, aria-expanded
  Popover            raised surface, radius lg, overlay shadow, z popover

components.name: Meter
components.description:
A bar that shows a quantity within a known range (disk used, quota, score), as opposed to
progress of a task. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"`).

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label, wired to the bar with `aria-labelledby`. Required unless you set `aria-label`
or `aria-labelledby`: a bar without a name is an accessibility bug (React Aria warns in development).

props.name: meta
props.description:
Text on the right of the label, in mono type: "6.2 / 10 GB". It is visual only. If it says
more than the percentage, also pass `valueLabel` so screen readers hear the same thing.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the formatted percentage (`62%`, from `Intl` with the active locale) as `meta` when `meta` is not given.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color of the fill. Color is never the only signal: pair it with a label or `meta`. Default `accent`.

docs.summary: A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.
whenToUse: `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
`Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.
whenNotToUse: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.
examples:
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
- `Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                            | Type                                             | Default    | Notes                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                         | `number`                                         | `0`        | Clamped to the range                                                                               |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`          | `number`                                         | `0`, `100` |                                                                                                    |
| `isIndeterminate`               | `boolean` (`Progress` only)                      |            | No `aria-valuenow`; the fill sweeps                                                                |
| `label`                         | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visible label, wired as the accessible name                                                        |
| `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                         |            | Use when there is no visible label. One of the three is required (React Aria warns in development) |
| `meta`                          | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visual text on the right ("6.2 / 10 GB")                                                           |
| `showValue`                     | `boolean`                                        | `false`    | Shows the formatted percentage as `meta`; hidden when indeterminate                                |
| `valueLabel`                    | `ReactNode`                                      |            | The spoken value (`aria-valuetext`). Pass it when `meta` says more than a percentage               |
| `formatOptions`                 | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                       | percent    | Formatting of the automatic value text                                                             |
| `tone`                          | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'accent'` | Fill color                                                                                         |

Other React Aria props, `className` and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Built on React Aria: `role`, name, `aria-valuetext` and the label wiring come from it. The handoff `div role="progressbar"` had no name.
- Indeterminate mode, `valueLabel`, `showValue` and `Meter` are new.
- Width changes use the motion tokens and are disabled under reduced motion. Height and sweep settings are component tokens (`--ds-progress-*`).
- `Progress` no longer takes a `style` prop.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
MenuTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton    aria-haspopup=true, aria-expanded
  Popover            raised surface, radius lg, overlay shadow, z popover
    Menu             role=menu, named by the trigger (aria-labelledby)
      MenuItem       role=menuitem | menuitemcheckbox | menuitemradio, height --ds-item-h
        indicator    check / dot (selectable menus)
        label
        shortcut     mono hint, optional
        chevron      when it opens a SubMenu
      MenuSection    role=group, caption optional (mono uppercase)
      MenuSeparator  1px line
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`Menu`

| Prop                                      | Type                               | Default        | Notes                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                                 | `ReactElement`                     | none           | A `Button` or `IconButton`. Its name becomes the menu's. |
| `children`                                | `ReactNode`                        | none           | Items, sections, separators, submenus.                   |
| `placement`                               | React Aria `Placement`             | `bottom start` | Flips on collision.                                      |
| `onAction`                                | `(key) => void`                    |                | Called for plain items with their `id`.                  |
| `selectionMode`                           | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'` | `none`         | `single` = radio items, `multiple` = checkbox items.     |
| `selectedKeys` / `defaultSelectedKeys`    | `Selection`                        |                | Controlled / uncontrolled selection.                     |
| `onSelectionChange`                       | `(keys) => void`                   |                |                                                          |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                    |                | Controlled / uncontrolled open state.                    |

`MenuItem`: `id`, `children` (label), `tone` (`neutral` | `danger`), `shortcut`, `isDisabled`, `onAction`, `href`, `textValue`.
`MenuSection`: `title` (caption and accessible name), own `selectionMode` for a radio group inside a command menu.
`SubMenu`: `label`, `children`, `textValue`, `isDisabled`, `delay`.
`MoreActionsMenu`: a `Menu` with an `IconButton` (ellipsis) trigger named "More actions" from the catalog; `size`, `messages`, default placement `bottom end`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
Keyboard contract (AGENTS.md section 8):

| Key                                     | Behavior                                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` (trigger) | Opens the menu and focuses the first item                       |
| `ArrowUp` (trigger)                     | Opens the menu and focuses the last item                        |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`                 | Move between items; disabled items are skipped                  |
| `Home` / `End`                          | First / last item                                               |
| Typing                                  | Typeahead: focus moves to the item whose label starts with it   |
| `Enter` / `Space`                       | Activates the item (checkbox and radio items toggle) and closes |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft`              | Open / close a submenu (mirrored in right-to-left)              |
| `Escape`                                | Closes one level; focus returns to the trigger                  |

components.name: NavItem
components.description:
One entry of a navigation list. A real link when it has an `href`, a button when it only has
`onPress`. The active item is marked with `aria-current="page"`, a raised background and a
2px ink bar at the start edge.

props.name: children
props.description: Label: a noun in sentence case ("Orders"). Truncated with an ellipsis when it does not fit.

props.name: href
props.description:
Destination. With `href` the item is a real link (`<a>`) and navigates through the router
set on `DSProvider`. Without it the item is a `<button>` that runs `onPress`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon from the curated set, drawn at 18px before the label. Decorative.

props.name: isActive
props.description:
Marks the item for the page or view being shown: sets `aria-current="page"`, the raised
background and the 2px ink bar. Exactly one item of a navigation should be active.

props.name: count
props.description:
A count shown in a pill at the end of the item. `0` shows no pill. Numbers are formatted
for the active locale.

props.name: countLabel
props.description:
The text a screen reader hears instead of the bare number, with what is being counted
("3 pending", "12 unread"). Always set it together with `count`; without it a generic
"Count: 3" from the message catalog is used.

props.name: countTone
props.description:
Tone of the count pill. Color never carries the meaning alone: `countLabel` does.
Default `neutral`.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<a>` (with `href`) or `<button>` element.

props.name: render
props.type: (props: DetailedHTMLProps<LinkWithRequiredHref, HTMLAnchorElement> | DetailedHTMLProps<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, HTMLSpanElement>, renderProps: LinkRenderProps) => ReactElement<...>

keys.description: Spoken text for a count when the consumer gives no `countLabel`.

items.name: ZeroCountHidden
items.description: A count of 0 shows no pill.

items.name: RouterNavigation
items.description: With DSProvider routing, pressing the link calls navigate instead of reloading the page.

docs.summary:
One entry of a navigation list: a real link (or a button) with an optional icon and count. Built on React Aria `Link` and `Button`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/NavItem.jsx` (TODO `CMP-NAV-03`).
whenToUse: Inside the `Sidebar`, or any vertical navigation list.
To go to a page or view (with `href`), or to run a navigation-like command such as "Log out" (with `onPress`).
whenNotToUse: For actions inside a page: use `Button`.
For switching panels on a page: use `Tabs`.
For a link inside text: use `Link`.
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` to focus; `Enter` follows a link; `Enter` and `Space` press a button.
examples:
<nav aria-label="Main">
  <NavItem
    href="/orders"
    icon={StarIcon}
    isActive
    count={3}
    countLabel="3 pending"
    countTone="warning"
  >
    Orders
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem href="/customers" icon={SearchIcon}>
    Customers
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem onPress={signOut}>Log out</NavItem>
</nav>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Inside the `Sidebar`, or any vertical navigation list.
- To go to a page or view (with `href`), or to run a navigation-like command such as "Log out" (with `onPress`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For actions inside a page: use `Button`.
- For switching panels on a page: use `Tabs`.
- For a link inside text: use `Link`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
a | button .root           (36px high, --ds-item-h)
  Icon                     (18px, optional, 0.7 opacity when inactive)
  label                    (truncates with an ellipsis)
  count                    (optional pill with tone)
    "3"                    (aria-hidden)
    "3 pending"            (visually hidden text alternative)
```

sections.heading: States
sections.content:
| State    | Look                                                                          | Semantics             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Rest     | transparent, `--ds-text-2`                                                    | link or button        |
| Hover    | raised background (`--ds-surface-raised`), ink text                           | none                  |
| Active   | raised background, ink text, 2px ink bar at the start edge, full-opacity icon | `aria-current="page"` |
| Focus    | accent ring                                                                   |                       |
| Disabled | `--ds-opacity-disabled`                                                       | `aria-disabled`       |

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                                                          | Default     | Notes                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`   | `ReactNode`                                                   | required    | The label.                                                                          |
| `href`       | `string`                                                      | none        | With it: a real `<a>` routed through `DSProvider`. Without it: a `<button>`.        |
| `icon`       | `IconComponent`                                               | none        | From the curated set. Drawn at `--ds-icon-md` (18px), decorative.                   |
| `isActive`   | `boolean`                                                     | `false`     | Sets `aria-current="page"` and the active look. One per navigation.                 |
| `count`      | `number \| string`                                            | none        | Pill at the end. `0` shows nothing. Numbers are formatted for the locale.           |
| `countLabel` | `string`                                                      | catalog     | Spoken text for the count ("3 pending"). Always set it; the fallback is "Count: 3". |
| `countTone`  | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | Tone of the pill.                                                                   |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`                                     | none        | Fired for both links and buttons.                                                   |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                                                     | `false`     |                                                                                     |
| `messages`   | `{ count?: (value: string) => string }`                       | catalog     | Per-instance override of the fallback count text (ADR-0005).                        |

`ref` points to the `<a>` or `<button>`. Other React Aria `Link` props (`target`, `routerOptions`, `aria-*`) pass through for links.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Real `<a href>` (or `<button>`), so opening in a new tab, copying the URL and screen reader link lists work. The handoff used `div role="link"` with no `href`.
- `aria-current="page"` on the active item, on links and on buttons.
- The count pill is not enough on its own: a screen reader hears the label then the text alternative ("Orders 3 pending"). Color (tone) is only reinforcement.
- Keys: `Tab` to focus; `Enter` follows a link; `Enter` and `Space` press a button.
- Contrast: label `--ds-text-2` on `--ds-bg`, ink on the raised surface. The pill text meets 4.5:1 on its soft background.
- Forced colors: the active bar and the pill border use system colors.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are nouns in sentence case: "Orders", "Customers". Long labels are truncated.
- `countLabel` states what is counted and its state: "3 pending", "12 unread".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<nav aria-label="Main">
  <NavItem
    href="/orders"
    icon={StarIcon}
    isActive
    count={3}
    countLabel="3 pending"
    countTone="warning"
  >
    Orders
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem href="/customers" icon={SearchIcon}>
    Customers
  </NavItem>
  <NavItem onPress={signOut}>Log out</NavItem>
</nav>
```

- Count pills have a text alternative and localized numbers.

components.name: NumberField
components.description:
A number field with minus and plus steppers (the handoff `Stepper`), built on React Aria
`NumberField`: a text `<input>` with `aria-roledescription="Number field"` (React Aria
deliberately drops `role="spinbutton"`: VoiceOver cannot focus a spin button with typed
text). You can type a value or step it: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` by `step`,
`PageUp` / `PageDown` like the arrows (React Aria has no larger step), `Home` / `End` to the
limits (when `minValue` / `maxValue` are set), the mouse wheel while focused, and press and hold on a button repeats.
The typed text is parsed with the locale of `DSProvider` (`1.234,5` in pt-BR) and committed on
blur or `Enter`; values are clamped to the limits and snapped to `step`.

`onChange` receives a number, `NaN` while the field is empty. For money use `CurrencyInput`.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control, linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for the label.

docs.summary: A number input with minus and plus steppers; the successor of the handoff `Stepper`. Built on React Aria `NumberField` (`Group`, `Input`, two `Button`s in the `decrement` / `increment` slots), styled like [Input](../Input/Input.md). Task: CMP-PAT-06.
whenToUse: A bounded or unbounded count or measure that users type or nudge: quantity, length, number of copies.
whenNotToUse: Money: `CurrencyInput` (integer minor units, currency formatting).
An approximate value on a range: `Slider`.
Digits that are an identifier (postal code, phone): `Input` with `mono`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - A bounded or unbounded count or measure that users type or nudge: quantity, length, number of copies.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Money: `CurrencyInput` (integer minor units, currency formatting).
- An approximate value on a range: `Slider`.
- Digits that are an identifier (postal code, phone): `Input` with `mono`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: `[ - ] [ value + suffix ] [ + ]`: three boxes of the same height (`sm` 32 / `md` 40 / `lg` 48). The middle box is the `Input` look (`--ds-line-control` border, focus ring, mono, centered); the steppers are `IconButton`s.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                          | Notes                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`                    | One is required.                                                                                     |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                  | RAC naming. `onChange` receives a `number`, `NaN` while the field is empty.                          |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`                                | Typed and stepped values are clamped and snapped to `step`.                                          |
| `formatOptions`                                               | `Intl.NumberFormat` options (`{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }`, `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`). |
| `suffix`                                                      | A visual unit after the number ("m", "pcs"). For a spoken unit use `formatOptions`.                  |
| `size`                                                        | `sm` / `md` (default) / `lg`; the steppers follow.                                                   |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                                 | As in `Input`.                                                                                       |
| `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | Standard. `name` submits the raw number (`1234.5`), not the formatted text.                          |
| `messages`                                                    | `decrease`, `increase`, `requiredMark`.                                                              |

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                       | Behavior                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`   | Step up / down                                                            |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`     | Same as the arrows (React Aria has no larger step)                        |
| `Home` / `End`            | `minValue` / `maxValue` (only when set)                                   |
| Typing                    | Parsed with the locale (`1.234,5` in pt-BR), committed on `Enter` or blur |
| Press and hold a stepper  | Repeats (React Aria)                                                      |
| Mouse wheel while focused | Steps                                                                     |

The input is a text input with `aria-roledescription="Number field"`: React Aria deliberately does not use `role="spinbutton"` because VoiceOver cannot focus a spin button that accepts typed text. The stepper buttons are named "Decrease" / "Increase" from messages and, through `aria-labelledby`, followed by the field label ("Increase Quantity"); they are out of the tab order (the input handles the keys) and disabled at the limits. The value is not a live region (RAC announces changes).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label with the noun ("Quantity"). Put the unit in `suffix` or `formatOptions`, not in the label. Error text says how to fix: "Enter a quantity between 0 and 10."

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<NumberField label="Quantity" name="quantity" defaultValue={1} minValue={1} maxValue={99} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `Stepper` became `NumberField`: direct typing, locale parsing, press-and-hold, min/max/step, form `name`, label wiring, description and error, sizes.
- The `aria-live` on the value was dropped.
- Button labels come from messages (en "Decrease" / "Increase", pt-BR "Diminuir" / "Aumentar").
- No `role="spinbutton"` (see Accessibility); the handoff `+` and `-` keys do not step.

components.name: Pagination
components.description:
Previous and next buttons, numbered page buttons with ellipses, and a text that says where
you are ("11–20 of 42", or "Page 2 of 5" when only the page count is known).

The text is a polite live region, so a screen reader announces the new range when the page
changes. The current page button has `aria-current="page"`. The buttons that cannot be used
(previous on page 1) are disabled; when pressing a button disables it, focus moves to the
current page button so it is never lost.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, 1-based (controlled).

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: Page shown first (uncontrolled). Default `1`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new page when the user picks one.

props.name: pageCount
props.description:
Number of pages. Optional when `total` and `pageSize` are given (then it is derived from
them). Default `1`.

props.name: total
props.description: Total number of items. With `pageSize` it enables the "1–10 of 42" range text.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Items per page.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ navLabel: string; previous: string; next: string; page: (page: string) => string; range: (from: string, to: string, total: string) => string; empty: string; pageOf: (page: string, count: string) => string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Accessible name of the pagination navigation landmark.
Accessible name of a page button; the button shows only the number.
Visible and announced range of items. All arguments are already formatted for the locale.
Visible and announced text when `total` is 0.
Visible and announced text when only the page count is known.

items.name: KeyboardNavigation
items.description: Tab reaches the buttons; Enter or Space pick a page and the range text updates.

items.name: FocusStaysAfterLastPage
items.description: Pressing Next on the second to last page disables it; focus moves to the current page.

docs.summary:
Previous and next buttons, numbered page buttons with ellipses and a text that says where you are ("11–20 of 42"). The list logic is a tested pure function, `getPageItems`.

- Handoff source: `components/data/Pagination.jsx` (TODO `CMP-DAT-02`).
whenToUse: Below a table or list that is split into pages on the server or the client.
whenNotToUse: For endless feeds: use a "Load more" `Button`.
For a handful of items that fit on one screen.
For moving through steps: use a stepper.
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` to move; `Enter` and `Space` press.
examples:
<Pagination total={42} pageSize={10} page={page} onChange={setPage} />

<Pagination pageCount={8} defaultPage={3} />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Below a table or list that is split into pages on the server or the client.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For endless feeds: use a "Load more" `Button`.
- For a handful of items that fit on one screen.
- For moving through steps: use a stepper.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  span[role=status, aria-live=polite]   "11–20 of 42"  or  "Page 2 of 5"
  nav[aria-label="Pagination"]
    ul
      li  IconButton  Previous page
      li  button      1    (aria-label "Page 1", aria-current="page" on the current one)
      li  …                (aria-hidden)
      li  IconButton  Next page
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                   | Type                     | Default | Notes                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page` / `defaultPage` | `number`                 | `1`     | Current page (1-based), controlled / uncontrolled. Clamped into range.                  |
| `onChange`             | `(page: number) => void` | none    | Called only when the page changes.                                                      |
| `pageCount`            | `number`                 | derived | Needed unless `total` and `pageSize` are given.                                         |
| `total`, `pageSize`    | `number`                 | none    | Together they enable the range text and derive `pageCount`.                             |
| `messages`             | partial catalog          | catalog | `navLabel`, `previous`, `next`, `page(n)`, `range(from, to, total)`, `empty`, `pageOf`. |

Exported helpers: `getPageItems(current, pageCount)`, `getPageCount(total, pageSize)`, `getItemRange(page, pageSize, total)`.

sections.heading: Page list algorithm
sections.content: Up to 7 pages every page is shown. Beyond that: the first page, the last page, the current page and its two neighbours; each gap becomes an ellipsis. A gap that would hide exactly one page shows that page instead (the handoff showed an ellipsis for it, which is wider than the page it hides). The page list never exceeds 7 slots.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `nav` named "Pagination" (from the catalog). Page buttons have `aria-label="Page 3"` and show only the number; the current one has `aria-current="page"`.
- The summary is a polite live region: when the page changes, a screen reader announces the new range ("11–20 of 42"). It is not announced on first render.
- Previous and next are disabled at the ends. When pressing one disables it, focus moves to the current page button, so focus is never lost to the page body.
- Ellipses are `aria-hidden` list items. In right-to-left locales the previous and next chevrons swap direction.
- Targets are 32px; page numbers are mono with tabular figures. Numbers are formatted for the locale ("1.248" in pt-BR).
- Keys: `Tab` to move; `Enter` and `Space` press.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Do not repeat the total elsewhere. Keep the labels from the catalog unless your product uses another word for the items ("rows", "orders").

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Pagination total={42} pageSize={10} page={page} onChange={setPage} />

<Pagination pageCount={8} defaultPage={3} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Labels, range and the page text come from the message catalog (the handoff was hard-coded pt-BR); numbers use `Intl`.
- Buttons are React Aria / `IconButton` components; hover and disabled are CSS; the disabled opacity is the shared token.
- `onChange` is only called for real changes; `page` can be controlled; focus is kept when an edge button becomes disabled.
- Not included yet: page size selector (P2).
