alternatives.reason: For endless feeds: use a "Load more" `Button`.

components.name: Popover
components.description:
A floating surface for interactive content (filters, a small form, a color picker), built on
React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `Popover` and `Dialog`.

It is not for lists of commands (use `Menu`), for choosing one option (use `Select`) or for
plain hints (use `Tooltip`). `Escape` and an outside press close it and focus returns to the
trigger; when the content has focusable elements, `Tab` stays inside until it is closed.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
The element that opens the popover: a `Button`, `IconButton` or any React Aria pressable.
It receives `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name of the popover (for example "Filters"). The popover is a `dialog`, so it
needs a name; a visible heading inside it can be linked with `aria-labelledby` instead.

props.name: children
props.description: Interactive content. A function receives `close` to dismiss the popover from inside.

props.name: placement
props.type: 'bottom' | 'bottom left' | 'bottom right' | 'bottom start' | 'bottom end' | 'top' | 'top left' | 'top right' | 'top start' | 'top end' | 'left' | 'left top' | 'left bottom' | 'start' | 'start top' | 'start bottom' | 'right' | 'right top' | 'right bottom' | 'end' | 'end top' | 'end bottom'
props.description: Side and alignment relative to the trigger. Default `bottom start`. Flips on collision.

props.name: showArrow
props.description: Draws an arrow that points at the trigger.

props.name: isNonModal
props.description:
Keeps the page outside the popover available to assistive technology and does not hide it.
Leave it off unless the popover is a long-lived tool the user returns to; React Aria's
guidance is that most popovers should stay modal for screen readers.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popover opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the popover surface.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the popover surface.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

docs.summary:
A floating surface that opens from a trigger and holds interactive content. Built on React Aria `DialogTrigger`, `Popover` and `Dialog`.

- Handoff source: `components/navigation/Popover` (CMP-NAV-04).
whenToUse: Filters, a small form, a date range, a color picker: content the user operates and then dismisses.
whenNotToUse: A list of commands: use `Menu`.
Choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
A hint on hover or focus: use `Tooltip`.
A decision that blocks the task: use `Dialog`.
keyboard: Keys: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens it and moves focus inside; `Tab` moves through the content; `Esc` closes it and focus returns to the trigger.
examples:
<Popover trigger={<Button>Filters</Button>} label="Filters" placement="bottom end">
  {({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Input label="Customer" />
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>
        Apply filters
      </Button>
    </>
  )}
</Popover>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Filters, a small form, a date range, a color picker: content the user operates and then dismisses.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A list of commands: use `Menu`.
- Choosing one option from a list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- A hint on hover or focus: use `Tooltip`.
- A decision that blocks the task: use `Dialog`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
DialogTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton            aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, aria-controls
  Popover            raised surface, strong line, radius lg, overlay shadow, z popover
    OverlayArrow     optional
    Dialog           role=dialog, aria-label = label
      children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                     | Type                                    | Default        | Notes                                                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                | `ReactElement`                          | none           | A `Button`, `IconButton` or other React Aria pressable. |
| `label`                  | `string` (required)                     | none           | Accessible name of the dialog.                          |
| `children`               | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` | none           | Interactive content.                                    |
| `placement`              | React Aria `Placement`                  | `bottom start` | Flips when there is no room.                            |
| `showArrow`              | `boolean`                               | `false`        | Arrow pointing at the trigger.                          |
| `isNonModal`             | `boolean`                               | `false`        | See Accessibility.                                      |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean`                               |                | Controlled / uncontrolled.                              |
| `onOpenChange`           | `(isOpen: boolean) => void`             |                |                                                         |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The handoff used a `span` with a click handler and no ARIA.
- The surface is a `dialog` named by `label`. A menu is **not** a dialog: use `Menu` for commands.
- Keys: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens it and moves focus inside; `Tab` moves through the content; `Esc` closes it and focus returns to the trigger.
- Outside press closes it. React Aria hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open (`isNonModal` turns that off; React Aria recommends it only for long-lived tool popovers).
- Focus is restored to the trigger on close.
- Placement is collision-aware. Forced colors: the arrow uses `CanvasText`/`Canvas`.
- Layer: `--ds-z-popover`. A popover opened from inside a `Dialog` or `Sheet` sits **below** them in the current z-index scale (see the Dialog doc, "Layers").

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- `label` is a noun phrase: "Filters", "Date range".
- Put the confirming action inside the content ("Apply filters"); verb plus object.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Popover trigger={<Button>Filters</Button>} label="Filters" placement="bottom end">
  {({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Input label="Customer" />
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>
        Apply filters
      </Button>
    </>
  )}
</Popover>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Real positioning with collision handling instead of `position: absolute` offsets.
- `role` is `dialog` with a name; ARIA attributes on the trigger; focus moves in and returns.
- Outside press and `Escape` are handled by React Aria (the handoff used `mousedown` and a window `keydown` listener per instance).
- The handoff's `width` and `style` props are gone: size the content, not the surface.

components.name: Progress
components.description:
A thin bar for a task that makes progress: determinate with a `value`, or indeterminate
when the amount is unknown. Built on React Aria `ProgressBar` (`role="progressbar"`).
For a measured quantity that is not a task (disk used, quota) use `Meter`.

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label, wired to the bar with `aria-labelledby`. Required unless you set `aria-label`
or `aria-labelledby`: a bar without a name is an accessibility bug (React Aria warns in development).

props.name: meta
props.description:
Text on the right of the label, in mono type: "6.2 / 10 GB". It is visual only. If it says
more than the percentage, also pass `valueLabel` so screen readers hear the same thing.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the formatted percentage (`62%`, from `Intl` with the active locale) as `meta` when `meta` is not given.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color of the fill. Color is never the only signal: pair it with a label or `meta`. Default `accent`.

docs.summary: A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.
whenToUse: `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
`Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.
whenNotToUse: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.
examples:
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
- `Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                            | Type                                             | Default    | Notes                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                         | `number`                                         | `0`        | Clamped to the range                                                                               |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`          | `number`                                         | `0`, `100` |                                                                                                    |
| `isIndeterminate`               | `boolean` (`Progress` only)                      |            | No `aria-valuenow`; the fill sweeps                                                                |
| `label`                         | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visible label, wired as the accessible name                                                        |
| `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                         |            | Use when there is no visible label. One of the three is required (React Aria warns in development) |
| `meta`                          | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visual text on the right ("6.2 / 10 GB")                                                           |
| `showValue`                     | `boolean`                                        | `false`    | Shows the formatted percentage as `meta`; hidden when indeterminate                                |
| `valueLabel`                    | `ReactNode`                                      |            | The spoken value (`aria-valuetext`). Pass it when `meta` says more than a percentage               |
| `formatOptions`                 | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                       | percent    | Formatting of the automatic value text                                                             |
| `tone`                          | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'accent'` | Fill color                                                                                         |

Other React Aria props, `className` and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Built on React Aria: `role`, name, `aria-valuetext` and the label wiring come from it. The handoff `div role="progressbar"` had no name.
- Indeterminate mode, `valueLabel`, `showValue` and `Meter` are new.
- Width changes use the motion tokens and are disabled under reduced motion. Height and sweep settings are component tokens (`--ds-progress-*`).
- `Progress` no longer takes a `style` prop.

alternatives.name: Spinner
alternatives.reason: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.

alternatives.name: Skeleton
alternatives.reason: Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

components.name: ProportionBar
components.description:
A single bar split into the parts of a whole (payment methods, composition). It is an image
with a text summary ("Payment methods: Pix 47%, Cash 16%…"), and an optional legend with the
percentage and the value of each part.

Neutral by default: signal colors are not used for categories. Parts are separated by a
gap, and beyond four parts the ramp repeats with a hatch so they never look alike.

props.name: segments
props.description:
The parts of the whole, in display order. Without `color` they use a neutral ramp of four
steps (`text`, `text-2`, `text-3`, `line-control`); from the fifth part on, the ramp
repeats with a hatch pattern so no two parts look the same (up to eight; group the tail
into "Other" or give explicit colors beyond that). The bar never sorts.

props.name: label
props.description: Name of the whole ("Payment methods"). It starts the summary read for the bar.

props.name: legend
props.description: Shows a list under the bar with swatch, label, percentage and formatted value for each part.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats each value in the legend. Default: `formatNumber` with the active locale. Use `formatCurrency` for money.

props.name: percentDigits
props.description: Decimals of the percentages in the summary and the legend. Default `0`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ segment: (label: string, percent: string) => string; summary: (items: string, label?: string) => string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: One segment in the summary read for the bar: "Cash 16%". Both arguments are already formatted.
The whole summary. `items` is the list of segments joined for the locale ("Cash 16%, Card 11% and Pix 73%"); `label` names the bar, if given.

items.name: Default
items.description: The bar is an image named by a text summary, so the percentages are never only visual.

items.name: EightParts
items.description: Beyond four parts the neutral ramp repeats with a hatch, so no two parts look alike (up to eight).

items.name: ExplicitColors
items.description: Explicit colors are for when the neutral ramp is not enough; the legend still names every part.

items.name: PortugueseBrazil

docs.summary: One bar split into the parts of a whole (payment methods, composition), with a text summary for assistive technology and an optional legend with the percentage and value of each part.
whenToUse: Showing how a total divides into a few parts (2 to 8) at a glance.
Next to or inside a `StatCard`.
whenNotToUse: Progress of a task: use `Progress`. A quantity within a range: use `Meter`.
Comparing separate values or many categories: use `Chart` or `RankList`.
Exact figures the user must read: show the legend (or a table).

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Showing how a total divides into a few parts (2 to 8) at a glance.
- Next to or inside a `StatCard`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Progress of a task: use `Progress`. A quantity within a range: use `Meter`.
- Comparing separate values or many categories: use `Chart` or `RankList`.
- Exact figures the user must read: show the legend (or a table).

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  div[role=img][aria-label="Payment methods: Pix 53%, Cash 18%…"]   the track, 10px, pill radius
    div  one segment per non-zero part (flex share = its share of the whole, 2px gap)
  ul (legend, optional)
    li  swatch (aria-hidden) · label · percentage · value
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop            | Type                         | Default | Notes                                                                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `segments`      | `{ label, value, color? }[]` | -       | Display order; never sorted. Negative and non-finite values count as 0 |
| `label`         | `string`                     |         | Name of the whole; starts the summary                                  |
| `legend`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | List with swatch, label, percentage and formatted value                |
| `format`        | `(value) => ReactNode`       | `Intl`  | Formats legend values. Use `formatCurrency` for money                  |
| `percentDigits` | `number`                     | `0`     | Decimals of the percentages                                            |
| `messages`      | `Partial<messages>`          |         | `segment(label, percent)`, `summary(items, label?)`                    |

sections.heading: Distinguishing the parts
sections.content:
Neutral by default: signal colors are not used for categories.

- The ramp has four solid steps: `text`, `text-2`, `text-3`, `line-control`. All reach 3:1 against the track background.
- Neighbours are always separated by a 2px gap.
- From the fifth part on, the ramp **repeats with a diagonal hatch**, so up to eight parts look different. This is the only place a gradient is used, as a pattern, not as decoration.
- Beyond eight parts, group the smallest into "Other" or pass explicit `color`s. In development a warning appears when more than eight parts have no color.
- Even so, the legend and the summary carry the identity of every part; the fill only helps sighted users.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The bar is `role="img"` with an `aria-label` that lists every part with its percentage: "Payment methods: Pix 53%, Cash 18%, Debit 17%, and Credit 11%". The list is joined with `Intl.ListFormat` for the locale; the per-part text comes from messages.
- The legend is a real list. It repeats the summary on purpose: it is the content sighted users read, and it stays available when you need more than the bar.
- Zero parts are listed in the legend (with 0%) but not drawn.
- Forced colors: segments use system colors (`CanvasText`, `GrayText`, `LinkText`, `Highlight`) and the track gets a border.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Part labels are short nouns ("Cash", "Pix"); the whole gets a label when the bar is not obvious from context.
- Percentages are rounded; they may not add up to exactly 100%. Use `percentDigits` if that matters.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<ProportionBar
  label="Payment methods"
  legend
  format={(value) => formatCurrency(value, 'USD', locale)}
  segments={[
    { label: 'Pix', value: 1693000 },
    { label: 'Cash', value: 573400 },
    { label: 'Debit', value: 538800 },
    { label: 'Credit', value: 359600 },
  ]}
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A text alternative: `role="img"` with a summary; the handoff relied on `title` tooltips.
- The ramp's fourth step is `line-control` (3:1) instead of `line-strong`, and parts beyond four are hatched instead of repeating the same four colors.
- `height` is a token (`--ds-proportion-bar-height`), not a prop; `RAMP` is not exported.
- Legend values and percentages use `Intl`; the legend is a list.
- Segment widths use a flex share, so they are exact even when values are fractions.

docs.summary: A labelled set of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` + `RadioField` + `RadioButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description per option). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).
whenToUse: Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options that users want to compare.
whenNotToUse: Many options: `Select`.
Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
Immediate on/off: `Switch`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options that users want to compare.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Many options: `Select`.
- Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Immediate on/off: `Switch`.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
`RadioGroup`:

| Prop                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                               | Group name. Required: pass `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise; development warning too). |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                         | Linked to the group by `aria-describedby`.                                                                             |
| `orientation`                                         | `vertical` (default) or `horizontal`.                                                                                  |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`          | React Aria naming; `value` is a string.                                                                                |
| `name`                                                | Shared by every radio; the selected value is submitted.                                                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | Standard states.                                                                                                       |

`Radio`: `value` (required), `label`, `description`, `isDisabled`, `className`, `inputRef`.

sections.heading: Look
sections.content:
- 18px circle (`--ds-radio-size`), `--ds-line-control` border at 3:1 or better in every state, accent border and a 9px accent dot when selected. Hover brightens the border.
- The option row is at least 24px tall and the whole row is clickable.
- A disabled group dims once; a single disabled option uses `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                        | Behavior                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                      | One tab stop: lands on the selected radio, or the first one when nothing is selected            |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` | Next radio, selects it, wraps from the last to the first (directions follow the text direction) |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft`    | Previous radio, selects it, wraps                                                               |
| `Space`                    | Selects the focused radio                                                                       |

Roving focus is handled by React Aria, so only one radio is in the tab order (the handoff made every radio tabbable). `role="radiogroup"` is named by the label; the description and error belong to the group; `aria-required` and `aria-invalid` are set.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Region"
  name="region"
  defaultValue="eu"
  description="You cannot change this later."
>
  <Radio value="eu" label="EU: Frankfurt" />
  <Radio value="us" label="US: Virginia" description="Default for new workspaces." />
</RadioGroup>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Native radios with roving focus replace `div role="radio"` with a tab stop each; the group is labelled, can be required or invalid, and has a description and error.
- Options are `Radio` children instead of an `options` array (a description per option is possible); `direction="row"` is `orientation="horizontal"`, and the default is vertical.
- `onChange(value)` and `value` follow React Aria.

components.name: RankList
components.description:
An ordered list of items with a value, a bar relative to the largest value and an optional
detail. Rows can be plain or buttons.

The list renders the items as given; pass `sort` and `limit` for a "top N". Put it in a
`Card` with `padding="none"`.

props.name: items
props.description:
The rows, rendered **in the order given** unless `sort` is set. This differs from the
handoff, which always sorted descending and kept only six rows: sorting and truncating
silently changes the data, so both are opt-in.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the list ("Top products"). Optional: a list inside a titled `Card` is already named by it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the list.

props.name: sort
props.description: Sorts by `value` (`desc` largest first, `asc` smallest first) before `limit` is applied. Ties keep their input order.

props.name: limit
props.description: Shows only the first `limit` rows (after `sort`). Default: all rows.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats each value. Default: `formatNumber` with the active locale; use `formatCurrency` for money.

props.name: showPosition
props.description: Shows the position (1, 2, 3...) before each row. The list is ordered either way. Default `true`.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content when there are no rows. Default: the "No data for this period" message.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Text shown when there are no items.

items.name: Default
items.description: Ranked data, largest first. Rows render in the order given: the list never re-sorts or truncates on its own.

items.name: GivenOrder
items.description: Without `sort`, unsorted data keeps its given order (here: insertion order).

items.name: SortedAndLimited
items.description: `sort` and `limit` are opt-in: a "top 3" by value.

items.name: Actionable
items.description: Rows with `onAction` are buttons: Tab reaches them, Enter or Space press.

items.name: BarsAlign
items.description: Bars of different rows share one column grid, so their lengths can be compared by eye.

docs.summary: An ordered list of items with a value, a bar relative to the largest value and an optional detail. Rows can be plain or buttons. Meant to sit inside a `Card` without body padding.
whenToUse: "Top products", "best customers", "colors by sales": a short ranking with comparable values.
whenNotToUse: Several columns, sorting by the user, selection: use `DataTable`.
Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
A trend over time: use `Chart`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - "Top products", "best customers", "colors by sales": a short ranking with comparable values.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Several columns, sorting by the user, selection: use `DataTable`.
- Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.
- A trend over time: use `Chart`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root
  ol (role=list)
    li > div | button     grid, shared columns for all rows (subgrid)
      position            decorative number (aria-hidden); the ol already numbers the items
      label               optional swatch (aria-hidden) + text, truncated
      value               mono, formatted
      bar                 4px track + fill, relative to the largest value (aria-hidden)
      meta                mono detail, optional
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                   | Default | Notes                                                                       |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`        | `RankItem[]`           | -       | `id`, `label`, `value`, `meta`, `swatch`, `onAction`. Rendered **as given** |
| `sort`         | `asc \| desc`          |         | Opt-in sort by value (stable ties)                                          |
| `limit`        | `number`               |         | Opt-in truncation, applied after `sort`                                     |
| `format`       | `(value) => ReactNode` | `Intl`  | Use `formatCurrency` for money                                              |
| `showPosition` | `boolean`              | `true`  | Numbers 1, 2, 3 of the rows shown                                           |
| `emptyState`   | `ReactNode`            |         | Default: "No data for this period" (messages)                               |
| `aria-label`   | `string`               |         | Optional name of the list                                                   |
| `messages`     | `Partial<messages>`    |         | `empty`                                                                     |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A real ordered list (`ol`, explicit `role="list"` so Safari keeps the semantics with `list-style: none`).
- Rows with `onAction` are `<button>`s (React Aria `Button`): Tab, Enter, Space. Their name is the label followed by the value; position, bar and swatch are hidden from assistive technology.
- The bar and swatch are decorative: the value (and `meta`) carry the information as text.
- Bars of all rows share one grid, so their lengths are comparable.
- Text colors: label `text`, meta `text-2` (stays above 4.5:1 on hover); focus is an inset accent outline (system color in forced colors).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are names, not sentences. Meta is short and mono: `12 units · 18%`.
- Use this for things (products, colors, customers). Give customers an `onAction` that opens the profile.

sections.heading: Example
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- **No silent sorting or truncation.** The handoff always sorted descending and kept six rows; here the items render as given, and `sort` / `limit` are opt-in props. Migrating: add `sort="desc" limit={6}`.
- An ordered list instead of `div`s; actionable rows are buttons instead of `div role="button"`; `it.onClick` is `onAction`.
- Empty text comes from messages (the Portuguese default is gone); `showPos` is `showPosition`.
- The swatch is the core `Swatch` (`decorative`, size `sm`); it takes a hex color.
- Bars align across rows (subgrid), values and positions use `Intl`.

alternatives.name: ProportionBar
alternatives.reason: Parts of a whole: use `ProportionBar`.

alternatives.name: Chart
alternatives.reason: A trend over time: use `Chart`.

components.name: Rating
components.description:
A read-only star rating. It is a single image (`role="img"`) with a text alternative such
as "3.5 out of 5 stars"; the stars themselves are decorative. Half stars are supported.

It does not accept input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics and is not part
of the design system yet.

props.name: value
props.description:
The rating to show, from 0 to `max`. Values are clamped and rounded to the nearest half
star ("3.7" shows three and a half stars, and says "3.5 out of 5 stars").

props.name: max
props.description: Number of stars. A whole number from 1. Default `5`.

props.name: size
props.description: Star size token: `sm` 12px, `md` 14px (default), `lg` 18px.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Also shows the value as text ("3.5/5") after the stars. Hidden from assistive technology: the name already says it.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ label: (value: string, max: string, maxCount: number) => string; }>
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

keys.description: Accessible name of the rating. Arguments are already formatted for the locale.

docs.summary:
A read-only star rating, such as a review score. One image with a text alternative ("3.5 out of 5 stars"); half stars are supported.

- Handoff source: `components/display/Rating` (TODO `CMP-DSP-06`).
whenToUse: Show a score someone else gave (a review, a quality grade).
Next to the review text in lists and cards, optionally with the numeric value.
whenNotToUse: To collect a rating: it takes no input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`) and is out of scope for now; use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` with labelled options meanwhile.
For an average with a distribution or a trend: use `Chart` or `ProportionBar`.
examples:
<Rating value={4} />
<Rating value={3.5} showValue size="lg" />
<Rating value={7} max={10} />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Show a score someone else gave (a review, a quality grade).
- Next to the review text in lists and cards, optionally with the numeric value.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To collect a rating: it takes no input. An interactive rating needs radio-group semantics (one tab stop, arrows, `Space`) and is out of scope for now; use `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` with labelled options meanwhile.
- For an average with a distribution or a trend: use `Chart` or `ProportionBar`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span[role=img][aria-label="3.5 out of 5 stars"]
  stars (aria-hidden)
    star x max      empty glyph + clipped filled glyph (0, 50 or 100 %)
  value             optional "3.5/5" (aria-hidden)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                   | Default  | Notes                                                         |
| ----------- | ---------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `number`               | required | Clamped to `0..max`, rounded to the nearest half star.        |
| `max`       | `number`               | `5`      | Number of stars (whole number, at least 1).                   |
| `size`      | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`   | Star size: 12, 14 and 18 px (icon tokens).                    |
| `showValue` | `boolean`              | `false`  | Adds "3.5/5" in mono text after the stars.                    |
| `messages`  | `{ label }`            |          | Override the accessible name (`label(value, max, maxCount)`). |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `role="img"` with an `aria-label` from messages; the glyphs and the visible value are `aria-hidden`, so the rating is announced once.
- The label is pluralized by the scale (`1 out of 1 star`, `3.5 out of 5 stars`) and numbers follow the locale (`3,5 de 5 estrelas` in pt-BR).
- The value is not carried by color alone: the label and the optional value text state the number. The empty star uses `--ds-line-control` (3:1 against the surfaces); filled uses `--ds-warning`.
- Forced colors: filled stars use `CanvasText`, empty ones `GrayText`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Show the number next to the stars when the exact value matters; stars alone are fine in dense lists.
- Pair a rating with the review it belongs to; do not leave it alone in a row of badges.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Rating value={4} />
<Rating value={3.5} showValue size="lg" />
<Rating value={7} max={10} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Half stars are displayed (the handoff rounded to whole stars).
- The label comes from messages, is pluralized and localized (it was hard-coded pt-BR).
- Stars are the bundled Lucide `Star` icon drawn with a CSS fill, not the text glyph; sizes are icon tokens.
- Documented decision: read-only. Interactive rating is a separate future component.
- Filled icons are normally avoided (AGENTS.md section 7); the star is the one exception because filled versus empty is the meaning.

components.name: RequiredMark
components.description:
The visible marker of a required field, text from messages. Hidden from assistive technology:
the control announces "required" itself. Use it when a field cannot use `Label`
(for example inside a `Checkbox` label).

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

keys.description: Visible marker after the label of a required field. Hidden from assistive technology.

items.name: Anatomy
items.description: The building blocks composed by hand inside a React Aria field. Prefer the ready-made fields.

items.name: ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt
items.description:
Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

items.name: RealtimeValidation
items.description: The alternative: `validationBehavior="aria"` reports problems while the user types. Use sparingly.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language. A static `errorMessage` replaces only that browser text: a message the app supplied (a `validate` rule or `validationErrors` on a `Form`) is shown instead (GAP-009).
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

components.name: ResponseFeedback
components.description:
Feedback and follow-up actions under an assistant response: two toggle buttons (good and bad
response, `aria-pressed`), then optional Copy and Regenerate.

Choosing a rating is reversible, so nothing asks to confirm: pressing the active rating again
removes it. A polite live region says "Feedback sent" or "Feedback removed" after the change.
The first render never announces anything. The buttons show text only for now: thumbs, copy
and refresh icons are not part of the curated icon set yet.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled rating. `null` means no rating.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial rating when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new rating, or `null` when the person takes their rating back.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Called when Copy is pressed. Without it there is no Copy button. Confirm with a toast ("Copied").

props.name: onRegenerate
props.description: Called when Regenerate is pressed. Without it there is no Regenerate button.

props.name: isRegenerating
props.description: Disables Regenerate while a new response is being generated.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every button.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ groupLabel: string; positive: string; negative: string; copy: string; regenerate: string; sent: string; removed: string; }>
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

keys.description: Accessible name of the group of rating buttons.
Toggle buttons; pressed means the rating is set.
Action buttons (verb plus object).
Polite announcements after a rating changes.

docs.summary: Feedback and follow-up actions under an assistant response: good and bad response toggles, then optional Copy and Regenerate. Import it from `@loui/ds/patterns`.
whenToUse: Under each assistant response in a `ChatPanel`, to learn which answers help.
whenNotToUse: Collecting a written review or a star rating: use `Rating` in a form.
Anything that sends the rating somewhere the owner cannot see: say where it goes in your product.
keyboard: The rating buttons are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) in a labelled group. Each is a tab stop; `Space` and `Enter` press.

sections.content: - Under each assistant response in a `ChatPanel`, to learn which answers help.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Collecting a written review or a star rating: use `Rating` in a form.
- Anything that sends the rating somewhere the owner cannot see: say where it goes in your product.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div
  group "Rate this response"   toggle "Good response" · toggle "Bad response"   (aria-pressed)
  button "Copy response"       only with onCopy
  button "Regenerate response" only with onRegenerate
  status                       visually hidden live region
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                     | Type                               | Default | Notes                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `'positive' \| 'negative' \| null` | `null`  | Controlled or uncontrolled rating.                                             |
| `onChange`               | `(value \| null) => void`          |         | `null` when the person takes the rating back.                                  |
| `onCopy`                 | `() => void`                       |         | Shows Copy. Copy the text yourself, then confirm with a toast.                 |
| `onRegenerate`           | `() => void`                       |         | Shows Regenerate.                                                              |
| `isRegenerating`         | `boolean`                          | `false` | Disables Regenerate while the new response is generated.                       |
| `isDisabled`             | `boolean`                          | `false` | Disables every button.                                                         |
| `messages`               | partial catalog                    |         | `groupLabel`, `positive`, `negative`, `copy`, `regenerate`, `sent`, `removed`. |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The rating buttons are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) in a labelled group. Each is a tab stop; `Space` and `Enter` press.
- Rating is reversible, so nothing asks to confirm: pressing the active button again removes the rating.
- A polite live region says "Feedback sent" or "Feedback removed" after a change. It is silent on first render.
- Each control shows a decorative icon (`ThumbsUpIcon`, `ThumbsDownIcon`, `CopyIcon`, `RefreshIcon`) next to its visible text label; the text is the accessible name.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Buttons are verb plus object ("Copy response", "Regenerate response").
- Confirm Copy with a short past-tense toast ("Copied"), outside this pattern.
- Regenerate replaces content: offer Undo, as for any reversible action.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.description:
A scrolling container with thin, themed scrollbars. It scrolls inside the space its parent
gives it: give it a height (or put it in a flex column and let it shrink).

While its content overflows it becomes a keyboard stop (`tabindex="0"`) and a labelled
`region`, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys (WCAG 2.1.1). When nothing
overflows it is a plain container, with no tab stop and no landmark. A name is therefore
always required.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which axes scroll. Default `vertical`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the region ("Order history").

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the region.

items.name: Default
items.description: Overflowing content: the area is a labelled region and a keyboard stop. Press Tab, then PageDown (the browser test covers the scrolling itself).

items.name: NotScrollable
items.description: Nothing overflows: a plain container, no tab stop and no landmark.

docs.summary: A scrolling container with thin, themed scrollbars that stays keyboard accessible.
whenToUse: A bounded list, log or panel inside a page: a notification list, a long form step, a code output.
A region that must scroll on its own while the page around it does not.
whenNotToUse: For the page itself: let the document scroll, or use `AppShell`'s `main`.
For a table: `DataTable` has its own horizontal scroll and sticky parts.
Inside a Dialog or Sheet body: those already scroll their body.
keyboard: Arrow keys, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End` scroll it natively.
examples: {events.map(renderEvent)}

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A bounded list, log or panel inside a page: a notification list, a long form step, a code output.
- A region that must scroll on its own while the page around it does not.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For the page itself: let the document scroll, or use `AppShell`'s `main`.
- For a table: `DataTable` has its own horizontal scroll and sticky parts.
- Inside a Dialog or Sheet body: those already scroll their body.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (overflow auto, scrollbar-width: thin)
  div (content wrapper, observed for size changes)
    children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                             | Type                                   | Default      | Notes                                             |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` | `string`                               | **required** | One of them. It names the region while it scrolls |
| `orientation`                    | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | Which axes scroll                                 |

Other `div` attributes (not `role`, `tabIndex`) and `ref` go to the root. Give the area a height, or put it in a flex column and let it shrink; it scrolls inside the space its parent gives it.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A scroll container must be reachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1). While the content overflows, the area gets `tabindex="0"` and `role="region"` with your label; with nothing to scroll it is a plain container (no tab stop, no landmark). A `ResizeObserver` keeps this in sync as content or size changes.
- Because focusability is dynamic, the type always requires a name, so a scrollable area is never unlabelled.
- Arrow keys, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End` scroll it natively.
- The focus ring is drawn inside the box, so a clipping parent cannot hide it.
- Scrollbars are the browser's thin scrollbars colored with `--ds-line-control` (3:1 on the background); on hover they brighten to `--ds-text-3`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Name it for what it holds: "Order history", "Activity", not "Scrollable area".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
{events.map(renderEvent)}
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff scrolled with unlabelled `overflow: auto` divs that keyboard users could not reach. Scrollbar colors come from tokens.

components.name: SearchInput
components.description:
A search box: leading search icon, clear button (and `Escape` clears), optional decorative
shortcut hint, optional suggestions with accent-insensitive match highlighting. Built on React
Aria `SearchField` (plain) or `ComboBox` (with `suggestions`).

`onSubmit(text)` fires on `Enter` when no suggestion is highlighted.

props.name: value
props.description: The text. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial text when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new text on every keystroke and when it is cleared.

props.name: suggestions
props.description:
Suggestions shown under the box while typing, matched accent- and case-insensitively against
`label` with the matching part highlighted. Strings are shorthand for `{ label }`. Without
this prop the component is a plain search field (`role="searchbox"`); with it the input is a
combobox (`role="combobox"`). Keep the array order: it is the order shown.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a suggestion is chosen (click or `Enter` on the highlighted one).

props.name: maxResults
props.description: Most suggestions shown. Default `6`.

props.name: shortcut
props.description:
A decorative hint of the global shortcut that focuses the search (`['Mod', 'K']`, `['/']`),
drawn with `Kbd` while the box is empty. It does not register the shortcut: use
`useHotkey` and focus `inputRef` yourself. Hidden from assistive technology, since the hint
is only useful when the shortcut exists; announce it with `aria-keyshortcuts` if it does.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the box is empty. Default from messages: "Search".

props.name: landmark
props.description:
Wraps the field in a `role="search"` landmark named by the label. Use it once per page for
the main search of a page or site; not for filters inside a table.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: popoverClassName
props.description: Class name for the popover that holds the suggestions.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ clear: string; placeholder: string; noResults: string; } & { requiredMark: string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `clear`, `placeholder`, `noResults`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

keys.description: Accessible name of the clear button.
Placeholder when none is given.
Shown in the suggestions list when nothing matches the text.

docs.summary: A search box: leading search icon, clear button, optional decorative shortcut hint and optional suggestions with accent-insensitive match highlighting. Built on React Aria `SearchField` (plain) or `ComboBox` (with `suggestions`). Task: CMP-INP-06.
whenToUse: Searching a list, a table or the app, with or without suggestions.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a value from a list: `Combobox` (it keeps a selected value; SearchInput keeps free text).
Filters with several fields: compose `Input`, `Select`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Searching a list, a table or the app, with or without suggestions.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Choosing a value from a list: `Combobox` (it keeps a selected value; SearchInput keeps free text).
- Filters with several fields: compose `Input`, `Select`.

sections.heading: Modes
sections.content:
| Mode               | Element                                  | Notes                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain (default)    | `input[type=search]`, `role="searchbox"` | Clear button; `Escape` clears; `onSubmit(text)` on `Enter`.                                                                                                |
| With `suggestions` | `role="combobox"`                        | List under the box while there is text. `Escape` closes the list, then clears. `Enter` on a highlighted suggestion calls `onSelect`; otherwise `onSubmit`. |

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `aria-label` / `label` / `aria-labelledby`                                                            | One is required. Most searches use `aria-label` ("Search products") and no visible label.                                                                                      |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(text)`                                                           | Controlled / uncontrolled text.                                                                                                                                                |
| `onSubmit(text)`, `onClear()`                                                                         | `Enter` and the clear action.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `suggestions`, `onSelect`, `maxResults`                                                               | Strings or `{ label, meta, data }`. Matched on `label` with `matchesSearch`, highlighted with `highlightMatch`, at most `maxResults` (default 6), in the order given.          |
| `shortcut`                                                                                            | Decorative hint such as `['Mod', 'K']`, drawn with `Kbd` while the box is empty. It registers nothing: use `useHotkey` and focus `inputRef`. Hidden from assistive technology. |
| `landmark`                                                                                            | Wraps the field in `role="search"` named by the label. Once per page.                                                                                                          |
| `size`, `placeholder`, `name`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `autoFocus`, `inputRef`, `ref`, `messages` | `messages`: `clear`, `placeholder`, `noResults`.                                                                                                                               |

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                     | Behavior                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Typing                  | Plain: updates the text. Suggestions: opens the list when there are matches |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | (Suggestions) move through the list; focus stays in the input               |
| `Enter`                 | Select the highlighted suggestion, else `onSubmit(text)`                    |
| `Escape`                | Plain: clear. Suggestions: close the list, then clear                       |

The clear button is "Clear search" (from messages), out of the tab order in suggestions mode, hidden while the box is empty. Highlighted parts are `<mark>` without a background: only weight and brightness change, so contrast holds.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: `aria-label` names the scope ("Search products"), not the control. Placeholder "Search" is a hint, never the name.

sections.heading: Example
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Suggestions use the combobox pattern with ARIA wiring (the handoff list had no roles), accent-insensitive highlighting (it matched by lowercase index) and an empty state from messages.
- Clear button, `Escape`, `role="search"` option, `onSubmit` and `onClear` are new. The shortcut is a decorative `Kbd` hint; registering it is the consumer's job (`useHotkey`).
- Uses RAC `ComboBox` rather than `Autocomplete` for suggestions: the floating list needs a popover and the ComboBox contract is already tested in `Combobox`.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.description:
A segmented control picks one value from a few options, like a radio group drawn as a
bar. It is a value control: it does not own panels (use `Tabs` for that). Exactly one
option is always selected.

Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup` with single selection and no empty selection:
it is exposed as a radio group, with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation.

props.name: options
props.description: The options, in display order. Two to five fit comfortably.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the group ("View"). Required: name this or use `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the group.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected option (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initially selected option (uncontrolled). Defaults to the first enabled option.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value when the user selects another option.

props.name: size
props.description: Height of the segments: `sm` 24px, `md` 32px (default).

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the container; the segments share the width equally.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the group element.

items.name: KeyboardSelection
items.description: One tab stop. Arrows move focus, Space selects, the selection can never be empty.

docs.summary:
A bar of two to five options where exactly one is selected, like a radio group drawn as buttons. It is a value control: it changes how something is shown or filtered, it does not own panels. Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup` with single selection and no empty selection.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/SegmentedControl.jsx` (TODO `CMP-FRM-09`).
whenToUse: A view mode (List, Board, Calendar), a period (Day, Week, Month) or a small filter (All, Open, Closed).
When the options are always visible and the change applies immediately.
whenNotToUse: To switch between panels of content: use `Tabs`.
For more than five options, or long labels: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`.
For on/off settings: use `Switch`.
keyboard: Keyboard: one tab stop; `←` / `→` move focus between options, `Space` selects the focused option. React Aria does not wrap at the ends. Disabled options are skipped. The selection can never be empty.
examples:
<SegmentedControl
  aria-label="View"
  options={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { value: 'board', label: 'Board' },
  ]}
  value={view}
  onChange={setView}
/>

<SegmentedControl
  aria-label="Order status"
  size="sm"
  options={[
    { value: 'all', label: 'All', count: 1248 },
    { value: 'open', label: 'Open', count: 12, countLabel: '12 open' },
  ]}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A view mode (List, Board, Calendar), a period (Day, Week, Month) or a small filter (All, Open, Closed).
- When the options are always visible and the change applies immediately.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To switch between panels of content: use `Tabs`.
- For more than five options, or long labels: use `Select` or `RadioGroup`.
- For on/off settings: use `Switch`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=radiogroup] aria-label        (bordered track)
  button[role=radio] aria-checked      (one per option)
    label
    count                              (optional, mono)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                             | Type                       | Default      | Notes                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `options`                        | `SegmentedControlOption[]` | required     | `{ value, label, count?, countLabel?, isDisabled? }`.                      |
| `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` | `string`                   | one required | Names the group ("View"). Enforced by the types.                           |
| `value` / `defaultValue`         | `string`                   | first option | Controlled / uncontrolled selection. Defaults to the first enabled option. |
| `onChange`                       | `(value: string) => void`  | none         | Called only when the selection changes.                                    |
| `size`                           | `'sm' \| 'md'`             | `'md'`       | Segment height: 24px (`sm`, the minimum target) or 32px (`md`).            |
| `fullWidth`                      | `boolean`                  | `false`      | Stretch to the container; segments share the width equally.                |
| `isDisabled`                     | `boolean`                  | `false`      | Disables every option.                                                     |

Counts are formatted for the active locale. `countLabel` is the text a screen reader hears after the label ("Open 12 open").

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Semantics: `radiogroup` with `radio` buttons and `aria-checked`. It is deliberately not a `tablist`.
- Keyboard: one tab stop; `←` / `→` move focus between options, `Space` selects the focused option. React Aria does not wrap at the ends. Disabled options are skipped. The selection can never be empty.
- Selected state is shown by a raised background, a line and ink text, not by color alone. The track border uses `--ds-line-control` (3:1).
- The count uses `--ds-text-2`: `--ds-text-3` would fail 4.5:1 on the selected surface.
- Focus: accent border and ring. Forced colors: the selected segment border uses `Highlight`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are one word or a short phrase in sentence case ("Open", "This week").
- Same-length labels look best; avoid mixing a count on some options only.

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `role="tablist"` / `tab` is replaced by `radiogroup` / `radio`: the control sets a value, not a panel.
- Roving focus and keyboard behavior come from React Aria; the handoff had none.
- `onChange` receives the value, is not called when the value does not change, and the group needs an accessible name.
- Counts are localized and can have a text alternative. Small segments are 24px (handoff 26px), medium 32px; both are tokens (`--ds-segmented-control-*`).
- The track border is `--ds-line-control` instead of `--ds-line` to meet 3:1 for UI boundaries.
