components.name: Select
components.description:
A single-choice dropdown built on React Aria `Select`: a button that opens a listbox in a
popover. Keyboard: Enter, Space or the arrow keys open it; typing selects by prefix (typeahead);
Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger. A hidden native `<select>` carries `name` and
the value into form submission and browser autofill.

Use it for 4 or more options; for 2 to 4 prefer `RadioGroup`.

props.name: options
props.description: The options, or groups of options. Keep the order you want users to see (see Select.md).

props.name: value
props.description: The selected `value`; `null` means nothing is selected. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initially selected `value` when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new `value`.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Error text, shown while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. See `Input`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Trigger text while nothing is selected. Default from messages: "Select an option".

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: popoverClassName
props.description: Class name for the popover that holds the options.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `placeholder`, `requiredMark`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

keys.description: Shown in the trigger while nothing is selected.

items.name: Open
items.description: The listbox open under the trigger, for the visual review (TEST-020).

docs.summary: Single-choice dropdown: a button that opens a listbox in a popover. Built on React Aria `Select` (`Button`, `SelectValue`, `Popover`, `ListBox`). A hidden native `<select>` carries `name` and the value into form submission and autofill. Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).
whenToUse: A choice from 4 or more options.
whenNotToUse: 2 to 4 options that users compare: `RadioGroup` (or a segmented control).
Typing to filter a long list: `ComboBox` (planned).
Several selections: `CheckboxGroup`.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - A choice from 4 or more options.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- 2 to 4 options that users compare: `RadioGroup` (or a segmented control).
- Typing to filter a long list: `ComboBox` (planned).
- Several selections: `CheckboxGroup`.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                            | Notes                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`          | As in `Input`.                                                                                      |
| `options`                                       | `SelectOption[]` (`value`, `label`, `isDisabled`) or groups `{ id, label, options }`, mixed freely. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`    | The selected option `value`; `null` means nothing selected. `onChange` receives `string \| null`.   |
| `placeholder`                                   | Trigger text while empty. Default from messages: "Select an option" (pt-BR "Selecione uma opção").  |
| `size`                                          | `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.                                                          |
| `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled` | Standard. `name` is submitted through the hidden `<select>`.                                        |
| `popoverClassName`, `className`, `ref`          | Styling hooks; `ref` is the field root.                                                             |
| `messages`                                      | `placeholder`, `requiredMark`.                                                                      |

Option order is yours: the component never reorders. The product rule that lists are alphabetical by default applies to what you pass in: use `sortByText(options, (o) => o.label, locale)` from `@loui/ds` (locale- and accent-aware) unless the order carries meaning (sizes, steps).

sections.heading: Anatomy and styling
sections.content:
- Trigger: the same box as `Input` (`--ds-line-control` border, focus ring, no hover fill), with a chevron.
- Popover: raised surface, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, radius `lg`, layer `--ds-z-dropdown`, at least as wide as the trigger, scrolls above `--ds-select-popover-max-height`.
- Option: `--ds-item-h` (36px) tall, hover and keyboard focus use `--ds-surface-hover`, the selected option shows a check (`Icon`), disabled options use the shared opacity.
- Section captions are mono, uppercase by CSS, in `--ds-text-2` (`--ds-text-3` fails contrast on the raised surface).

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                                      | Behavior                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Open the list and focus the selected (or first/last) option    |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`                  | Next / previous enabled option                                 |
| `Home` / `End`                           | First / last option                                            |
| Letters                                  | Typeahead: focus the option starting with what you type        |
| `Enter` / `Space`                        | Select the focused option, close, focus returns to the trigger |
| `Escape`                                 | Close without changing; focus returns to the trigger           |
| Typing on the closed trigger             | Selects by prefix without opening                              |

The trigger is a `button` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, named by the label and described by the description and error. Options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; sections are `role="group"` named by their caption; disabled options have `aria-disabled`.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Select
  label="Region"
  name="region"
  options={[
    { value: 'eu', label: 'EU: Frankfurt' },
    { value: 'us', label: 'US: Virginia' },
  ]}
  isRequired
  errorMessage="Choose a region."
/>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A custom accessible listbox replaces the native `<select>` (ADR-0001), with a hidden native select kept for forms and autofill. This resolves the "native or custom" question of CMP-FRM-05.
- Label association, description, error, `aria-invalid`, required, placeholder and groups are new; handoff `onChange(value, event)` is `onChange(value)`.
- No inline chevron data URI; the chevron is an `Icon` using the icon set.
- Focus styling is CSS and survives consumer `onFocus`/`onBlur`.

alternatives.name: RadioGroup
alternatives.reason: 2 to 4 options that users compare: `RadioGroup` (or a segmented control).

alternatives.name: CheckboxGroup
alternatives.reason: Several selections: `CheckboxGroup`.

components.name: Sheet
components.description:
A side panel that slides in from the inline-end edge, for viewing or editing one record
without leaving the list. Built on React Aria `Modal` and `Dialog`: focus is trapped and
restored, the page is inert and does not scroll, and `Escape` closes only the top-most layer
(a `Dialog` opened from a sheet closes first).

The header (title, mono meta, extra content, close button) is `--ds-topbar-h` tall; the body
scrolls; the footer stays at the bottom.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the sheet and its accessible name. One line; it is truncated with an ellipsis.

props.name: meta
props.description: Short mono text after the title, such as a record code ("ORD-1048").

props.name: headerExtra
props.description: Extra header content after the meta, usually a `Badge` with the status.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description linked to the sheet with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: children
props.description: Body of the sheet; it scrolls when it is taller than the viewport. A function receives `close`.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Footer actions, aligned to the end: Cancel (secondary) then the primary action. A function
receives `close`. The footer stays at the bottom while the body scrolls.

props.name: footerStart
props.description: Footer content aligned to the start, for the destructive action ("Delete order").

props.name: size
props.description: Width: `sm` 440px (default), `md` 460px, `lg` 480px. Full width on small screens.

props.name: padded
props.description: Pads the body (24px, 18px between children). Turn off for a table or a full-bleed list. Default `true`.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the sheet. Optional: omit it and control the sheet with `isOpen`.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the sheet opens or closes.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Whether pressing the scrim closes the sheet. Default `true`.

props.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
props.description: Disables closing with `Escape`. Use it only while a request is running.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the sheet panel.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the sheet panel.

keys.description: Name of the close button in the Sheet header.

items.name: Default
items.description: Open, focus trapped inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: LongContent
items.description: Long content scrolls in the body; the header and the footer stay in view.

items.name: NotPadded
items.description: A list or table that bleeds to the edges.

docs.summary:
A side panel that slides in from the inline-end edge to view or edit one record without leaving the list. Built on React Aria `Modal` and `Dialog`. Generic: it lives in the core entry point.

- Handoff source: `components/erp/Sheet` (CMP-PAT-01).
whenToUse: A record's details or edit form next to the list it came from.
Filters or settings with a footer of actions.
whenNotToUse: A short confirmation or a small form: use `Dialog`.
A hint or a few controls on a trigger: use `Popover`.
Page-level navigation: use `Sidebar`.
keyboard: Same overlay contract as `Dialog`: focus trapped and restored, `inert` page, scroll lock, `Escape` closes only the top layer (a `Dialog` opened inside the sheet closes first; tested in `Dialog.test.tsx`).
examples:
<Sheet
  trigger={<Button>View order</Button>}
  title="Order"
  meta="ORD-1048"
  headerExtra={<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>}
  footerStart={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>
        Save order
      </Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Customer" />
</Sheet>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A record's details or edit form next to the list it came from.
- Filters or settings with a footer of actions.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A short confirmation or a small form: use `Dialog`.
- A hint or a few controls on a trigger: use `Popover`.
- Page-level navigation: use `Sidebar`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
DialogTrigger
  trigger
  ModalOverlay       --ds-scrim, z sheet
    Modal            surface, strong line at the start edge, dialog shadow, width sm | md | lg
      Dialog         role=dialog, aria-labelledby = title
        header       --ds-topbar-h tall: title (ellipsis) · meta (mono) · headerExtra · close IconButton
        body         scrolls; padded (24px) or not
        footer       sticky: footerStart (destructive) ... footer (Cancel + primary)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                      | Type                                    | Default | Notes                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`                                   | `ReactNode` (required)                  | none    | Heading and accessible name (not limited to strings, unlike the handoff). |
| `meta`                                    | `ReactNode`                             |         | Mono text after the title ("ORD-1048").                                   |
| `headerExtra`                             | `ReactNode`                             |         | Usually a `Badge`.                                                        |
| `description`                             | `ReactNode`                             |         | Linked with `aria-describedby`.                                           |
| `children`                                | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |         | Body.                                                                     |
| `footer` / `footerStart`                  | `ReactNode \| ({ close }) => ReactNode` |         | End / start aligned actions.                                              |
| `size`                                    | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                  | `sm`    | 440 / 460 / 480 px (`--ds-sheet-width-*`); full width on small screens.   |
| `padded`                                  | `boolean`                               | `true`  | `false` for a table or list that bleeds to the edges.                     |
| `trigger`                                 | `ReactElement`                          |         | Optional when controlled.                                                 |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                         |         | Controlled / uncontrolled open state.                                     |
| `isDismissable`                           | `boolean`                               | `true`  | Press on the scrim closes it.                                             |
| `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`               | `boolean`                               | `false` |                                                                           |
| `messages`                                | `{ close }`                             |         | "Close panel" (pt-BR "Fechar painel").                                    |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Same overlay contract as `Dialog`: focus trapped and restored, `inert` page, scroll lock, `Escape` closes only the top layer (a `Dialog` opened inside the sheet closes first; tested in `Dialog.test.tsx`).
- Named by the title through `aria-labelledby`, so a non-string title works (the handoff only labeled string titles).
- The close button is an `IconButton` named from messages. The handoff set `title="Close (Esc)"`.
- Slide-in is a 150 ms transform and the scrim fades; both are removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The slide direction follows the writing direction (`:dir(rtl)`).
- The panel is `Modal` content inside the overlay, so it stacks above the scrim without a second z-index.
- See the Dialog doc ("Layers") for popovers opened from inside the sheet.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: the record type or name, sentence case. Meta: its code, as data.
- Footer: destructive action at the start ("Delete order"); Cancel then the primary action at the end ("Save order"). Deleting still goes through a `ConfirmDialog`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Sheet
  trigger={<Button>View order</Button>}
  title="Order"
  meta="ORD-1048"
  headerExtra={<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>}
  footerStart={<Button variant="danger">Delete order</Button>}
  footer={({ close }) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>
        Save order
      </Button>
    </>
  )}
>
  <Input label="Customer" />
</Sheet>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Built on React Aria `Modal`: focus trap/restore, `inert`, scroll lock, stack-aware `Escape` (the handoff added a window listener per sheet).
- `width` (440 / 460 / 480 ERP-specific values) became `size` (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) with component tokens; header height is `--ds-topbar-h`; layers come from `--ds-z-sheet`.
- `contained` mode is not ported. `onClose` is replaced by `onOpenChange`.
- The scrim is `--ds-scrim`, no blur; the panel is `--ds-surface` with the dialog shadow.
- New: `description`, `footerStart`, controlled state, close label from messages, RTL slide.

alternatives.reason: A short confirmation or a small form: use `Dialog`.

alternatives.name: Popover
alternatives.reason: A hint or a few controls on a trigger: use `Popover`.

alternatives.name: Sidebar
alternatives.reason: Page-level navigation: use `Sidebar`.

components.name: ShortcutsHelp
components.description:
A dialog that lists the registered keyboard shortcuts (`useHotkeys` with a `description`),
grouped by their `group`, one table per group with the keys drawn by `Kbd`. Opens with `?` by
default. Place it once, anywhere under the app, and it stays in sync with what is mounted.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog opens (from the hotkey) or closes.

props.name: hotkey
props.description:
The shortcut that opens the dialog, registered in the hotkey registry. Default `'?'`.
It does not fire while an input has focus, so typing a question mark still works.
Pass `false` to open the dialog only through `isOpen`.

props.name: includeInactive
props.description: Also list shortcuts whose scope is not active right now. Default `false`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ title: string; description: string; ungrouped: string; empty: string; close: string; action: string; keys: string; openDescription: string; openGroup: string; }>
props.description: Message overrides for this instance.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the dialog panel.

keys.description: Title of the dialog.

keys.default: Shortcuts that work on this page.
keys.description: Description under the title.
Heading for shortcuts that have no `group`.

keys.default: No keyboard shortcuts on this page.
keys.description: Shown when no shortcut is registered.
Label of the button that closes the dialog.
Column header: what the shortcut does.
Column header: the keys.
Description of the shortcut that opens the dialog.
Group of the shortcut that opens the dialog.

items.name: Default
items.description: `?` opens the dialog from anywhere outside an input; the page shortcuts stay quiet while it is open.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: Empty
items.description: No shortcut is registered.

items.name: PortugueseBrazil
items.description: Brazilian Portuguese: title, group fallback, column headers (hidden) and the spoken key names.

docs.summary: A dialog that lists the keyboard shortcuts registered on the page, one table per group, with the keys drawn by `Kbd`. It opens with `?` by default.
whenToUse: Once per app (or per module), next to the `CommandPalette`, so users can learn the shortcuts without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: To register shortcuts: use `useHotkeys`. This only lists what is registered.
As the only way to find a command: the `CommandPalette` also searches by name.
keyboard: `Escape` and the Close button close it.
examples:
<HotkeyProvider>
  <App />
  <ShortcutsHelp />
</HotkeyProvider>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Once per app (or per module), next to the `CommandPalette`, so users can learn the shortcuts without leaving the page.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To register shortcuts: use `useHotkeys`. This only lists what is registered.
- As the only way to find a command: the `CommandPalette` also searches by name.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
Dialog "Keyboard shortcuts"  (size md, Close button)
  table  caption = group
    tr   th[scope=row] description · td Kbd keys
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop              | Type                        | Default | Notes                                                                |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `isOpen`          | `boolean`                   | -       | Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`                      |
| `defaultOpen`     | `boolean`                   | `false` | Initial state when uncontrolled                                      |
| `onOpenChange`    | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` | -       | Called on open (from the hotkey) and close                           |
| `hotkey`          | `string \| false`           | `'?'`   | Registered in the hotkey registry. Not fired while typing in a field |
| `includeInactive` | `boolean`                   | `false` | Also lists shortcuts whose scope is not active now                   |
| `messages`        | `Partial<messages>`         | -       | Per-instance overrides                                               |

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- Lists shortcuts that have a `description` (`useHotkeys`). Groups are sorted with the locale; shortcuts without a `group` go under "Other", last. Rows are sorted by description.
- Updates while it is open: shortcuts that mount or unmount appear or disappear.
- It lists itself ("Show keyboard shortcuts") and the `CommandPalette` shortcut.
- While it is open, page shortcuts do not fire.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A modal `dialog` named "Keyboard shortcuts" with a description; focus is trapped and returns on close.
- Each group is a real `<table>` named by its `<caption>`; the description is the row header, the keys are the cell. The column headers exist for screen readers and are visually hidden.
- Keys use `Kbd`, with spoken names for symbols.
- `Escape` and the Close button close it.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Descriptions are verb plus object in sentence case ("Create order"), as in the command palette.
- Messages: `title`, `description`, `ungrouped`, `empty`, `close`, `action`, `keys`, `openDescription`, `openGroup`. English and pt-BR ship.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<HotkeyProvider>
  <App />
  <ShortcutsHelp />
</HotkeyProvider>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff drew a static keyboard card. This list is generated from the registry, so it cannot drift from the real shortcuts.

alternatives.reason: As the only way to find a command: the `CommandPalette` also searches by name.

components.name: Sidebar
components.description:
The app sidebar: a workspace block, navigation sections, an optional status card, a footer
slot and the signed-in user. It is an `aside` landmark; each section is a separate `nav`
landmark named by its caption. It is `--ds-sidebar-w` wide and scrolls on its own when it is
taller than its container, so give the parent a fixed height.

Reading order and focus order follow the visual order: sections top to bottom, then the
footer. Collapsing or an off-canvas mobile variant is not part of this component.

props.name: workspace
props.description: The workspace block at the top.

props.name: sections
props.description: Navigation groups. Each one is its own labelled `nav` landmark.

props.name: value
props.description: `value` of the active item (gets `aria-current="page"`).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the `value` of the item the user pressed.

props.name: status
props.description: Optional status card above the footer.

props.name: footer
props.description: Free slot above the user block, for example a help link or an upgrade note.

props.name: user
props.description: The signed-in user, at the bottom.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Overrides the accessible name of the landmark (default "Sidebar" from the catalog).

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Accessible name of the sidebar landmark.

items.name: FocusOrder
items.description: Focus order follows the visual order: sections top to bottom, then the footer.

items.name: ManyItems
items.description: Taller content scrolls inside the sidebar; the page does not.

docs.summary:
The app sidebar: workspace block, navigation sections, optional status card, footer slot and the signed-in user. It is an `aside` landmark and each section is its own `nav`.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/Sidebar.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-01`).
whenToUse: The persistent primary navigation of an app shell, next to the content and below a `SkipLink`.
whenNotToUse: For in-page navigation or a table of contents.
For mobile off-canvas navigation: collapsing and responsive behavior are not part of this component yet.
examples:
<Sidebar
  workspace={{ name: 'Northwind', subtitle: 'Production' }}
  value="orders"
  onChange={setView}
  sections={[
    {
      id: 'work',
      title: 'Work',
      items: [
        {
          value: 'orders',
          label: 'Orders',
          href: '/orders',
          icon: StarIcon,
          count: 3,
          countLabel: '3 pending',
          countTone: 'warning',
        },
        { value: 'customers', label: 'Customers', href: '/customers' },
      ],
    },
  ]}
  status={{ title: 'All systems operational', meta: 'Last sync', value: '2 min ago' }}
  user={{ name: 'Ana Souza', role: 'Owner' }}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - The persistent primary navigation of an app shell, next to the content and below a `SkipLink`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For in-page navigation or a table of contents.
- For mobile off-canvas navigation: collapsing and responsive behavior are not part of this component yet.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
aside[aria-label="Sidebar"]         (--ds-sidebar-w wide, scrolls on its own)
  workspace                         (initial tile, name, subtitle)
  nav[aria-labelledby=caption]      (one per section)
    caption                         (mono, uppercase by CSS)
    ul > li > NavItem
  bottom
    status                          (role=status: dot + title + meta/value)
    footer                          (slot)
    user                            (Avatar + name + role)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                              | Notes                                                                                    |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workspace`  | `{ name, subtitle?, initial? }`   | `initial` defaults to the first letter of the name (locale upper-casing).                |
| `sections`   | `SidebarSection[]`                | `{ id, title, items }` or `{ id, label, items }` (one of `title` / `label` is required). |
| `value`      | `string`                          | `value` of the active item.                                                              |
| `onChange`   | `(value: string) => void`         | Called with the item the user pressed (links and buttons).                               |
| `status`     | `{ tone?, title, meta?, value? }` | `tone`: `success` (default), `warning`, `danger`. The title carries the meaning.         |
| `footer`     | `ReactNode`                       | Free slot above the user block.                                                          |
| `user`       | `{ name, role?, avatarSrc? }`     | Rendered with a decorative `Avatar` (the name is next to it).                            |
| `aria-label` | `string`                          | Overrides the landmark name (default "Sidebar" from the catalog).                        |
| `messages`   | `{ label?: string }`              | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                                |

A `SidebarItem` is `{ value, label, href?, icon?, count?, countLabel?, countTone?, isDisabled? }`; it renders a `NavItem`. Always set `countLabel` with `count`.

sections.heading: Layout
sections.content:
- Width is `--ds-sidebar-w` (240px). The handoff's `width` prop and 248px default are dropped; there is one width in the system.
- The sidebar uses `max-block-size: 100%` and `overflow-y: auto`: give its parent a definite height (for example a full-height flex row) and it scrolls on its own while the content scrolls separately. The status, footer and user stay at the bottom when there is room.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Landmarks: `aside` (complementary) named "Sidebar", and one `nav` per section named by its visible caption (or by `label` when there is no caption). Names are unique, so landmark lists are meaningful.
- Items are in a `ul`, so screen readers announce "list, 5 items".
- Focus order follows the visual order: sections top to bottom, then the footer, then nothing in the status or user blocks (they are text).
- The status block is `role="status"` (polite live region): a change from "Synced" to "Sync failed" is announced. The dot is `aria-hidden`; the title says the status in words.
- The workspace tile and the user avatar are decorative because the names are shown next to them.
- The active item has `aria-current="page"` (see `NavItem`).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Section captions are written in sentence case ("Work"); the CSS makes them uppercase mono.
- Status titles say the state: "All systems operational", not "OK".

sections.heading: Examples
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Width is the token (240px) instead of a 248px default prop.
- `aside` + one labelled `nav` per section + lists, instead of anonymous `nav`s with `div` captions.
- Items are `NavItem`s (real links); the user avatar is the `Avatar` component; the status card is a `role="status"` region with a decorative dot.
- Not included yet: collapsed/icon-only mode and a responsive off-canvas variant (needs its own decision).

components.name: Skeleton
components.description:
A placeholder block in the shape of content that is still loading. It is always hidden
from assistive technology: mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"` and
remove the attribute (and the skeletons) when the content arrives.

The `width` and `height` props are the only dynamic values in the library that reach the
DOM as custom properties on `style`, because arbitrary sizes cannot be tokens.

props.name: width
props.description: Width: a number in px or any CSS length. Default `100%`. Ignored when `circle` is set (the circle is as wide as it is tall).

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the block, or of each line: a number in px or any CSS length. Default `12px` (`--ds-skeleton-height`).

props.name: circle
props.description: Renders a circle, for an avatar. The diameter is `height`.

props.name: lines
props.description: Renders this many text lines; the last one is shorter. Takes precedence over `circle`.

items.name: BusyRegion
items.description: The loading region carries `aria-busy`; the skeletons themselves are hidden from assistive technology.

docs.summary: A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading: a block, a circle, or a few text lines.
whenToUse: The layout of the content is known (a list of rows, a card, an avatar next to text) and the wait is short.
Keep the page from jumping when the data arrives.
whenNotToUse: For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.
For a measurable task: use `Progress`.
When there is nothing to show after loading: use `EmptyState`.
examples:
<section aria-busy={isLoading} aria-label="Recent orders">
  {isLoading ? (
    <>
      <Skeleton circle height={28} />
      <Skeleton lines={3} />
    </>
  ) : (
    <OrderList orders={orders} />
  )}
</section>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- The layout of the content is known (a list of rows, a card, an avatar next to text) and the wait is short.
- Keep the page from jumping when the data arrives.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.
- For a measurable task: use `Progress`.
- When there is nothing to show after loading: use `EmptyState`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span[aria-hidden="true"]  block | circle
span[aria-hidden="true"]  lines → n × span (last one is 60% wide)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop     | Type               | Default | Notes                                                             |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `width`  | `number \| string` | `100%`  | Number is px. Ignored with `circle`                               |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `12px`  | Height of the block or of each line (`--ds-skeleton-height`)      |
| `circle` | `boolean`          | `false` | Diameter is `height`                                              |
| `lines`  | `number`           |         | Text lines; the last is shorter (not when there is only one line) |

Other `span` attributes and `ref` go to the root. `width` and `height` reach the DOM as custom properties on `style` (the only dynamic styles in the component); everything else is CSS.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every skeleton is `aria-hidden="true"`: it is decoration and has no text.
- **Mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"`** and remove it, together with the skeletons, when the content arrives. This tells assistive technology the region is being updated. A skeleton on its own does not do this.
- If the wait is long, also expose a polite status ("Loading orders") near the region; skeletons never announce it.
- The pulse (opacity only) is switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. In forced-colors mode the placeholder gets a border because background colors are dropped.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Match the final layout: the same number of rows and similar widths, so nothing moves when the data arrives.
- Show at most one screenful of placeholders.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<section aria-busy={isLoading} aria-label="Recent orders">
  {isLoading ? (
    <>
      <Skeleton circle height={28} />
      <Skeleton lines={3} />
    </>
  ) : (
    <OrderList orders={orders} />
  )}
</section>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Always hidden from assistive technology (the handoff hid only the single block, not the `lines` variant).
- Reduced motion switches the pulse off; the keyframes are local to the component.
- Pulse duration and default height are component tokens.
- No `radius` or `style` props. A `SkeletonGroup` wrapper was not added: `aria-busy` on your own region is one attribute, and a wrapper would hide which element is busy.
- Presets (avatar, row, card) are compositions of `circle`, `lines` and `width`/`height`; see the busy-region story.

alternatives.reason: For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.reason: For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.

alternatives.name: Progress
alternatives.reason: For a measurable task: use `Progress`.

alternatives.name: EmptyState
alternatives.reason: When there is nothing to show after loading: use `EmptyState`.

components.name: SkipLink
components.description:
A link that is invisible until a keyboard user focuses it, then jumps past the repeated
navigation to the main content (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). Put it as the very first
focusable element of the page, before the sidebar and the top bar.

It moves focus itself instead of relying on the hash navigation, so it also works with hash
based routers and with a target that is not focusable by default.

props.name: targetId
props.description:
Id of the element to jump to, without the `#`. Default `main`. The element should be the
page's `<main>` (or its first heading); it does not need a `tabindex`.

props.name: children
props.description: Link text. Defaults to "Skip to main content" from the message catalog.

props.name: messages
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Default text of the skip link.

items.name: Default
items.description: Hidden until it receives keyboard focus: press Tab.

items.name: JumpsToMain
items.description: Enter jumps past the navigation: focus lands on the main content.

docs.summary:
A link that stays invisible until a keyboard user focuses it, then jumps past the repeated navigation to the main content (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).

- Source: TODO `BASE-002` (there was no handoff component).
whenToUse: Once per page, as the first focusable element, before the sidebar and the top bar.
whenNotToUse: As a general "go to section" link: use `Link`.
keyboard: It is a real link, so it appears in link lists and works with `Enter`.
examples:
<>
  <SkipLink />
  <Sidebar … />
  <main id="main">…</main>
</>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Once per page, as the first focusable element, before the sidebar and the top bar.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content: - As a general "go to section" link: use `Link`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop       | Type                 | Default                | Notes                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `targetId` | `string`             | `'main'`               | Id of the element to jump to, without `#`. Becomes `href="#<targetId>"`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode`          | "Skip to main content" | Custom text. Default comes from the catalog (English and pt-BR).         |
| `messages` | `{ label?: string }` | catalog                | Per-instance override (ADR-0005).                                        |
| `onClick`  | click handler        | none                   | Runs first; `preventDefault()` cancels the jump.                         |

`ref` points to the `<a>`; `className` and other anchor attributes pass through.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
- Hidden with the same technique as `VisuallyHidden` (1px, clipped), so it is still focusable. On focus it becomes a primary-colored button at the top start corner, above everything (`--ds-skip-link-z-index`).
- On activation it focuses the target element itself and cancels the hash navigation. This works with hash-based routers and with targets that are not focusable (a temporary `tabindex="-1"` is added and removed on blur; an existing `tabindex` is kept). If the target does not exist, the browser's default behavior runs.
- Give the target `id="main"`; put it on `<main>`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- It is a real link, so it appears in link lists and works with `Enter`.
- Visible focus with the accent ring; forced colors use `Highlight`.
- The text says where it goes. Do not shorten it to "Skip".

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - "Skip to main content" (default). For a second link use the destination: "Skip to the results".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<>
  <SkipLink />
  <Sidebar … />
  <main id="main">…</main>
</>
```

sections.heading: `.ds-sr-only` (BASE-002)
sections.content: The TODO asks for a `.ds-sr-only` utility class too. It belongs in `src/styles/base.css` (`@layer utilities`), a shared file this component does not own. The rule to add is the same as `.root` of `VisuallyHidden` (absolute, 1px, `clip-path: inset(50%)`, no overflow).

alternatives.name: Link
alternatives.reason: As a general "go to section" link: use `Link`.

components.name: Slider
components.description:
A single-value slider built on React Aria `Slider`: a labelled track with one thumb that is a
real `<input type="range">`, so keyboard, pointer, touch and form submission (`name`) work
natively. Keys: arrows step by `step`, `PageUp`/`PageDown` move by a larger step (10% of the
range, at least `step`), `Home`/`End` jump to the limits.

Range selection with two thumbs is not part of this component yet.

props.name: value
props.description: The value when controlled. Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value when uncontrolled. Defaults to `minValue`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called while the value changes (each key press, each pointer move).

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.description: Called once when a drag ends or a key press is committed. Use it to save.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description:
Formats the value shown next to the label and spoken to screen readers
(`aria-valuetext`): `{ style: 'percent' }`, `{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer' }`, ...
Uses the locale of `DSProvider`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name for form submission; the form receives the number.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the formatted value (mono) on the right of the label. Default `true`.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the track, linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

docs.summary: Single-value slider: a labelled track with one thumb and a formatted value. Built on React Aria `Slider` (`SliderTrack`, `SliderFill`, `SliderThumb`, `SliderOutput`). The thumb is a real `<input type="range">`, so keyboard, pointer, touch and form submission work natively. Task: CMP-INP-04.
whenToUse: Picking a number from a bounded range where the approximate value matters more than the exact one (discount, opacity, threshold).
whenNotToUse: An exact quantity: `NumberField`. Money: `CurrencyInput`.
A range with two ends: not supported yet (two-thumb range is P2).
Fewer than about five discrete choices: `RadioGroup` or a segmented control.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Picking a number from a bounded range where the approximate value matters more than the exact one (discount, opacity, threshold).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- An exact quantity: `NumberField`. Money: `CurrencyInput`.
- A range with two ends: not supported yet (two-thumb range is P2).
- Fewer than about five discrete choices: `RadioGroup` or a segmented control.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
- Header: `Label` (left) and the formatted value in mono (right, `SliderOutput`).
- Track: rail (`--ds-line-control`, 3:1 against the page), fill from the start to the thumb (`--ds-accent`), thumb.
- Thumb: a 24px hit area (`--ds-slider-thumb-size`, WCAG 2.5.8) with a 16px visible knob; the focus ring follows the hit area.
- Optional description under the track.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`   | One is required (types and a development warning).                                               |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)` | Controlled / uncontrolled, RAC naming. `onChange` fires on every step; `onChangeEnd` on commit.  |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`               | Defaults `0`, `100`, `1`.                                                                        |
| `formatOptions`                              | `Intl.NumberFormat` options for the shown value and `aria-valuetext`, locale from `DSProvider`.  |
| `showValue`                                  | Default `true`.                                                                                  |
| `description`                                | Helper text, linked with `aria-describedby` on the thumb.                                        |
| `name`                                       | Submitted with the form as the number.                                                           |
| `isDisabled`                                 | Dimmed track; the text drops to `--ds-text-3` instead of using opacity so it keeps its contrast. |

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                       | Behavior                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowUp`  | Increase by `step`                                                       |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowDown` | Decrease by `step`                                                       |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`     | Increase / decrease by a larger step (10% of the range, at least `step`) |
| `Home` / `End`            | Minimum / maximum                                                        |

The thumb is `input[type=range]`, named by the label, with `aria-valuetext` from `formatOptions`. The value text is not a live region (RAC announces changes through the input).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: Label with the thing being set ("Discount"), not an instruction. Put the unit in `formatOptions` (`{ style: 'percent' }`, `{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer' }`), never in the label.

sections.heading: Example
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The thumb is a real range input (the handoff `div role="slider"` had no name, no Home/End/PageUp/PageDown and no `aria-valuetext`).
- `format(value)` became `formatOptions` (locale-aware `Intl`); `min`/`max` became `minValue`/`maxValue` (RAC names); the knob has a 24px hit area; the label is required.
- The decorative shadow on the knob was dropped (shadows only on overlays).

components.name: SourceList
components.description:
The numbered list of sources an answer is based on. Each source is a list item that
`Citation` markers jump to; the title is a link when the source has a `url`.

Source numbers are the position in `sources`: keep the order stable while the answer streams,
and append new sources at the end.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the list. Required: citations use it to find their source.

props.name: sources
props.description: The sources, in citation order. The first is source 1.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading text. Defaults to "Sources".

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Default `3`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ title: string; citation: (number: number, title: string) => string; }>
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

keys.description: Default heading of the source list.
Accessible name of a citation marker: "Source 2: Title".

items.name: WithCitations
items.description: Markers in a sentence jump to the matching source; focus lands on it.

docs.summary: The numbered list of sources an answer is based on (`SourceList`) and the inline markers that point to it (`Citation`). Import both from `@loui/ds/patterns`.
whenToUse: An assistant answer that rests on documents, pages or records, and the owner should be able to check them.
whenNotToUse: Footnotes in long-form documents: use plain links.
A list of results the user searched for: use a table or a list of cards.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - An assistant answer that rests on documents, pages or records, and the owner should be able to check them.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Footnotes in long-form documents: use plain links.
- A list of results the user searched for: use a table or a list of cards.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: ``` p ... a claim [2] ... Citation: 2 section named by its heading ("Sources") ol li tabIndex=-1 (focus target) title (link when it has a url) · domain (mono) · snippet ```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`SourceList`

| Prop           | Type            | Default   | Notes                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | `string`        | -         | Required. Citations find their source through it.                            |
| `sources`      | `Source[]`      | -         | `{ id, title, url?, domain?, snippet? }`. The position is the source number. |
| `title`        | `string`        | "Sources" | Heading text.                                                                |
| `headingLevel` | `1`-`6`         | `3`       |                                                                              |
| `messages`     | partial catalog |           | `title`, `citation(number, title)`.                                          |

`Citation`: `number` (1-based, the visible text), `title`, `listId`, `sourceId`, plus anchor props. `getSourceElementId(listId, sourceId)` returns the DOM id when you need it.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A citation is a real link (`href="#..."`) named "Source 2: Title"; the visible text is the number, which the name contains.
- Activating it moves focus to the matching list item and scrolls it into view. It does not change the URL hash, so it does not fight your router. Without JavaScript the hash link still works.
- Source titles with a `url` are links that open in a new tab (with the external-link icon and a screen-reader note).
- The marker is 24 px square (WCAG 2.5.8).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Keep source order stable while the answer streams; append new sources at the end, so numbers already shown never change.
- Titles say what the page is, not "Click here". Snippets are short, plain text.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx

Orders move through four statuses .

```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: No handoff source: new pattern (TODO `AI-013`).

components.name: Sparkline
components.description:
A tiny trend line (or area) without axes, drawn in SVG, for tables, stat cards and lists. It
shows the shape of a series, not its values: put the current number next to it.

It is an image with a required text summary (`aria-label`), or `decorative` when the same
information is written next to it. It is not interactive and not focusable. The vertical
range is the data's own minimum to maximum, so a small change on a large number still
shows; use `Chart` when readers need axes, values per point or zero as a reference.

props.name: data
props.description:
The values in display order, usually time. `null`, `undefined` and non-finite numbers are
gaps: the line breaks there. An empty array draws nothing.

props.name: variant
props.description: `line` (default) or `area`, which also fills softly under the line.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Color of the line: `neutral` (default), `accent`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`. Color is
never the only signal: say what the trend means in the accessible name or next to it.

props.name: width
props.description: Width in px (user units). Shrinks to fit a narrower container. Default 96.

props.name: height
props.description: Height in px (user units). Default 24.

props.name: showLast
props.description: Draws a solid dot on the last value, the current one.

props.name: showMinMax
props.description: Draws hollow markers on the lowest and the highest value (omitted when all values are equal).

props.name: includeZero
props.description: Keeps 0 in the vertical range. Default: the range is the data's own minimum to maximum.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Summary of the trend, required unless `decorative` or `aria-labelledby`: "Revenue, last 7 days: up 12%".

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that summarizes the trend.

props.name: decorative
props.description:
Hides the sparkline from assistive technology. Use it only when the same information
is in text next to it (a number and "+12%"): the line alone is never the only source.

docs.summary:
A tiny trend line (or area) without axes, drawn in SVG, for tables, stat cards and lists. It shows the shape of a series, not its values: put the current number next to it.

- TODO `GAP-007`.
whenToUse: Next to a number in a `StatCard`, a table row or a list item, to show the recent trend.
When the shape matters more than exact values.
whenNotToUse: When readers need axes, values per point or keyboard exploration: use `Chart`.
To show a quantity within a range: use `Meter` or `DonutMeter`.
As the only place a number appears: the sparkline is a summary, not a source.
examples: Orders 1,248 +12%

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Next to a number in a `StatCard`, a table row or a list item, to show the recent trend.
- When the shape matters more than exact values.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- When readers need axes, values per point or keyboard exploration: use `Chart`.
- To show a quantity within a range: use `Meter` or `DonutMeter`.
- As the only place a number appears: the sparkline is a summary, not a source.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
svg[role=img] aria-label            (or aria-hidden when decorative)
  path.area                         (variant="area" only)
  path.line                         (one per run of values, a gap starts a new one)
  circle.marker[min|max]            (showMinMax: hollow rings)
  circle.last                       (showLast: solid dot)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                             | Type                                                          | Default      | Notes                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `data`                           | `(number \| null \| undefined)[]`                             | required     | Values in display order. `null`, `undefined`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are gaps.         |
| `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                                      | one of three | A text summary of the trend. Required unless `decorative`. Enforced by the types.    |
| `decorative`                     | `true`                                                        | none         | Hides it from assistive technology. Only when the same facts are written next to it. |
| `variant`                        | `'line' \| 'area'`                                            | `'line'`     | `area` fills softly under the line.                                                  |
| `tone`                           | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'`  | Color of the line. Never the only signal.                                            |
| `width` / `height`               | `number`                                                      | 96 / 24      | Size in px. Shrinks to a narrower container, keeping its aspect ratio.               |
| `showLast`                       | `boolean`                                                     | `false`      | Solid dot on the last value.                                                         |
| `showMinMax`                     | `boolean`                                                     | `false`      | Hollow rings on the lowest and the highest value (not drawn when all are equal).     |
| `includeZero`                    | `boolean`                                                     | `false`      | Keeps 0 in the vertical range. Default: the data's own min to max.                   |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- It is an `img` with a required text summary: say what a sighted reader sees, with the numbers that matter ("Orders, last 7 days: up 12%"). Use `decorative` only when that text is already next to the sparkline.
- It is not focusable and not interactive; there are no tooltips. For exploration use `Chart`.
- Color is never the only signal: tone changes the line color, the trend must be in the name or next to it. Min and max are hollow rings and the last value is a solid dot, so they differ by shape.
- Line, markers and area use `--ds-text-2` or a signal color (3:1 or better on the dark surfaces). Forced colors: everything is drawn in `CanvasText`.
- Under 200% zoom and in narrow containers it shrinks with the container.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Summaries are one short sentence in sentence case with the period and the direction: "Revenue, last 30 days: up 8%".

sections.heading: Differences from `Chart`
sections.content: The vertical range is the data's own minimum to maximum, not a "nice" axis that includes zero (`niceScale`), because a trend line on `98, 100, 102` must not be flattened. For that reason `niceScale` and the `Chart` layout helpers are not reused; the geometry lives in `sparklineLayout.ts` and is unit tested.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx

Orders 1,248 +12%

```

components.name: Spinner
components.description:
An indeterminate loading ring that inherits the text color.

It is a `progressbar` without a value, not a live region, so many spinners on a screen do
not each interrupt a screen reader. For large areas prefer `Skeleton`. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion` the ring is static.

props.name: size
props.description: Size token: `sm` 14px, `md` 18px (default), `lg` 20px.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name. Defaults to the "Loading" message. Say what is loading when it helps
("Loading orders").

props.name: decorative
props.description:
Hide the spinner from assistive technology. Use it only when the surrounding UI already
announces the busy state (visible status text, `aria-busy` region). Not needed inside a
pending `Button`, which wires the spinner as its busy label.

props.name: messages
props.description: Override the built-in messages for this instance.

items.name: WithLabel
items.description: Say what is loading when the page has more than one busy area.

items.name: DecorativeWithText
items.description: Visible status text next to the spinner; the spinner itself is hidden from assistive technology.

items.name: InheritsColor
items.description: Inherits the text color of its container.

docs.summary:
An indeterminate loading ring that inherits the text color. Small, quiet, and not a live region.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Spinner` (CMP-FBK-06).
- Built on: a plain element with `role="progressbar"`. A pending `Button` wires it as its busy label through React Aria.
whenToUse: Inside a pending `Button` (`isPending`), which renders it for you.
Next to a short status text for a small, bounded wait ("Saving changes").
A single small area that is loading and has no better placeholder.
whenNotToUse: For large areas or page loads: use `Skeleton` so the layout does not jump.
When you know the progress: use `Progress` with a value.
As a decoration. It means "busy", so remove it when the work ends.
examples: Saving changes

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Inside a pending `Button` (`isPending`), which renders it for you.
- Next to a short status text for a small, bounded wait ("Saving changes").
- A single small area that is loading and has no better placeholder.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For large areas or page loads: use `Skeleton` so the layout does not jump.
- When you know the progress: use `Progress` with a value.
- As a decoration. It means "busy", so remove it when the work ends.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: One element: a ring with an open top edge. Size comes from `--ds-icon-sm|md|lg`, thickness from `--ds-spinner-stroke-width`, rotation time from `--ds-spinner-duration`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                   | Default   | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`    | 14, 18, 20 px. Use `sm` inside `sm` and `md` buttons.                                     |
| `label`      | `string`               | "Loading" | Accessible name. Say what is loading when it helps ("Loading orders").                    |
| `decorative` | `boolean`              | `false`   | Hides the spinner from assistive technology. Only when other UI announces the busy state. |
| `messages`   | `{ loading?: string }` | none      | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                                 |
| `className`  | `string`               | none      | Merged with the component class.                                                          |

Other attributes and `ref` pass through to the element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `role="progressbar"` with no value (indeterminate) and an accessible name. It is **not** `role="status"` or `aria-live`: a screen reader does not announce every spinner when it mounts. One announcement strategy per screen: the button (`Button` announces pending and done) or a single status region you control.
- Decorative mode: `aria-hidden="true"`. Pair it with visible status text in a `role="status"` region, as in the `DecorativeWithText` story.
- Reduced motion: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the ring does not rotate. It stays as a static open ring; the accessible name and the busy control state carry the meaning.
- Forced colors: the ring is drawn with `currentColor` borders, which follow the system text color.
- Color: inherits the text color, so it needs no extra contrast treatment beyond its container's.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- The name is a short noun phrase in sentence case: "Loading", "Loading orders". No ellipsis, no exclamation mark.
- Default text comes from the `Spinner` message catalog (`en`: "Loading", `pt-BR`: "Carregando"). Override it per instance or through `DSProvider messages={{ Spinner: { loading: '...' } }}`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx

Saving changes

```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The pt-BR default label is gone; English is the default and pt-BR is in the catalog.
- `size` is `sm | md | lg` mapped to icon tokens instead of a pixel number; `color` and `style` props were removed (the ring follows `currentColor`).
- `role="status"` was replaced by `progressbar`, and a visible `label` is no longer part of the component: place your own text next to a decorative spinner.
- Reduced-motion alternative added.

components.name: Stack
components.description:
Lays its children out in a vertical column with a consistent gap. The gap is a space token
key, never a pixel value. Children can shrink below their content width (`min-inline-size: 0`).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, as a key of the space scale (`4` = `--ds-space-4` = 16px). Default `4`.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis (horizontal) alignment of the children. Default `stretch`.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render, `div` by default. Use `ul` or `ol` for a list of `li` children: the
list reset is applied and `role="list"` keeps the list semantics in Safari.

items.name: AsList
items.description: As a list: the list reset is applied and the list role is kept.

items.name: LongText
items.description: Children shrink instead of overflowing a narrow container.

items.name: RightToLeft
items.description: Mirrors nothing (it is vertical), but start and end alignment follow the writing direction.

docs.summary: A vertical column of children with one consistent gap. The gap is a key of the space scale, never a pixel value.
whenToUse: Stack blocks of content, fields or cards with the same rhythm.
A list of items with a uniform gap (`as="ul"`).
whenNotToUse: For a row of items: use `Inline`.
For a grid of equal cells: use `Grid`.
To space one pair of elements apart once: a margin from the parent is simpler. Use the layout components for repeated structure.
examples:

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Stack blocks of content, fields or cards with the same rhythm.
- A list of items with a uniform gap (`as="ul"`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a row of items: use `Inline`.
- For a grid of equal cells: use `Grid`.
- To space one pair of elements apart once: a margin from the parent is simpler. Use the layout components for repeated structure.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (flex column, gap)
  children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop    | Type                                                | Default     | Notes                                                       |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gap`   | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 8 \| 12 \| 16`       | `4`         | Space token key: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64 px        |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'stretch'`         | `'stretch'` | Horizontal alignment of the children                        |
| `as`    | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'article' \| 'ul' \| 'ol' …` | `'div'`     | `ul` and `ol` get the list reset and `role="list"` (Safari) |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root. The gap travels as the custom property `--ds-stack-gap` (ADR-0002 amendment); a consumer `style` is kept.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A `div` Stack adds no semantics. Choose `as` for the meaning: `ul`/`ol` for lists, `section` with a label for a region.
- `list-style: none` removes list semantics in Safari/VoiceOver, so lists get an explicit `role="list"`.
- Children can shrink below their content width (`min-inline-size: 0`), so long text wraps instead of overflowing at 320px.
- Direction-neutral: `start` and `end` follow the writing direction.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - None. Stack holds whatever its children are.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff had no layout primitives; screens used inline `display: flex` styles with raw pixel gaps. Gaps are now token keys, typed, with no raw pixels.
