components.description:
A text field that turns what you type into removable tags: `Enter` or a comma adds the
tag, pasting `a, b, c` adds three, `Backspace` on the empty input removes the last one.
Duplicates are ignored with a polite message; `maxTags` and `validateTag` reject with an
error that is read aloud.

Built from `TagGroup` / `Tag` and React Aria `TextField`. The tags are a keyboard-navigable
list (one tab stop; `Shift+Tab` from the input reaches it, `Backspace` or `Delete` on a tag
removes it), the input is a normal text box. The value is the list of tags; with `name` each
tag is submitted as a hidden field.

For choosing from known options use `Combobox`; for filters that are always visible use
`ToggleGroup`.

props.name: value
props.description: The tags (controlled). Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial tags (uncontrolled).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the full list of tags whenever a tag is added or removed.

props.name: name
props.description:
Name used to submit the tags with a form. Each tag is submitted as its own hidden field with
this name (read them with `formData.getAll(name)`). The text being typed is never submitted.

props.name: form
props.description: The `id` of the `<form>` the hidden fields belong to, when the field is outside it.

props.name: inputValue
props.description: The text in the input, not yet a tag (controlled). Pair with `onInputChange`.

props.name: defaultInputValue
props.description: The initial text in the input (uncontrolled).

props.name: onInputChange
props.description: Called with the text of the input as the user types.

props.name: delimiters
props.description:
Characters that end a tag while typing and split pasted text. `Enter` always adds the tag,
and line breaks always split pasted text. Default `[',']`. Pass `[]` to use only `Enter`.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: Maximum number of tags. Trying to add another shows an error and keeps the text.

props.name: validateTag
props.description:
Decides whether a tag may be added. Return a message to reject it ("Use letters and digits
only."); return nothing to accept it. The message is shown as the field error and read
aloud. It receives the trimmed text.

props.name: caseSensitive
props.description: Treat "Notebook" and "notebook" as different tags. Default: they are the same, and the second is ignored.

props.name: addOnBlur
props.description: Turns the text left in the input into a tag when the input loses focus. Default `true`.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the control. Linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description:
Error text from your own validation, shown while the field is invalid (`isInvalid`). The
messages of `validateTag` and `maxTags` take its place while they apply.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown while the field has no tags and no text. Never a substitute for the label.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. The box grows when tags wrap.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the field root.

props.name: inputClassName
props.description: Class name for the text `<input>`.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the text `<input>`. The `ref` prop points at the field root.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ tagsLabel: (fieldLabel?: string) => string; added: (tag: string) => string; addedMany: (count: number) => string; removed: (tag: string) => string; duplicate: (tag: string) => string; duplicates: (count: number) => string; maxReached: (max: number) => string; } & { ...; }>
props.description:
Message overrides for this instance: `tagsLabel`, `added`, `addedMany`, `removed`,
`duplicate`, `duplicates`, `maxReached`, `requiredMark`. The remove button of a tag uses the
`Tag` messages.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the field root `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the field.

items.name: BackspaceRemovesLast
items.description: `Backspace` on the empty input removes the last tag.

items.name: RemoveWithKeyboard
items.description: The input is a tab stop of its own; `Shift+Tab` reaches the tags, where `Delete` removes one.

docs.summary:
A text field that turns what you type into removable tags: `Enter` or a comma adds a tag, pasting `a, b, c` adds three, `Backspace` on the empty input removes the last one. Built from `TagGroup` / `Tag` and React Aria `TextField`. The value is the list of tags; with `name` each tag is submitted as a hidden form field.

- TODO `GAP-005`.
whenToUse: Free-form lists the user types: keywords, e-mail recipients, labels, SKUs.
When the list can grow beyond what you want to show as checkboxes.
whenNotToUse: Choosing from known options: use `Combobox` (or `Select`).
A fixed set of filters that are always visible: use `ToggleGroup`.
Showing tags the user cannot edit: use `TagGroup`.
keyboard: The input is a normal `textbox` named by the label. The tags are a `grid` named "Products, added tags" with one `row` per tag (React Aria `TagGroup`): `Shift+Tab` from the input reaches the tags; a row, then its remove button, are tab stops; `←` / `→` move between tags; `Backspace` or `Delete` on a focused tag removes it. After the last tag is removed focus returns to the input.
examples:
<TagInput label="Products" name="products" value={products} onChange={setProducts} maxTags={10} />

<TagInput
  label="Recipients"
  delimiters={[',', ';']}
  validateTag={(tag) => (tag.includes('@') ? undefined : 'Enter a complete email address.')}
/>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Free-form lists the user types: keywords, e-mail recipients, labels, SKUs.
- When the list can grow beyond what you want to show as checkboxes.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Choosing from known options: use `Combobox` (or `Select`).
- A fixed set of filters that are always visible: use `ToggleGroup`.
- Showing tags the user cannot edit: use `TagGroup`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (field root)
  Label
  div.control                     (the bordered box, wraps over several rows)
    TagGroup[role=grid] aria-label    (only while there are tags; one row per tag)
      Tag > text + remove button (24x24)
    input[type=text]              (the textbox; named by the Label)
  Description
  FieldError                      (role=alert: validation and maximum)
  div[role=status]                (polite: added, removed, duplicate; visible for a duplicate)
  input[type=hidden] x N          (only with `name`)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                                     | Type                           | Default      | Notes                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`               | `ReactNode` / `string`         | one required | Names the field. Enforced by the types.                                                              |
| `value` / `defaultValue`                                 | `readonly string[]`            | `[]`         | Controlled / uncontrolled tags.                                                                      |
| `onChange`                                               | `(tags: string[]) => void`     | none         | Called with the full list after each addition or removal.                                            |
| `inputValue` / `defaultInputValue` / `onInputChange`     | `string`                       | `''`         | The text being typed, when you need to own it.                                                       |
| `name` / `form`                                          | `string`                       | none         | Each tag is submitted as its own field (`formData.getAll(name)`). The draft text is never submitted. |
| `delimiters`                                             | `readonly string[]`            | `[',']`      | End a tag while typing and split pasted text. `Enter` always adds; line breaks always split a paste. |
| `maxTags`                                                | `number`                       | none         | Error "You can add up to N tags." when exceeded; the text is kept.                                   |
| `validateTag`                                            | `(tag) => string \| undefined` | none         | Return a message to reject a tag. Shown as the field error and read aloud.                           |
| `caseSensitive`                                          | `boolean`                      | `false`      | By default `Notebook` and `notebook` are the same tag.                                               |
| `addOnBlur`                                              | `boolean`                      | `true`       | Turns the text left in the input into a tag on blur.                                                 |
| `description` / `errorMessage`                           | `ReactNode`                    | none         | Helper text; your own error while `isInvalid`.                                                       |
| `placeholder`                                            | `string`                       | none         | Shown only while there are no tags.                                                                  |
| `size`                                                   | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`         | `'md'`       | Minimum height 32 / 40 / 48px; the box grows when tags wrap.                                         |
| `isDisabled` / `isReadOnly` / `isRequired` / `isInvalid` | `boolean`                      | `false`      | `isRequired` is satisfied by one tag. Read-only and disabled fields show no remove buttons.          |
| `messages`                                               | see below                      | none         | Per-instance message overrides.                                                                      |

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.content:
| Input                                        | Result                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` with text                            | Adds the tag (trimmed), clears the input. Does not submit the form. `Enter` on an empty input submits as usual. |
| A delimiter key (`,`)                        | Same as `Enter`; the character is never typed.                                                                  |
| Paste with delimiters or line breaks         | Adds every piece. Duplicates are skipped; a message counts them. A paste without delimiters is a normal paste.  |
| `Backspace` on an empty input                | Removes the last tag (announced: "Removed “headphones”.").                                                      |
| Duplicate                                    | Ignored, input cleared, polite message "“notebook” is already added." Not an error.                             |
| Beyond `maxTags` / rejected by `validateTag` | Error (`role="alert"`, field invalid), nothing is added, the text stays so it can be fixed.                     |
| Blur with text                               | Adds it (`addOnBlur`).                                                                                          |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The input is a normal `textbox` named by the label. The tags are a `grid` named "Products, added tags" with one `row` per tag (React Aria `TagGroup`): `Shift+Tab` from the input reaches the tags; a row, then its remove button, are tab stops; `←` / `→` move between tags; `Backspace` or `Delete` on a focused tag removes it. After the last tag is removed focus returns to the input.
- Remove buttons are 24x24 and named "Remove notebook" (message `Tag.remove`).
- Additions, removals and duplicates are announced in one polite `role="status"` region; errors are in the field's `role="alert"` message, linked with `aria-describedby`. Only duplicates are also shown as text below the box, so the notice is not color-only; the error is text and the box border turns danger.
- The click target of the whole box focuses the input.
- Contrast: the box border is `--ds-line-control` (3:1) in every state, as in the other fields.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Label as a noun phrase ("Products", "Recipients"). Placeholder: an example or an action ("Add a product"), never the label.
- `validateTag` messages say how to fix it: "Enter a complete email address."
- Tags are shown as typed (trimmed); sorting is up to you.

sections.heading: Messages (`messages` prop, or `DSProvider messages={{ TagInput: … }}`)
sections.content: `tagsLabel(fieldLabel?)`, `added(tag)`, `addedMany(count)`, `removed(tag)`, `duplicate(tag)`, `duplicates(count)`, `maxReached(max)`, `requiredMark`. English and `pt-BR` ship with the library. The remove button uses the `Tag` messages.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<TagInput label="Products" name="products" value={products} onChange={setProducts} maxTags={10} />

<TagInput
  label="Recipients"
  delimiters={[',', ';']}
  validateTag={(tag) => (tag.includes('@') ? undefined : 'Enter a complete email address.')}
/>
```

components.name: Text
components.description:
Body text on the type scale. It sets size, line height, color tone and an optional mono
face; the element (`as`) carries the meaning. Use `Heading` for headings and `Code` for code.

props.name: size
props.description:
Type scale step: `body` 15px, `small` 14px, `label` 13px, `meta` 12px, or `caption` 11.5px.
`caption` is always Geist Mono, uppercase by CSS, with extra tracking: write the source text
in sentence case. Default `body`.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Text color: `default` (`--ds-text`), `secondary` (`--ds-text-2`, supporting text) or
`tertiary` (`--ds-text-3`, hints). Tertiary passes 4.5:1 on every surface, but signals
the lowest importance: use it for meta and hints, never for primary content. Default `default`.

props.name: mono
props.description: Geist Mono with tabular figures, for codes, identifiers, amounts and shortcuts.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Keeps the text on one line and cuts it with an ellipsis. Put the full text in `title` or nearby for sighted users.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. Default `span`, which is safe inside any inline context; use `p` for a paragraph.

items.name: Caption
items.description: Mono, uppercase by CSS and tracked: the source text stays in sentence case.

items.name: Tertiary
items.description: Tertiary text is for hints on the base surfaces. It is too faint on raised and hover surfaces.

items.name: Truncated
items.description: One line, cut with an ellipsis.

docs.summary: Body text on the type scale, with a tone, an optional mono face and truncation.
whenToUse: Paragraphs, supporting lines, labels, counts, metadata and small captions.
Anywhere a size from the type scale or a secondary tone is needed on plain text.
whenNotToUse: Headings: use `Heading`.
Code: use `Code`.
Links: use `Link`. Field labels: use the `Label` of the field.
examples:
<Text as="p">Your order has shipped.</Text>
<Text size="small" tone="secondary">Updated 2 minutes ago</Text>
<Text size="caption" tone="secondary">Shipping</Text>
<Text mono>ORD-1048</Text>
<Text truncate>{longFileName}</Text>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Paragraphs, supporting lines, labels, counts, metadata and small captions.
- Anywhere a size from the type scale or a secondary tone is needed on plain text.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Headings: use `Heading`.
- Code: use `Code`.
- Links: use `Link`. Field labels: use the `Label` of the field.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span (or the element in `as`)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop       | Type                                                      | Default     | Notes                                                                             |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`     | `'body' \| 'small' \| 'label' \| 'meta' \| 'caption'`     | `'body'`    | 15/24 · 14/22 · 13/18 · 12/16 · 11.5/16 px. `caption` is mono, uppercase, tracked |
| `tone`     | `'default' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary'`                  | `'default'` | `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`                                         |
| `mono`     | `boolean`                                                 | `false`     | Geist Mono with tabular figures, for codes, amounts and shortcuts                 |
| `truncate` | `boolean`                                                 | `false`     | One line with an ellipsis. Becomes a block                                        |
| `as`       | `'span' \| 'p' \| 'div' \| 'label' \| 'strong' \| 'em' …` | `'span'`    | Pick the element for the meaning                                                  |

Other attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `tertiary` passes 4.5:1 on every surface (TOK-004), but it carries the lowest importance: use it for hints and meta, never for primary content.
- Truncated text hides content visually: show the full value elsewhere (a `title`, a tooltip, a detail view) when it matters.
- The caption's uppercase is CSS only, so screen readers read the sentence-case source.
- Long unbroken values wrap (`overflow-wrap: break-word`).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Sentence case. Numbers, codes and amounts go in `mono`, formatted with `Intl` (see `utils`).

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Text as="p">Your order has shipped.</Text>
<Text size="small" tone="secondary">Updated 2 minutes ago</Text>
<Text size="caption" tone="secondary">Shipping</Text>
<Text mono>ORD-1048</Text>
<Text truncate>{longFileName}</Text>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content: - The handoff repeated font sizes and colors per element in inline styles. Text maps them to the type and text tokens, with `caption` defined once (mono, uppercase, +8% tracking).

components.description: Multi-line text field built on React Aria `TextField` + `TextArea`. Same contract as `Input`.

props.description: Message overrides for this instance: `count`, `remaining`, `over`, `requiredMark`.

props.name: ref

props.name: label

docs.summary: Multi-line text field. Same contract as [Input](../Input/Input.md) (label, description, error, states, validation timing from [Field](../Field/Field.md)), plus an aside, auto-growing height and a character count. Built on React Aria `TextField` + `TextArea`.
whenToUse: Notes, comments, descriptions, messages longer than a line.
whenNotToUse: One line of text: `Input`.
Rich text or Markdown editing: a dedicated editor.
keyboard: Keyboard: standard text editing; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Tab` leaves the field.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Notes, comments, descriptions, messages longer than a line.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- One line of text: `Input`.
- Rich text or Markdown editing: a dedicated editor.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`       | As in `Input`.                                                                                                           |
| `aside`                                      | Text on the label line, aligned to the end ("Optional", "Markdown supported"). Part of the description, not of the name. |
| `rows`                                       | Visible lines. Default 3.                                                                                                |
| `resize`                                     | `none`, `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, `both`.                                                                      |
| `autoGrow`                                   | Grows with its content; the manual resize handle is off.                                                                 |
| `maxLength` + `showCount`                    | Shows "used / max" on the label line and announces the remaining characters politely.                                    |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)` | React Aria naming; `onChange` receives the string.                                                                       |
| `textareaRef` / `ref`                        | `textareaRef` is the `<textarea>`, `ref` the field root.                                                                 |
| `messages`                                   | `count`, `remaining`, `over`, `requiredMark`.                                                                            |

sections.heading: Character count
sections.content:
- The visible counter ("12 / 200", formatted for the locale) is `aria-hidden`: announcing it on every keystroke would drown the user.
- A separate visually hidden `role="status"` (polite) region announces "N characters remaining" once typing has paused for one second. It stays silent until the value changes, and says "N characters over the limit" when a controlled value exceeds `maxLength`.
- Plural forms and the pt-BR text come from `Textarea.messages.ts`. Override `count`, `remaining` and `over` per instance or via `DSProvider messages={{ Textarea: { ... } }}`.
- `showCount` has no effect without `maxLength`. The native `maxLength` stops typing at the limit.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Native `<textarea>` named by its label; `aside` and `description` are in `aria-describedby` (description first, then aside).
- Keyboard: standard text editing; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Tab` leaves the field.
- Auto-grow keeps all content visible (no inner scrollbar), which helps zoom and reflow.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Textarea label="Notes" aside="Optional" description="Plain text only." maxLength={500} showCount />
<Textarea label="Message" autoGrow rows={2} isRequired errorMessage="Write a message." />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `aside` is associated with the field; it was a floating span.
- New: `autoGrow`, character count with a debounced polite announcement, read-only, shared validation timing.
- Focus styling is CSS and survives consumer `onFocus`/`onBlur`.
- `resize` accepts four values and is ignored with `autoGrow`.

components.description:
A chronological list of events. It is an ordered list; each event has a `<time>`, a title, an

docs.summary: A chronological list of events: when it happened, what happened, who did it, and an optional detail and tone marker. It is a semantic ordered list, newest event first by default.
whenToUse: The history of a record or a process: status changes, comments, deliveries, audit entries.
Events that have a time and read as a story, a few lines each.
whenNotToUse: Tabular data that people sort and compare: use `DataTable`.
The steps of a flow someone is going through now: use `Stepper`.
The state of a record in a fixed flow: use `StatusSteps`.
Totals and amounts per line: use `LedgerList`.
examples:
<Timeline
  aria-label="Request history"
  items={[
    { id: 'a', time: '2026-10-28T09:15:00Z', title: 'Request created', actor: 'Ana Costa' },
    { id: 'b', time: '2026-10-31T16:05:00Z', title: 'Request approved', tone: 'success' },
  ]}
/>

<Timeline aria-label="Audit log" items={events} order="oldest-first" timeZone="UTC" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- The history of a record or a process: status changes, comments, deliveries, audit entries.
- Events that have a time and read as a story, a few lines each.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Tabular data that people sort and compare: use `DataTable`.
- The steps of a flow someone is going through now: use `Stepper`.
- The state of a record in a fixed flow: use `StatusSteps`.
- Totals and amounts per line: use `LedgerList`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
ol[aria-label]
  li[data-tone]
    marker (aria-hidden)         dot (neutral) | icon: accent info, success check, warning triangle, danger circle
    div
      title                      VisuallyHidden tone text ("Success") + title
      meta                       "By <actor>" · <time dateTime>
      description                optional
  connector line                 (CSS pseudo-element, decorative)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop       | Type                                             | Default          | Notes                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`    | `TimelineItem[]`                                 |                  | `{ id, time, title, description?, tone?, actor? }`                                     |
| `order`    | `'newest-first' \| 'oldest-first' \| 'as-given'` | `'newest-first'` | Dated records are newest first (AGENTS.md section 5, rule 5b). Does not mutate `items` |
| `timeZone` | `string`                                         | viewer's zone    | IANA zone for date-times                                                               |
| `empty`    | `ReactNode`                                      |                  | Rendered instead of the list when `items` is empty                                     |
| `messages` | `{ accent, success, warning, danger, actor }`    |                  | Per-instance overrides                                                                 |

`time` is an ISO 8601 date-time, a `Date`, or a date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` (shown as a date without a time, in UTC so the day never shifts). Other `ol` attributes (`aria-label`, `id`) and `ref` go to the list; name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the heading does not.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A real ordered list; each time is a `<time dateTime>` with a machine-readable value, and its text comes from `Intl` for the active locale (never hand-built).
- The tone is not only color and icon: a visually hidden prefix ("Success", "Warning", "Error", "Highlighted", from messages) comes before the title. The marker and the line are `aria-hidden`.
- The list is not interactive, so it has no keyboard behavior of its own; put links or buttons in the `title` or `description` when an event needs an action.
- Text uses `text` and `text-2` (4.5:1 on the page surface). Forced colors: markers and line use system colors.
- Reflow: text wraps (long words break) and the layout is a single column, so it works at 320 px.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: what happened, past tense, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Order shipped", "Request approved").
- Description: one short sentence of detail, only when it adds something.
- Actor: a person or system name. The component adds "By".
- Do not repeat the time in the title.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Timeline
  aria-label="Request history"
  items={[
    { id: 'a', time: '2026-10-28T09:15:00Z', title: 'Request created', actor: 'Ana Costa' },
    { id: 'b', time: '2026-10-31T16:05:00Z', title: 'Request approved', tone: 'success' },
  ]}
/>

<Timeline aria-label="Audit log" items={events} order="oldest-first" timeZone="UTC" />
```

Renders the toasts of a queue. Mount **one** near the app root, inside `DSProvider`, and call
`toast()` from anywhere. Built on React Aria's toast region (isolated in `toast.rac.ts`).

The region is a landmark named "Toast notifications" that `F6` moves into; the timer of every toast
pauses while the pointer is over the region or focus is inside it (WCAG 2.2.1). Toasts stack
at the bottom center of the viewport, clear of side panels, above dialogs and below tooltips.

items.description:
The undo pattern: do the action at once, tell the user in a toast, offer Undo. No
confirmation dialog for reversible actions. Press the button, then Tab to Undo.

docs.summary:
A short, temporary message about something that just happened, with an optional action (usually Undo). Mount one `ToastRegion` and call `toast()` from anywhere. Built on React Aria's toast region and queue.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Toast` (CMP-FBK-02). Undo recipe: GAP-008 groundwork.
whenToUse: Feedback for an action that finished: "Order #1051 created", "3 items archived".
Reversible actions, with **Undo**.
whenNotToUse: A state that stays on the page ("Scheduled maintenance"): use `Alert`.
A field error: use the field's error message.
Anything the user must read to proceed: use `Dialog` or `Alert`. A toast disappears.
The only place an essential result is shown: toasts can be missed.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Feedback for an action that finished: "Order #1051 created", "3 items archived".
- Reversible actions, with **Undo**.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A state that stays on the page ("Scheduled maintenance"): use `Alert`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- Anything the user must read to proceed: use `Dialog` or `Alert`. A toast disappears.
- The only place an essential result is shown: toasts can be missed.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
ToastRegion          role=region, aria-label "Toast notifications", landmark (F6); fixed, bottom center; z toast
  Toast              role=alertdialog (React Aria), raised surface, strong line, radius lg, overlay shadow
    dot              decorative, colored by tone
    message          "Success: " (visually hidden) + text
    Button           optional action ("Undo")
    IconButton       "Dismiss notification"
```

sections.heading: API
Default timeout: 5000 ms
sections.content: The handoff closed toasts after 3.6 s, which is too short to read a sentence and reach Undo (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable). The default is 5 s **and** the timer pauses while the pointer is over the toast region or focus is inside it, so a keyboard or slow reader can always finish. Use `timeout: null` for failures the user has to act on.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The region is a landmark named "Toast notifications". **F6** moves focus into it (and back), so Undo is keyboard reachable. React Aria registers a region as a landmark only if it is mounted with its first toast, so `ToastRegion` renders nothing while the queue is empty and mounts the region when a toast arrives.
- Each toast is announced by React Aria's toast semantics. The tone is spoken as a prefix ("Success: ...", "Error: ...") from messages; the colored dot is decorative and `aria-hidden`.
- Pause on hover and on focus within the region; the timer resumes on leave or blur.
- Dismiss button named from messages ("Dismiss notification"); action is a real `Button`.
- Layer `--ds-z-toast` (58): above dialogs, below tooltips. Bottom center keeps it clear of side panels (Sheet, Sidebar).
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade-in is removed. Forced colors: border and dot use `CanvasText`.
- `UNSTABLE_*` isolation: all React Aria `UNSTABLE_Toast*` imports live in `toast.rac.ts`. Renaming or stabilizing them is a one-file change.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Past tense, short, no exclamation marks: "Order #1051 created", "3 items archived".
- Action: a verb ("Undo"). No "Close" button text; the dismiss control is an icon.
- Do not repeat what is already visible on the page.

sections.heading: The undo pattern (recipe)
Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- A queue and region instead of a single stateless `Toast` you position yourself; timeout, pause on hover/focus, keyboard region, dismiss label from messages.
- 5 s default instead of 3.6 s.
- Tones `info | success | warning | danger` (the handoff's `neutral | accent` dot colors became `info`); the tone is spoken, not only colored.
- Position is bottom center, away from side panels.

components.name: Toggle
components.description:
A button that stays pressed: it switches one setting on or off (bold text, a filter, "show
archived"). Built on React Aria `ToggleButton`: a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`,
toggled by `Enter` and `Space`.

Use it for an independent on/off choice that applies at once. For a setting inside a form
use `Switch` or `Checkbox`; for several related toggles use `ToggleGroup`; for one value out
of a few use `SegmentedControl`.

props.name: children
props.description: Label: a short noun or verb in sentence case ("Bold", "Show archived").

props.name: leading
props.description: Node before the label, usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative; the label names the toggle.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Replaces the accessible name when the visible label is not enough. Rarely needed.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the toggle.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon to draw: one of the curated set (for example `StarIcon`). Decorative inside the button.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name of an icon-only toggle, required. Name what the toggle controls, not what
it looks like and not its state ("Bold", "Show archived"): the pressed state is announced
separately.

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
Shows `label` in a `Tooltip` on hover and keyboard focus. Pass `true`, or an object to add
a shortcut or change the side. The `label` stays the accessible name.

props.name: id
props.description:
Inside a `ToggleGroup`: the value of this toggle in the group's `value` (required there,
unique in the group). Standalone: the DOM id.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual style, as for `Button`. `secondary` (default) has a border; `ghost` has none at rest.
Inside a `ToggleGroup` it defaults to the group's `variant`.

props.name: size
props.description:
Height token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. Inside a `ToggleGroup` it defaults
to the group's `size`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<button>` element.

items.name: KeyboardToggle
items.description: `Space` and `Enter` toggle the focused button.

docs.summary:
A button that stays pressed: it switches one setting on or off (bold text, a filter, "show archived") and applies it at once. A native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, built on React Aria `ToggleButton`. Looks like `Button` (`secondary` and `ghost`), with a clear pressed state.

- TODO `GAP-005`.
whenToUse: One independent on/off choice in a toolbar or filter bar: Bold, Show archived, Only mine.
An icon-only on/off control (Favorite, Pin) with a required `label`.
whenNotToUse: A setting that is saved with a form: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
Several related toggles that share a value: use `ToggleGroup`.
One value out of a few options (View: List, Board): use `SegmentedControl`.
An action that does something once: use `Button`.
keyboard: Keyboard: `Tab` focuses; `Space` and `Enter` toggle.
examples:
<Toggle isSelected={showArchived} onChange={setShowArchived}>
  Show archived
</Toggle>

<Toggle icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" tooltip variant="ghost" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- One independent on/off choice in a toolbar or filter bar: Bold, Show archived, Only mine.
- An icon-only on/off control (Favorite, Pin) with a required `label`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A setting that is saved with a form: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- Several related toggles that share a value: use `ToggleGroup`.
- One value out of a few options (View: List, Board): use `SegmentedControl`.
- An action that does something once: use `Button`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
button[aria-pressed]
  leading   (optional, decorative)
  label     (or a single icon when icon-only)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                             | Type                                   | Default       | Notes                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`                       | `ReactNode`                            | required\*    | Label in sentence case. \*Not used by an icon-only toggle.       |
| `icon` + `label`                 | `IconComponent` + `string`             | none          | Icon-only: `label` is required and becomes `aria-label`.         |
| `tooltip`                        | `boolean \| { shortcut?, placement? }` | off           | Icon-only only: shows `label` in a `Tooltip` on hover and focus. |
| `leading`                        | `ReactNode`                            | none          | Decorative node before the label.                                |
| `variant`                        | `'secondary' \| 'ghost'`               | `'secondary'` | As for `Button`. Inside a `ToggleGroup`: the group's `variant`.  |
| `size`                           | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                 | `'md'`        | 32 / 40 / 48px. Inside a `ToggleGroup`: the group's `size`.      |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` | `boolean`                              | `false`       | Controlled / uncontrolled pressed state.                         |
| `onChange`                       | `(isSelected: boolean) => void`        | none          | Called with the new state.                                       |
| `id`                             | `string`                               | none          | Inside a `ToggleGroup`: the toggle's value (required there).     |
| `isDisabled`                     | `boolean`                              | `false`       | Reduced opacity, not focusable.                                  |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Semantics: `<button aria-pressed="true|false">`. Inside a single-selection `ToggleGroup` it is a `radio` with `aria-checked`.
- Keyboard: `Tab` focuses; `Space` and `Enter` toggle.
- The pressed state is shown by a brighter border, a raised fill and ink text, never by color alone. Focus is the accent border and ring.
- Icon-only toggles need a `label` that names what the toggle controls, not its state: the pressed state is announced by the browser. The icon is decorative.
- Targets are at least 32px (`sm`). Forced colors: the pressed toggle gets a `Highlight` border and an underline.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Label with a short noun or verb phrase in sentence case: "Bold", "Show archived". Do not change the label when the state changes ("Hide archived" would be read as the opposite of the state).

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Toggle isSelected={showArchived} onChange={setShowArchived}>
  Show archived
</Toggle>

<Toggle icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" tooltip variant="ghost" />
```

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.description:
A row (or column) of related `Toggle`s that share one value: the list of pressed `id`s.

With the default `multiple` selection the toggles are independent (bold, italic, underline;
or a set of filters) and the group is a `toolbar`. With `single` selection it behaves like
a radio group that can also be empty.

`ToggleGroup` vs `SegmentedControl`: a `SegmentedControl` is one value of one setting (View:
List, Board), exactly one option is always selected. A `ToggleGroup` is a set of on/off
choices where none, one or several are on.

Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup`: one tab stop, arrow keys move between toggles (they
stop at the ends), `Space` and `Enter` toggle the focused one.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Toggle` children. Each needs an `id` that is unique in the group.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the group ("Text formatting"). Required: name this or use `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the group.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description:
`multiple` (default): any number of toggles can be pressed, independently (text formatting,
filters); the group is a toolbar. `single`: at most one is pressed; the group is a radio
group. To pick exactly one value of a setting prefer `SegmentedControl`.

props.name: value
props.description: The `id`s of the pressed toggles (controlled). Pair with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The `id`s of the toggles that start pressed (uncontrolled).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the `id`s of all pressed toggles after the user presses or releases one.

props.name: disallowEmptySelection
props.description: Keeps at least one toggle pressed. Pointless in `multiple` mode unless you want that rule.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout and arrow keys: `horizontal` (default, `←` `→`) or `vertical` (`↑` `↓`).

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style handed down to every `Toggle` that does not set its own.

props.name: size
props.description: Size handed down to every `Toggle` that does not set its own.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the group element.

items.name: KeyboardSelection
items.description: One tab stop. Arrows move focus (and stop at the ends), Space and Enter press.

docs.summary:
A row (or column) of related `Toggle`s that share one value: the list of pressed `id`s. With the default `multiple` selection the toggles are independent (bold, italic, underline; a set of filters). With `single` selection at most one is pressed. Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup`.

- TODO `GAP-005`.
whenToUse: Text formatting (Bold, Italic), list markers, or a small set of filters that combine.
whenNotToUse: A single on/off choice: use `Toggle`.
Choosing one value of a setting: use `SegmentedControl`.
A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.
keyboard: Keyboard: one tab stop; `←` / `→` (`↑` / `↓` when vertical) move focus and stop at the ends (React Aria does not wrap); `Space` and `Enter` press the focused toggle. Disabled toggles are skipped.
examples:
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Text formatting" value={marks} onChange={setMarks}>
  <Toggle id="fav" icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" />
  <Toggle id="pin" icon={StarIcon} label="Pinned" />
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup aria-label="Order filters" defaultValue={['mine']}>
  <Toggle id="mine">Only mine</Toggle>
  <Toggle id="late">Late</Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>

sections.heading: ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl
sections.content:
|           | `SegmentedControl`                           | `ToggleGroup`                                                    |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Meaning   | One value of one setting (View: List, Board) | Independent on/off choices (Bold, Italic; filters)               |
| Selection | Exactly one option, always                   | None, one or several (`multiple`), or none/one                   |
| Role      | `radiogroup` of `radio`                      | `toolbar` of `button[aria-pressed]` (`radiogroup` when `single`) |
| Value     | `string`                                     | `string[]`                                                       |
| Content   | `options` array with optional counts         | `Toggle` children, text or icon-only                             |

Rule of thumb: if choosing one option makes the others "not selected" and one must always be on, use `SegmentedControl`. If each choice can stand alone, use `ToggleGroup`. Use `single` here only when "nothing selected" is meaningful (for example an optional filter).

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Text formatting (Bold, Italic), list markers, or a small set of filters that combine.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A single on/off choice: use `Toggle`.
- Choosing one value of a setting: use `SegmentedControl`.
- A long list of filters: use `CheckboxGroup` or a `Select`/`Combobox` with multiple selection.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=toolbar] aria-label       (or role=radiogroup when single)
  button[aria-pressed]             (one `Toggle` per choice, each with an id)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                             | Type                         | Default          | Notes                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` | `string`                     | one required     | Names the group ("Text formatting"). Enforced by the types. |
| `children`                       | `Toggle`s                    | required         | Each `Toggle` needs a unique `id`.                          |
| `selectionMode`                  | `'multiple' \| 'single'`     | `'multiple'`     | See the table above.                                        |
| `value` / `defaultValue`         | `readonly string[]`          | `[]`             | Controlled / uncontrolled list of pressed ids.              |
| `onChange`                       | `(value: string[]) => void`  | none             | Called with all pressed ids after each change.              |
| `disallowEmptySelection`         | `boolean`                    | `false`          | Keeps at least one toggle pressed.                          |
| `orientation`                    | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'`   | Layout and arrow keys.                                      |
| `variant` / `size`               | as `Toggle`                  | `secondary`/`md` | Defaults for the toggles; a toggle's own props win.         |
| `isDisabled`                     | `boolean`                    | `false`          | Disables every toggle.                                      |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Semantics: `multiple` is a `toolbar` (a group of buttons with `aria-pressed`); `single` is a `radiogroup` of `radio` buttons. The group needs an accessible name (enforced by the types).
- Keyboard: one tab stop; `←` / `→` (`↑` / `↓` when vertical) move focus and stop at the ends (React Aria does not wrap); `Space` and `Enter` press the focused toggle. Disabled toggles are skipped.
- Pressed state is shown by border, fill and ink text, not by color alone.
- Icon-only toggles need a `label`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content: - Group name: a noun phrase ("Text formatting", "Filters"). Toggle labels: one word or a short phrase in sentence case.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Text formatting" value={marks} onChange={setMarks}>
  <Toggle id="fav" icon={StarIcon} label="Favorite" />
  <Toggle id="pin" icon={StarIcon} label="Pinned" />
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup aria-label="Order filters" defaultValue={['mine']}>
  <Toggle id="mine">Only mine</Toggle>
  <Toggle id="late">Late</Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>
```

The steps of a multi-step agent run as an ordered list of `ToolCallStep`. Use it under the
message the run belongs to; each step opens its own details.

props.name: steps

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the list. Defaults to "Steps"; say which run it is ("Steps of the order check").

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ running: string; succeeded: string; failed: string; input: string; output: string; error: string; finishedSucceeded: (name: string) => string; finishedFailed: (name: string) => string; listLabel: string; }>

keys.description: Visible status text of a step.
Labels of the detail blocks, and the accessible names of their code blocks.
Label of the output block when the step failed.

whenToUse: Under an assistant message, to show what the agent did before it answered ("search_orders", "draft_reply").
A run log where the owner wants to check why the agent answered as it did.
whenNotToUse: Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.

sections.heading: When to use

- Under an assistant message, to show what the agent did before it answered ("search_orders", "draft_reply").
- A run log where the owner wants to check why the agent answered as it did.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Progress of a long job with a known number of steps: use `StatusSteps` or `Progress`.
- Something the owner has to approve: use `ApprovalCard`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div (ToolCallStep)
  h{headingLevel} > button   chevron · status icon + text · name (mono) · duration (mono)
  details (when open)        "Input" label + code block · "Output" or "Error" label + code block
  status                     visually hidden live region
ol (ToolCallList)            one li per step
```

Without `input` and `output` the header is plain text and there is nothing to open.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                                  | Type                                   | Default | Notes                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                                                | `string`                               | -       | Required. Mono; part of the button name.                                     |
| `status`                                              | `'running' \| 'succeeded' \| 'failed'` | -       | Required. Always shown as text plus an icon (Spinner while running).         |
| `durationMs`                                          | `number`                               |         | Milliseconds. Shown as `85 ms` or `1.2 s`, formatted with the active locale. |
| `input` / `output`                                    | `ReactNode`                            |         | A string goes in a `Code` block; nodes are rendered as given.                |
| `isExpanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange` | `boolean` / `boolean` / `(b) => void`  | closed  | Controlled or uncontrolled details.                                          |
| `headingLevel`                                        | `1`-`6`                                | `4`     |                                                                              |
| `messages`                                            | partial catalog                        |         | `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `input`, `output`, `error`, announcements. |

`ToolCallList` takes `steps` (each a `ToolCallStep` prop set plus a stable `stepId`), an `aria-label` (default "Steps") and `messages`, which it shares with every step.

sections.heading: Accessibility

- The header is a button inside a heading (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`); `Enter` and `Space` toggle it.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description:
An ink-style hint for a control, built on React Aria `TooltipTrigger` and `Tooltip`.

It opens on hover (after a delay) and on keyboard focus, closes with `Escape` (WCAG 1.4.13),
stays open while the pointer is over it, and describes the trigger through `aria-describedby`.
A tooltip is a supplement: the trigger must already have its own accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description:
The element the tooltip describes. It must be focusable and built on React Aria, such as
`Button`, `IconButton` or `Link`, so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus as well as hover.

props.name: content
props.description:
Short text, a few words. It is linked to the trigger with `aria-describedby`, so it must
add detail only: never put the only copy of essential information in a tooltip, because
touch users cannot hover and the text is not shown until the trigger is focused.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard shortcut shown after the text in mono type ("⌘K"). Pair it with `aria-keyshortcuts` on the trigger.

props.name: placement
props.description: Side of the trigger, `top` by default. `start` and `end` follow the writing direction.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds before opening on hover. Default 500. Focus opens it immediately.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: Milliseconds before closing after the pointer leaves. Default 0.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Never opens when `true`, for example while the trigger is disabled.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the tooltip opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the tooltip bubble.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the tooltip bubble.

items.name: Default
items.description: Keyboard focus opens the tooltip at once; `Escape` dismisses it while the trigger keeps focus.

items.name: Open
items.description: Open for the visual review.

items.name: OnIconButton
items.description: An icon-only control already has its name; the tooltip repeats it and can add the shortcut.

items.name: Disabled
items.description: Never opens while disabled.

docs.summary:
A short, ink-style hint for a control. Built on React Aria `TooltipTrigger` and `Tooltip`.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Tooltip` (CMP-FBK-04).
whenToUse: Name or add a shortcut to an icon-only control ("Add order", with `N`).
Explain a truncated label, in a few words.
whenNotToUse: Essential information (an error, a requirement, a price). **A tooltip is never the only source of essential information**: touch users cannot hover, and the text is not shown until the trigger is focused or hovered.
Interactive content (links, buttons, forms): use `Popover`.
A long explanation: put it in the page, or use a `Popover`.
keyboard: Opens on **keyboard focus and hover**, closes on blur, pointer leave or `Escape` (WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible). The pointer can move onto the tooltip without closing it (hoverable), and it stays until dismissed (persistent).
examples:
<Tooltip content="Add order" shortcut="N">
  <IconButton label="Add order" icon={PlusIcon} />
</Tooltip>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Name or add a shortcut to an icon-only control ("Add order", with `N`).
- Explain a truncated label, in a few words.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Essential information (an error, a requirement, a price). **A tooltip is never the only source of essential information**: touch users cannot hover, and the text is not shown until the trigger is focused or hovered.
- Interactive content (links, buttons, forms): use `Popover`.
- A long explanation: put it in the page, or use a `Popover`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
TooltipTrigger
  trigger            Button | IconButton | Link   (focusable, React Aria based)
  Tooltip            role=tooltip, primary background, label type, radius sm
    content          text
    shortcut         optional, mono caption, --ds-primary-fg-muted
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                     | Type                                    | Default | Notes                                                           |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`               | `ReactElement`                          | none    | The trigger. Must be focusable and React Aria based.            |
| `content`                | `ReactNode`                             | none    | A few words.                                                    |
| `shortcut`               | `string`                                |         | Mono text after the content ("Ctrl+K").                         |
| `placement`              | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'start' \| 'end'` | `top`   | `start`/`end` follow the writing direction; collisions flip it. |
| `delay`                  | `number`                                | `500`   | ms before a hover opens it. Focus opens it immediately.         |
| `closeDelay`             | `number`                                | `0`     | ms before it closes after the pointer leaves.                   |
| `isDisabled`             | `boolean`                               | `false` | Never opens.                                                    |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean`                               |         | Controlled / uncontrolled.                                      |
| `onOpenChange`           | `(isOpen: boolean) => void`             |         |                                                                 |

`TOOLTIP_DELAY` (500) is exported. The handoff used no delay; React Aria's own default (1500 ms) feels slow for a dense tool.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Role `tooltip`, linked to the trigger with `aria-describedby` while open. The trigger keeps its own accessible name.
- Opens on **keyboard focus and hover**, closes on blur, pointer leave or `Escape` (WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible). The pointer can move onto the tooltip without closing it (hoverable), and it stays until dismissed (persistent).
- Placement is collision-aware.
- Contrast: `--ds-primary-fg` on `--ds-primary-bg`; the shortcut uses `--ds-primary-fg-muted` (at least 4.5:1 on the ink surface).
- Reduced motion: the 150 ms fade is disabled. Forced colors: a `CanvasText` border is drawn.
- Layer: `--ds-z-tooltip`, the top of the stack.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Sentence case, no final period for a fragment, no exclamation marks.
- Do not repeat a visible label; add the shortcut or the missing detail.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Tooltip content="Add order" shortcut="N">
  <IconButton label="Add order" icon={PlusIcon} />
</Tooltip>
```

`IconButton` also takes a `tooltip` prop that does this for you.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Built on React Aria: focus and hover, `Escape`, `aria-describedby`, hoverable content and collision-aware placement came for free; the handoff used a `span` with mouse handlers and absolute positioning.
- All four sides; delay; controlled state; `isDisabled`.
- No `forceOpen`: use `defaultOpen` or `isOpen`.

components.name: TopBar
components.description:
The page header: a title with an optional subtitle, or a breadcrumb trail, and an actions
slot. It is a `header` element, `--ds-topbar-h` (64px) high, with a bottom divider. It does
not stick by itself; position it in your layout.

props.name: title
props.description:
The title of the page or section. Rendered as a heading (see `headingLevel`). Ignored
when `breadcrumb` is set: the trail then names the page and the page supplies its own `h1`.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: One short line under the title (a count, a date, an environment). Not used with `breadcrumb`.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title, `1` by default (one `h1` per page).

props.name: breadcrumb
props.description: A breadcrumb trail shown instead of the title.

props.name: children
props.description: Free content next to the title, for example a `Badge` or a `SegmentedControl`.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Actions at the end of the bar. Put the single primary action of the screen last, as a
`Button variant="primary"` with its shortcut as a `Kbd` in `trailing`.

docs.summary:
The page header: a title with an optional subtitle, or a breadcrumb trail, and a slot for actions. A `header` element, 64px high (`--ds-topbar-h`), with a bottom divider.

- Handoff source: `components/layout/TopBar.jsx` (TODO `CMP-LAY-02`).
whenToUse: At the top of the content area of an app shell, next to the `Sidebar`.
To hold the single primary action of the screen, at the top right, with its keyboard shortcut.
whenNotToUse: For the heading of a card or section: use `Card` or a heading.
For a floating or sticky toolbar: position this component in your layout instead.
examples:
<TopBar
  title="Orders"
  subtitle="1,248 orders"
  actions={
    <Button variant="primary" trailing={<Kbd keys={['N']} />}>
      Create order
    </Button>
  }
/>

<TopBar breadcrumb={[{ label: 'Orders', href: '/orders' }, { label: 'ORD-1048' }]} />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- At the top of the content area of an app shell, next to the `Sidebar`.
- To hold the single primary action of the screen, at the top right, with its keyboard shortcut.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For the heading of a card or section: use `Card` or a heading.
- For a floating or sticky toolbar: position this component in your layout instead.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type               | Default | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`        | none    | Rendered as a heading. Ignored when `breadcrumb` is set.                 |
| `subtitle`     | `ReactNode`        | none    | One short line under the title.                                          |
| `headingLevel` | `1`-`6`            | `1`     | One `h1` per page; use another level when the bar sits inside a section. |
| `breadcrumb`   | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | none    | Shown instead of the title. The page then supplies its own `h1`.         |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`        | none    | Free content next to the title: a `Badge`, a `SegmentedControl`.         |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`        | none    | End of the bar. Put the primary action last.                             |

`ref` points to the `<header>`; `className` and other `header` attributes pass through.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A `header` that is not inside `main`, `section` or `article` is the page's banner landmark. Use at most one banner per page; inside a section it is a plain group.
- The title is a real heading. A breadcrumb replaces it, so keep a page-level `h1` elsewhere in that case.
- The title wins the space: content next to it (`children`, such as badges) wraps to a second line before the title truncates, and the bar grows taller. A title truncates with an ellipsis only when it alone is wider than the bar. The actions never shrink or move out of the bar; on narrow screens keep the primary action and put the others in a `Menu`.
- The primary action is a `Button variant="primary"` with its shortcut as a `Kbd` in `trailing`. Register the shortcut with `useHotkey`; `Kbd` only displays it.
- Height is a minimum, so a 200% text zoom grows the bar instead of clipping it.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Titles are nouns in sentence case ("Orders"). Subtitles give context: a count, a date, an environment.
- One primary action per screen, a verb plus object: "Create order".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<TopBar
  title="Orders"
  subtitle="1,248 orders"
  actions={
    <Button variant="primary" trailing={<Kbd keys={['N']} />}>
      Create order
    </Button>
  }
/>

<TopBar breadcrumb={[{ label: 'Orders', href: '/orders' }, { label: 'ORD-1048' }]} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Height is `--ds-topbar-h` (64px) as a minimum; the handoff code used 56px while the tokens and the ERP spec said 64px.
- The title is a heading with a level; `subtitle` is new; `breadcrumb` takes `Breadcrumb` items.
- No `sticky` prop (the handoff hard-coded `z-index: 20`, which is not a layer token). Make it sticky in your layout with a token layer.

alternatives.reason: For the heading of a card or section: use `Card` or a heading.

components.name: Tour
components.description:
A step-by-step onboarding tour. Each step is a non-modal popover (React Aria `Popover` with
`isNonModal`) anchored to an element, with a title, a short text, a "Step 2 of 5" counter and
Skip, Back and Next or Done buttons. The page stays interactive; there is no scrim.

Focus moves into each step as it appears (the step is a named dialog, so a screen reader
announces its title). `Escape` skips the tour. When the tour ends, focus returns to the element
that had it before the tour opened, normally the button that started it.

Use a `Tooltip` for a hint on one control, and a `Popover` for interactive content. A tour is
for a few steps shown once; do not use it to hold documentation.

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps, in order. Each points at one element through `target`.

props.name: step
props.description: Zero-based index of the current step (controlled). Pair with `onStepChange`.

props.name: defaultStep
props.description: Initial step when uncontrolled. Default `0`.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Called when the user moves to another step.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with `false` when the tour is finished or skipped.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Called when the user presses Done on the last step. `onOpenChange(false)` follows.

props.name: onSkip
props.description: Called when the user skips the tour, with `Skip tour` or `Escape`. `onOpenChange(false)` follows.

props.name: placement
props.type: 'bottom' | 'bottom left' | 'bottom right' | 'bottom start' | 'bottom end' | 'top' | 'top left' | 'top right' | 'top start' | 'top end' | 'left' | 'left top' | 'left bottom' | 'start' | 'start top' | 'start bottom' | 'right' | 'right top' | 'right bottom' | 'end' | 'end top' | 'end bottom'
props.description: Side and alignment relative to the target. Default `bottom start`. Flips on collision.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ progress: (current: number, total: number) => string; back: string; next: string; done: string; skip: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the step surface.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the step surface.

keys.description: Progress text of a step, such as "Step 2 of 5".
Goes to the previous step.
Goes to the next step.
Finishes the tour on the last step.
Ends the tour before the last step.

items.name: FirstStep
items.description: Open on the first step for the visual review.

docs.summary: Step-by-step onboarding hints anchored to elements of the page. Each step is a non-modal popover (React Aria `Popover` with `isNonModal`) with a title, a short text, a "Step 2 of 5" counter and Skip, Back and Next or Done buttons. Generic: it lives in the core entry point.
whenToUse: Guiding new users through the interface with a few onboarding hints (three to six steps) that introduce a screen.
Pointing at controls that are not obvious from their label.
whenNotToUse: A hint on one control: `Tooltip`.
Interactive content anchored to a button (filters, a small form): `Popover`.
Documentation or long explanations: link to help instead.
A task the user must finish before going on: `Dialog` or `Sheet`.
keyboard: Focus moves into each step as it appears (the dialog itself, so a screen reader reads its title; the next `Tab` reaches Skip, Back and Next). Pressing Next or Back mounts the next step and moves focus to it, so focus never lands on a removed button.

While a step is open, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` cycle through the step's buttons (React Aria contains focus in the dialog); `Escape` skips the tour and is the keyboard way out. A pointer press elsewhere on the page does not end it, and the page stays visible and readable (no scrim, not inert).

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Guiding new users through the interface with a few onboarding hints (three to six steps) that introduce a screen.
- Pointing at controls that are not obvious from their label.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- A hint on one control: `Tooltip`.
- Interactive content anchored to a button (filters, a small form): `Popover`.
- Documentation or long explanations: link to help instead.
- A task the user must finish before going on: `Dialog` or `Sheet`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
Popover (non-modal, anchored to step.target, z popover, overlay shadow)
  OverlayArrow
  Dialog (role=dialog, named by the title)
    Heading        step title
    content        step text (--ds-text-2)
    footer         "Step 2 of 5" (mono) ... Skip tour (ghost) · Back · Next | Done (primary)
```

The primary button is Next, or Done on the last step. Skip is hidden on the last step, Back on the first.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                                      | Type                                                                   | Default        | Notes                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `steps`                                   | `{ target: RefObject<Element \| null>, title, content, placement? }[]` | required       | A step whose target is not mounted renders nothing.                                          |
| `step` / `defaultStep` / `onStepChange`   | `number`                                                               | `0`            | Zero-based index; controlled / uncontrolled.                                                 |
| `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` |                                                                        | closed         | Controlled / uncontrolled. `onOpenChange(false)` fires when the tour is finished or skipped. |
| `onComplete`                              | `() => void`                                                           |                | Done on the last step.                                                                       |
| `onSkip`                                  | `() => void`                                                           |                | Skip tour or `Escape`.                                                                       |
| `placement`                               | popover placement                                                      | `bottom start` | Flips on collision; each step may override it.                                               |
| `messages`                                | `{ progress, back, next, done, skip }`                                 |                | pt-BR included.                                                                              |

When the tour ends (finished or skipped) an uncontrolled step index returns to the first step.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Each step is a `dialog` named by its title. It is non-modal: the page is not inert, there is no scrim, nothing is hidden from assistive technology.
- Focus moves into each step as it appears (the dialog itself, so a screen reader reads its title; the next `Tab` reaches Skip, Back and Next). Pressing Next or Back mounts the next step and moves focus to it, so focus never lands on a removed button.
- While a step is open, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` cycle through the step's buttons (React Aria contains focus in the dialog); `Escape` skips the tour and is the keyboard way out. A pointer press elsewhere on the page does not end it, and the page stays visible and readable (no scrim, not inert).
- When the tour ends, focus returns to the element that had focus when the tour opened (normally the button that started it); for a tour that is open on first render, to the target of the current step if it is focusable. If the consumer closes a controlled tour from outside, focus is left where the user put it.
- The target is scrolled into view (`block: nearest`) when its step appears. The step is positioned against the target and flips when it does not fit; the arrow points at the target.
- The fade-in is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Visuals are calm: raised surface, strong line and the overlay shadow only; accent is used only for focus rings.
- Because the step is rendered in a portal, it comes last in the Tab order of the page: the user reaches it by the focus that moves into it, not by tabbing from the target.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: the name of the thing, in sentence case ("Filters"). Text: one or two sentences saying what it does, with no exclamation marks or emoji.
- Button labels come from the message catalog: Back, Next, Done, Skip tour.

Hides content visually while keeping it available to assistive technology.
Use it for text alternatives that sighted users do not need.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. Defaults to `span`.

docs.summary: Hides content visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree. It renders a `span` (or the element given by `as`) with the standard "screen reader only" clipping, so the text is read aloud and found by assistive technology but takes no space on screen.
whenToUse: A text alternative for an icon-only control when a `label` prop is not available (for example the name of a custom control).
A heading or landmark label that sighted users do not need because the layout already implies it.
Extra context for a repeated link or button ("Edit" followed by a hidden "order ORD-1048").
whenNotToUse: To hide content from everyone: use the `hidden` attribute or conditional rendering.
To hide content from assistive technology only: use `aria-hidden="true"`.
For a skip link that appears on focus: use `SkipLink`.
For text that sighted keyboard users need to see: render it visibly.
examples: Order summary

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A text alternative for an icon-only control when a `label` prop is not available (for example the name of a custom control).
- A heading or landmark label that sighted users do not need because the layout already implies it.
- Extra context for a repeated link or button ("Edit" followed by a hidden "order ORD-1048").

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To hide content from everyone: use the `hidden` attribute or conditional rendering.
- To hide content from assistive technology only: use `aria-hidden="true"`.
- For a skip link that appears on focus: use `SkipLink`.
- For text that sighted keyboard users need to see: render it visibly.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span.root   (or as="h2", "div", ...)
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0); position: absolute; 1px box; overflow: hidden
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type          | Default  | Notes                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `as`        | `ElementType` | `'span'` | Element to render (`h2`, `div`, `label`, ...).             |
| `className` | `string`      | -        | Merged with the internal class.                            |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`   | -        | The text read by assistive technology.                     |
| `...rest`   | `span` props  | -        | Spread onto the element (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`, `ref`). |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The content stays in the accessibility tree and in the reading order; place it where it should be read.
- Do not put interactive elements inside: a focusable element that cannot be seen is a focus-visibility failure (WCAG 2.4.7).
- Write the text as you would write visible copy: sentence case, no emoji, no decorative punctuation.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Keep it short and specific ("Close dialog", not "Click here to close the dialog window").
- Do not repeat what the visible label already says.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: ```tsx Order summary ```

sections.content: - New in Loui DS: the handoff had no equivalent; screen-reader-only text was ad hoc.
